ui.하루 몇 개씩 외우는 게 좋아요?: How many words a day should I learn?
ui.목표 점수와 시험일로 계산한 양이 기본이에요. 바쁘면 줄여도 되지만 <b: The default is based on your target score and test date. You can lower it when you're busy, but reviewing every day matters most. Change it anytime in Settings → Study Plan.

ui.밀린 복습이 다음 날 한꺼번에 나와요. 많으면 오늘은 복습만 해도 괜찮아: Missed reviews all show up the next day. If there are a lot, it's okay to do just reviews that day. Continue with new words after you finish your reviews.

ui.목표 점수를 바꾸면 기록이 지워지나요?: Will changing my target score erase my progress?
ui.아니요. 외운 단어와 문제 기록은 그대로이고, 앞으로 나올 단어의 범위와: No. Your learned words and question history stay as they are. Only the range and difficulty of upcoming words change.
ui.네. 단어·음성·문제가 모두 앱 안에 들어 있어서 비행기 모드에서도 쓸: Yes. All words, audio and questions are built into the app, so it works even in airplane mode.
ui.기록을 새 폰으로 옮기려면?: How do I move my progress to a new phone?
ui.설정 → <b>학습 기록 백업</b>으로 파일을 만들고, 새 폰에서 <b: Create a file with Settings → Back Up Progress, then use Restore Backup on your new phone. Your progress is stored only on this device.
ui.실전 진행과 내 속도로는 뭐가 달라요?: What's the difference between Real Test Mode and My Pace?
ui.<b>실전 진행</b>은 실제 시험처럼 안내 방송과 번호를 들려주고, 답: Real Test Mode plays the directions and question numbers like the real test, and moves to the next question automatically when the answer time is up. With no replays, it's great for getting used to test conditions. My Pace plays each question once, and then you tap 'Next' yourself. We recommend Real Test Mode starting 2–3 weeks before your test. If you get a phone call during Real Test Mode, tap Pause. When you resume, it replays from that question.
ui.실전 문제는 기출 문제인가요?: Are the practice questions from past exams?
ui.아니요. 모든 문제는 실제 토익 형식에 맞춰 새로 만든 문제예요. 정답: No. Every question is original, written to match the real TOEIC format. Each one comes with the evidence for the answer and a translation.

{1}Daily Study Routine

The Today's Study button on Home shows what's next, in the order below. Just follow the button.

{2} {3} {4}

{5}What the Card Buttons Mean

Don't knowComes back in this session and goes to Mistakes
UnsureShortens the review interval by one step (new words: tomorrow)
Know itReview intervals keep getting longer

If a new word is one you already know, tap Know it and it'll be checked just once more in 3 days. Swipe right for Know it, left for Don't know.

{6}When Do Reviews Come Up?

{7}

Each correct answer stretches the gap until the next review; a miss resets it to the shortest gap. Once a word reaches the 14-day interval, it counts as Mastered. Missed words collect automatically in Review → Mistakes.

{8}Estimated Score and Half Mock Tests

Your estimated score is calculated from your accuracy on recent LC and RC questions (30+ each). The more you solve, the more accurate it gets.

A half mock test is half the length of the real test. LC audio plays only once, and RC is timed. Mock test questions never appear in practice, so you're tested on questions you've never seen.

With Real Test Mode, LC runs just like at the test center: English directions for each part → the number ("Number 7.") → question audio → answer time (5 sec for Part 1·2, 8 sec per question for Part 3·4) → next question automatically. Full mock tests use Real Test Mode by default; for half mock tests, you choose when you start.

If you take the same test again, it's marked as a Retake and isn't counted in your estimated score. Your first-attempt score is the benchmark.

{9}One-Line Tips by Part

Part 1 In photos with no people, 'is being p.p.' (being done right now) is usually wrong
Part 2 Indirect replies ('Let me check') are often correct
Part 3·4 Read the questions before the audio
Part 5 First check which part of speech the blank needs
Part 6 For sentence insertion, the link to the surrounding sentences is key
Part 7 Correct answers paraphrase the passage

words/#01-01/exKo: 마케팅 보조 직원 채용 광고에 200명이 넘는 지원자가 응답했다.
Over 200 people answered our job ad for a marketing assistant.
words/#01-01/der/0/m: to ask for (a job, etc.); to request formally
words/#01-01/tip: 사람명사 applicant와 사물명사 application(지원서)을 구분하는 품사 문제가 자주 나온다. '~ 직책의 지원자'는 applicant for + 직책으로 쓴다.
Part-of-speech questions often test applicant (a person) vs. application (the form). "Someone applying for a job" is applicant for + job title.
words/#01-01/q/k: with 이하의 경력을 가진 '사람'이 면접에 초대되는 것이므로 사람명사 applicants가 정답. applications(지원서)는 면접에 초대될 수 없다.
The ones with the experience described after with, who get invited to an interview, are people, so the person noun applicants is correct. Applications (forms) can't be invited to an interview.
words/#01-02/exKo: 우리는 지역 관리자 직책의 후보자를 세 명으로 좁혔다.
We have cut the list to three people for the regional manager job.
words/#01-02/col/1/k: person being considered for the job
words/#01-02/der/0/m: running for a position; being a contender
words/#01-02/tip: 'candidate for + 직책' 형태로 쓰며, '적임자'는 the ideal(right) candidate로 표현된다. Part 7에서는 applicant로 바꿔 표현되는 경우가 많다.
Used as candidate for + job title; "the perfect person for the job" is the ideal (right) candidate. In Part 7 it is often paraphrased as applicant.
words/#01-02/q/k: 주어 Ms. Ryu는 사람이므로 '후보자'를 뜻하는 candidate가 정답. application, qualification, nomination은 사물·행위 명사라 사람을 가리킬 수 없다.
The subject, Ms. Ryu, is a person, so candidate (person being considered) is correct. The nouns application, qualification, and nomination name things or actions and can't refer to a person.
words/#01-03/exKo: 그 회사는 서울 사무소에서 함께 일할 자격을 갖춘 회계사를 찾고 있다.
The firm wants an accountant with the right credentials to work at its Seoul office.
words/#01-03/col/1/k: to have the right to do; to be able to do
words/#01-03/col/2/k: very well trained; with strong credentials
words/#01-03/der/0/m: to become eligible; to make eligible
words/#01-03/tip: 'be qualified for + 명사', 'be qualified to + 동사원형' 형태를 기억할 것. 명사 앞 수식 자리에는 분사형 형용사 qualified가 온다.
Remember the patterns be qualified for + noun and be qualified to + base verb. Before a noun, use the participle adjective qualified.
words/#01-03/q/k: 부사 highly의 수식을 받으면서 명사 engineers를 꾸미는 형용사 자리이므로 qualified가 정답. 동사 qualify(qualifies)나 명사 qualification은 올 수 없다.
The blank is modified by the adverb highly and describes the noun engineers, so it needs an adjective: qualified. The verb qualify (qualifies) and the noun qualification can't go here.
words/#01-04/exKo: 필요한 자격 요건을 갖추지 못한 지원자는 그 직무에 고려되지 않는다.
Applicants who lack the required credentials will not be considered for the job.
words/#01-04/der/0/m: to become eligible; to make eligible
words/#01-04/tip: '자격 요건'의 의미로는 보통 복수형 qualifications로 쓴다. 'qualifications for + 직책', 'meet the qualifications' 연어를 통째로 기억할 것.
In the sense of "requirements" it is usually plural: qualifications. Learn the set phrases qualifications for + job title and meet the qualifications as whole units.
words/#01-04/q/k: 형용사 minimum 뒤, 동사 meet의 목적어인 명사 자리이므로 qualifications가 정답. qualified와 qualifying은 형용사·분사라 명사 자리에 올 수 없다.

After the adjective minimum and as the object of the verb meet, the blank needs a noun, so qualifications is correct. Qualified and qualifying are adjective/participle forms and can't fill a noun slot.
words/#01-05/m/0: CV; summary of your work history
words/#01-05/exKo: Patel 씨는 오늘 아침 인사부에 이력서를 이메일로 보냈다.
Ms. Patel e-mailed her CV to the personnel department this morning.
words/#01-05/col/1/k: to bring your CV up to date
words/#01-05/tip: 악센트 없이 resume로도 쓰지만 동사 resume(재개하다)과는 발음과 뜻이 다르다. 가산명사이므로 a résumé, résumés 형태로 쓴다.
It is also written resume without accents, but don't confuse it with the verb resume (to start again), which differs in pronunciation and meaning. It is countable: a résumé, résumés.
words/#01-05/q/k: 지원자가 추천서와 함께 보내는 서류는 이력서이므로 résumé가 정답. receipt(영수증), reservation(예약), refund(환불)는 채용 문맥에 맞지 않는다.
The document applicants send along with letters of reference is a CV, so résumé is correct. Receipt, reservation, and refund don't fit a hiring context.
words/#01-06/exKo: 지원자는 업무 관련 추천인 두 명의 연락처를 제공해야 한다.
Applicants must give contact details for two people from work who can recommend them.
words/#01-06/col/1/k: so you can check it later
words/#01-06/der/0/m: to mention; to consult (a source); to send (someone) to
words/#01-06/tip: 채용 문맥에서는 '추천인' 또는 '추천서'를 뜻한다. 'for future reference(향후 참고용으로)', 'with reference to(~에 관하여)'도 Part 5·6에 자주 나온다.
In hiring contexts it means a referee or a recommendation letter. The phrases for future reference (to keep for later) and with reference to (about) also often appear in Part 5·6.
words/#01-06/q/k: 'for future reference(나중에 참고하도록)'는 고정 표현이므로 reference가 정답. referral은 '소개, 추천'이라는 뜻이라 문맥에 맞지 않는다.
The phrase for future reference (so you can check it later) is fixed, so reference is correct. Referral means "recommendation (of someone)", which doesn't fit the context.
words/#01-07/exKo: 그 회사는 향후 1년 동안 신규 엔지니어 50명을 채용할 계획이다.
The company plans to take on 50 new engineers over the next year.
words/#01-07/tip: recruit는 명사로 '신입 사원'이라는 뜻도 있다. 명사 자리에서 '채용(활동)'은 recruitment, '채용 담당자'는 recruiter로 구분할 것.
As a noun, recruit also means "new employee". In noun slots, tell apart recruitment (the hiring process) and recruiter (the person who hires).
words/#01-07/q/k: 빈칸 뒤 목적어 experienced drivers를 받아 '경력 운전기사를 모집하고 있다'는 뜻이 되어야 하므로 recruiting이 정답. respond, graduate는 자동사이고 apply는 사람을 목적어로 취해 '지원하다'라는 뜻을 만들 수 없다.

The blank takes the object experienced drivers, meaning "is looking to hire experienced drivers", so recruiting is correct. Respond and graduate are intransitive, and apply can't take a person as its object.
words/#01-08/exKo: 그 식당은 바쁜 연휴 시즌에 대비해 서빙 직원 세 명을 추가로 고용했다.
The restaurant took on three more servers for the busy holiday season.
words/#01-08/tip: hire는 명사로 '신입 사원'(a new hire)의 뜻도 있다. 'newly hired employees'처럼 과거분사가 명사를 수식하는 형태가 Part 5에 자주 나온다.
As a noun, hire also means "new employee" (a new hire). In Part 5 you often see a past participle describing a noun, as in newly hired employees.
words/#01-08/q/k: 부사 newly의 수식을 받아 명사 staff members를 꾸미는 자리이며, 직원은 '고용되는' 대상이므로 과거분사 hired가 정답.
The blank is modified by newly and describes staff members. Staff are the ones being employed, so the past participle hired is correct.
words/#01-09/exKo: Mr. Larson accepted the job of head of the accounting department.
words/#01-09/tip: 'a position as + 직책', 'a position in + 부서/분야', 'apply for a position'이 빈출 형태다. Part 1에서는 '위치, 자세'의 의미로도 쓰인다.
Common patterns: a position as + job title, a position in + department/field, and apply for a position. In Part 1 it can also mean "place" or "posture".
words/#01-09/q/k: 'apply for the position of + 직책(~ 자리에 지원하다)'이므로 position이 정답. condition(조건), situation(상황), location(장소)은 직책과 어울리지 않는다.
The pattern is apply for the position of + job title, so position is correct. Condition, situation, and location don't go with a job title.
words/#01-10/exKo: 현재 우리 고객 서비스 부서에 두 자리의 공석이 있다.
Our customer service department currently has two unfilled jobs.
words/#01-10/col/2/k: launch of a new store or business
words/#01-10/tip: '공석'의 의미일 때 가산명사이며, job opening은 Part 7에서 vacancy로 바꿔 표현된다. 'grand opening(개업, 개장)'은 매장 개장 공지에 자주 나온다.
In the sense of "vacancy" it is countable, and job opening is paraphrased as vacancy in Part 7. Grand opening (a new store's launch) often appears in store announcements.
words/#01-10/q/k: 관사 an 뒤 명사 자리이며 '~ 자리의 공석'이라는 뜻이 되어야 하므로 opening이 정답. opener(따개), openness(개방성)는 의미가 맞지 않고 openly는 부사다.

After the article an, the blank needs a noun meaning "a vacancy for", so opening is correct. Opener (a tool for opening things) and openness (being open) don't fit the meaning, and openly is an adverb.
words/#01-11/exKo: 유효한 운전면허증은 이 배송 업무의 기본 요건이다.
A valid driver's license is a basic condition for this delivery job.
words/#01-11/tip: 'meet/satisfy the requirements'가 대표 연어다. 동사 require는 'require A to do', 'be required to do' 형태로 Part 5에 자주 나온다.
The key collocation is meet/satisfy the requirements. The verb require often appears in Part 5 as require A to do and be required to do.
words/#01-11/q/k: 관사 a 뒤에 오는 명사 자리이므로 requirement가 정답. required는 형용사라 뒤에 수식할 명사가 필요하다.
After the article a, the blank needs a noun, so requirement is correct. Required is an adjective and needs a noun after it.
words/#01-12/exKo: 석사 학위는 선임 연구원으로 승진하기 위한 필수 조건이다.
A master's degree is required for promotion to senior researcher.
words/#01-12/tip: 'a prerequisite for(to) + 명사' 형태로 쓴다. Part 7에서는 requirement나 necessary condition으로 바꿔 표현된다.
Used as a prerequisite for (to) + noun. In Part 7 it is paraphrased as requirement or necessary condition.
words/#01-12/q/k: 안전 교육 이수가 중장비 운전을 위한 '필수 조건'이라는 뜻이므로 prerequisite가 정답. 형태가 비슷한 presentation(발표), preference(선호), prediction(예측)은 의미가 맞지 않는다.

Completing the safety course is a "requirement" for operating heavy machinery, so prerequisite is correct. The look-alikes presentation (talk), preference (liking), and prediction (forecast) don't fit the meaning.
words/#01-13/exKo: Kim 박사는 데이터 분석에 대한 전문 지식을 갖추고 있어 그 프로젝트에 가장 적합한 인물이었다.
Dr. Kim's deep knowledge of data analysis made her the best person for the project.
words/#01-13/tip: expertise는 불가산명사라 an expertise, expertises로 쓰지 않는다. 사람명사 expert(전문가)와 구분하는 문제가 출제된다.
Expertise is uncountable, so don't write an expertise or expertises. Questions test it against the person noun expert (specialist).
words/#01-13/q/k: 형용사 considerable 뒤 동사 has의 목적어 자리로, '전문 지식'을 뜻하는 불가산명사 expertise가 정답. expert(s)는 사람명사라 '상당한 전문가를 가지고 있다'는 어색한 뜻이 된다.

After the adjective considerable, the blank is the object of has, so the uncountable noun expertise (specialist knowledge) is correct. Expert(s) is a person noun and would give the odd meaning "has considerable specialists".
words/#01-14/exKo: 지원자는 Microsoft Excel 및 기타 스프레드시트 프로그램에 능숙해야 한다.
Applicants must be skilled in Microsoft Excel and other spreadsheet programs.
words/#01-14/tip: 'be proficient in(at) + 분야' 전치사 짝이 핵심이다. 명사 proficiency는 'proficiency in English(영어 실력)' 형태로 쓰인다.
The key is the preposition: be proficient in (at) + field. The noun proficiency appears as proficiency in English (English ability).
words/#01-14/q/k: 언어 능력을 나타내는 'be proficient in(~에 능숙하다)'이 문맥에 맞으므로 proficient가 정답. eligible은 for, dependent는 on, attentive는 to와 짝을 이룬다.
The phrase be proficient in (good at), describing language ability, fits the context, so proficient is correct. Eligible pairs with for, dependent with on, and attentive with to.
words/#01-15/exKo: 정규직 직원은 매년 2주간의 유급 휴가를 받을 자격이 있다.
Full-time employees are entitled to two weeks of paid vacation every year.
words/#01-15/tip: 'be eligible for + 명사', 'be eligible to + 동사원형' 두 형태를 모두 기억할 것. Part 7에서는 be entitled to로 바꿔 표현되는 경우가 많다.
Remember both patterns: be eligible for + noun and be eligible to + base verb. In Part 7 it is often paraphrased as be entitled to.
words/#01-15/q/k: 'be eligible to do(~할 자격이 있다)' 구문이므로 eligible이 정답. capable은 'be capable of -ing'로 써야 하며, considerate(사려 깊은)와 accessible(접근 가능한)은 의미가 맞지 않는다.

The pattern is be eligible to do (be entitled to do), so eligible is correct. Capable must be used as be capable of -ing, and considerate (thoughtful) and accessible (easy to reach) don't fit the meaning.
words/#01-16/m/2: to put to use; to be relevant (to)
words/#01-16/exKo: 우리 회사는 최근 졸업생들이 하계 인턴십 프로그램에 지원하기를 적극 권장한다.
We strongly encourage recent graduates to put in for our summer internship program.
words/#01-16/col/1/k: to be relevant to; to cover
words/#01-16/col/2/k: to hand in an application face to face
words/#01-16/tip: 'apply for + 직책/혜택(~에 지원하다)'과 'apply to + 대상(~에 적용되다)'을 구분할 것. '지원하다'의 apply는 자동사라 직책을 바로 목적어로 받지 않는다.
Distinguish apply for + job/benefit (to seek) from apply to + target (to be relevant to). Apply in the sense of "seek a job" is intransitive, so it can't take the job title directly as its object.
words/#01-16/q/k: '규정이 ~에게 적용되다'는 apply to로 표현하므로 apply가 정답. submit to(~에 따르다), attend to(~을 처리하다)는 의미가 맞지 않고, qualify는 to와 함께 '적용되다'라는 뜻을 만들지 못한다.
"Rules apply to someone" is expressed with apply to, so apply is correct. Submit to (to obey) and attend to (to deal with) don't fit the meaning, and qualify to doesn't mean "be relevant to".
words/#01-17/m/0: to hand in; to send in
words/#01-17/exKo: 지원자는 이력서와 함께 최근 작업물 포트폴리오를 제출해야 한다.
Applicants must hand in a portfolio of recent work together with their CV.
words/#01-17/col/1/k: to hand in A to B
words/#01-17/tip: '제출하다'의 submit는 타동사라 'submit the report to + 대상' 형태로 쓴다. 명사 submission은 'submission deadline(제출 마감일)'으로 자주 나온다.
Submit (hand in) is transitive, used as submit the report to + recipient. The noun submission often appears as submission deadline (the last day to hand something in).
words/#01-17/q/k: be동사 뒤에서 제안서가 '제출되는' 것이므로 수동태를 만드는 과거분사 submitted가 정답. submitting은 능동이라 뒤에 목적어가 필요하다.
After the be-verb, the proposals are being handed in, so the past participle submitted, forming the passive, is correct. Submitting is active and would need an object after it.
words/#01-18/exKo: The last day to apply has been pushed back to June 30.
words/#01-18/tip: 'meet the deadline(기한을 맞추다)', 'miss the deadline(기한을 놓치다)'이 빈출 연어다. 무엇의 마감인지는 'deadline for + 명사'로 나타낸다.
Common collocations: meet the deadline (finish on time) and miss the deadline (be late). Show what is due with deadline for + noun.
words/#01-18/q/k: 주어가 특정 날짜(Friday, December 1)와 같다고 했으므로 '마감일'을 뜻하는 deadline이 정답. period(기간), agenda(안건), schedule(일정)은 하루라는 날짜와 동일시될 수 없다.

The subject is equated with a specific date (Friday, December 1), so deadline (due date) is correct. Period (span of time), agenda (list of topics), and schedule (plan) can't be equal to a single date.
words/#01-19/m/0: meeting to assess a job candidate
words/#01-19/exKo: Torres 씨는 내일 오전 10시에 인사부장과 면접이 있다.
Ms. Torres has a job interview with the human resources director at 10 A.M. tomorrow.
words/#01-19/col/0/k: meeting to assess a job applicant
words/#01-19/col/1/k: to set a time to meet a candidate
words/#01-19/col/2/k: to hold a candidate meeting; to question applicants
words/#01-19/tip: 동사로도 쓰여 'interview candidates(지원자를 면접하다)'처럼 목적어를 바로 받는다. 사람명사 interviewer(면접관)와 interviewee(면접 대상자)를 구분할 것.
It is also a verb that takes an object directly, as in interview candidates (to question applicants). Tell apart the person nouns interviewer (the one asking) and interviewee (the one being asked).
words/#01-19/q/k: 관사 an 뒤 동사 schedule의 목적어로 '면접'을 뜻하는 interview가 정답. interviewer는 면접관(사람)이라 일정을 잡는 대상이 될 수 없다.
After the article an, as the object of schedule, the noun interview (job meeting) is correct. Interviewer is a person, so it can't be what gets scheduled.
words/#01-20/exKo: Wong 씨는 국제 마케팅 분야에서 인상적인 실적을 보유하고 있다.
Mr. Wong has a remarkable record of success in international marketing.
words/#01-20/tip: 사물이 감명을 '주는' 경우는 impressive, 사람이 감명을 '받은' 경우는 impressed(be impressed with/by)를 쓴다.
Use impressive when a thing impresses others, and impressed (be impressed with/by) when a person feels impressed.
words/#01-20/q/k: 명사 results를 수식하는 형용사 자리이며, 결과가 감명을 '주는' 것이므로 impressive가 정답. impressed는 사람이 감명을 '받은' 상태를 나타낸다.
The blank is an adjective describing the noun results, and the results impress others, so impressive is correct. Impressed describes a person who has been impressed.
words/#01-21/exKo: 우리는 고객 응대를 즐기는 열정적인 팀원을 찾고 있다.
We want passionate team members who like dealing with customers.
words/#01-21/tip: 'be enthusiastic about + 명사' 전치사 짝이 핵심이다. 명사 enthusiasm은 'with enthusiasm(열정적으로)' 형태로 쓰인다.
The key is the preposition: be enthusiastic about + noun. The noun enthusiasm is used as with enthusiasm (eagerly).
words/#01-21/q/k: 관사 an과 명사 response 사이의 형용사 자리이므로 enthusiastic이 정답. enthusiastically는 부사라 명사를 꾸밀 수 없다.
The blank is between the article an and the noun response, so it needs an adjective: enthusiastic. Enthusiastically is an adverb and can't describe a noun.
words/#01-22/exKo: 금융 분야 경력이 있는 지원자의 지원을 특히 환영한다.
We especially welcome applicants with experience in finance.
words/#01-22/tip: 채용 공고의 'a background in + 분야'는 '~ 분야의 경력이나 전공'을 뜻하며 Part 7에서 experience in으로 바꿔 표현된다. Part 1에서는 'in the background(뒤쪽에)'로 쓰인다.
In job ads, a background in + field means experience or study in that field, and Part 7 paraphrases it as experience in. In Part 1 it appears as in the background (at the back).
words/#01-22/q/k: 'a background in + 분야(~ 분야의 배경 지식, 경력)'이므로 background가 정답. attendance(출석), occupation(직업), appearance(외모)는 in + 분야와 어울리지 않는다.
The pattern is a background in + field (experience or knowledge in a field), so background is correct. Attendance (being present), occupation (job), and appearance (looks) don't go with in + field.
words/#01-23/exKo: 다섯 개 세션을 모두 마친 참가자는 원장이 서명한 수료증을 받는다.
Participants who complete all five sessions will get a completion document signed by the director.
words/#01-23/col/0/k: proof that you finished a course
words/#01-23/tip: certificate는 '증서' 자체(가산명사)이고 certification은 '인증, 자격 취득'을 뜻한다. 'gift certificate(상품권)'도 쇼핑 지문에 자주 나온다.
Certificate is the document itself (countable), while certification means official approval or getting qualified. Gift certificate (store voucher) also often appears in shopping texts.
words/#01-23/q/k: 형용사 valid 뒤 동사 hold의 목적어인 명사 자리로, teaching certificate(교사 자격증)가 하나의 복합명사를 이룬다. certified, certifying은 명사 자리에 올 수 없다.
After the adjective valid, the blank is a noun as the object of hold, and teaching certificate (teaching license) forms one compound noun. Certified and certifying can't fill a noun slot.
words/#01-24/exKo: 그 직책은 경영학 학사 학위를 요구한다.
The job requires a bachelor's in business administration.
words/#01-24/tip: 'a degree in + 전공' 형태로 쓰며 'to some degree(어느 정도)'도 기억할 것. Part 4 일기 예보에서는 '(온도의) 도'로 나온다.
Used as a degree in + subject; also remember to some degree (to some extent). In Part 4 weather reports it means a unit of temperature.
words/#01-24/q/k: 'master's degree(석사 학위)'는 고정 표현이며 in 뒤에 전공이 온다. major는 '전공' 자체를 뜻하므로 master's와 결합하지 않는다.
Master's degree is a fixed expression, followed by in + subject. Major means the subject itself, so it doesn't combine with master's.
words/#01-25/exKo: 올해 컨벤션 센터에서 열리는 취업 박람회에 80개가 넘는 기업이 참가한다.
Over 80 companies will take part in this year's career fair at the convention center.
words/#01-25/col/0/k: to go to a career fair
words/#01-25/tip: Part 3·4에서 career fair, recruiting event로 바꿔 말하는 경우가 많다. 박람회 부스는 booth, 참가 업체는 participating companies로 함께 나온다.
In Part 3·4 it is often paraphrased as career fair or recruiting event. You'll also see booth (a company's stand) and participating companies.
words/#01-25/q/k: 여러 업체 대표가 토요일에 채용 활동을 하는 '행사'이므로 job fair가 정답. job offer(일자리 제안), job title(직함), job description(직무 기술서)은 행사가 아니다.
It is an "event" where many companies recruit on Saturday, so job fair is correct. Job offer (an offer of work), job title (name of a position), and job description (list of duties) are not events.
words/#01-26/m/0: list of duties for a job
words/#01-26/exKo: 직무 기술서에 따르면, 그 보조 직원은 부서 예산 관리도 맡는다.
According to the list of duties, the assistant will also handle the department's budget.
words/#01-26/tip: Part 7 채용 공고에서 '담당 업무'를 묻는 문제의 근거가 된다. 지문 속 duties, responsibilities가 같은 내용을 가리킨다.
In Part 7 job ads, it is the basis for questions about job duties. Words like duties and responsibilities in the text refer to the same content.
words/#01-26/q/k: 직무의 의무와 책임을 파악하기 위해 '읽는' 문서는 job description이다. job seeker(구직자), job fair(취업 박람회), job interview(면접)는 읽는 대상이 아니다.

The document you "read" to understand the duties and responsibilities is the job description. Job seeker (a person looking for work), job fair (career fair), and job interview (meeting with a candidate) aren't things you read.
words/#01-27/exKo: 우리 회사는 경쟁력 있는 급여와 넉넉한 복리후생 제도를 제공한다.
We offer pay that matches the market and a generous benefits package.
words/#01-27/der/0/m: to try to win; to rival
words/#01-27/tip: 채용 공고의 competitive salary는 '경쟁사에 뒤지지 않는 높은 급여'를 뜻한다. 사람명사 competitor, 명사 competition과 품사를 구분하는 문제가 빈출이다.
In job ads, competitive salary means pay that's as good as or better than other companies'. Part-of-speech questions often test it against the person noun competitor and the noun competition.
words/#01-27/q/k: 부사 highly의 수식을 받아 명사 rates를 꾸미는 형용사 자리이므로 competitive가 정답. competitively는 부사라 명사를 꾸밀 수 없다.
The blank is modified by the adverb highly and describes the noun rates, so it needs an adjective: competitive. Competitively is an adverb and can't describe a noun.
words/#01-28/exKo: 이 직책의 초봉은 경력에 따라 달라진다.
The starting pay for this job depends on experience.
words/#01-28/col/0/k: first pay at a new job
words/#01-28/tip: salary는 주로 정규직의 월급·연봉을, wage는 시급·주급을 뜻한다. 급여가 많고 적음은 high/low salary로 쓰며 expensive/cheap은 쓰지 않는다.
Salary usually means the fixed monthly or yearly pay of regular staff, while wage means hourly or weekly pay. Use high/low salary for amount, not expensive/cheap.
words/#01-28/q/k: 직책에 대한 연간 '급여'이며 지원자의 경력에 따라 정해지므로 salary가 정답. fare(운임), price(가격), fee(수수료)는 급여를 뜻하지 않는다.
It is yearly "pay" for a job, set by the candidate's experience, so salary is correct. Fare (ticket price), price (cost of goods), and fee (charge for a service) don't mean pay.
words/#01-29/exKo: 우리 회사의 복리후생에는 건강 보험, 유급 휴일, 퇴직 연금 제도가 포함된다.
Our perks include health insurance, paid holidays, and a retirement plan.
words/#01-29/col/0/k: set of perks offered with a job
words/#01-29/der/1/m: person who receives money or help
words/#01-29/tip: '복리후생'의 의미로는 복수형 benefits로 쓴다. 동사 benefit은 'benefit from(~로부터 이익을 얻다)' 형태가 Part 5에 자주 나온다.
In the sense of "employee perks" it is plural: benefits. The verb benefit often appears in Part 5 as benefit from (to gain from).
words/#01-29/q/k: the same 뒤 동사 receive의 목적어인 명사 자리이며, 치과 보험을 포함하는 '복리후생'이므로 benefits가 정답. beneficiary는 '수혜자(사람)'라 의미가 맞지 않는다.
After the same, the blank is a noun as the object of receive, meaning perks that include dental insurance, so benefits is correct. Beneficiary (a person who receives) doesn't fit the meaning.
words/#01-30/exKo: 보수 패키지에는 기본급과 연간 성과 보너스가 포함된다.
The pay package includes a base salary plus yearly performance bonuses.
words/#01-30/col/2/k: to be paid for a loss
words/#01-30/der/0/m: to make up for (a loss); to pay
words/#01-30/tip: 채용 문맥에서는 '급여와 복리후생 전체'를, 고객 불만 문맥에서는 '보상금'을 뜻한다. 동사는 'compensate A for B(A에게 B를 보상하다)' 형태로 쓴다.
In hiring contexts it means total pay and benefits; in complaint contexts, money paid for a loss. The verb is used as compensate A for B (pay A for B).
words/#01-30/q/k: 형용사 financial의 수식을 받는 명사 자리이므로 compensation이 정답. compensate는 동사, compensated와 compensating은 분사라 명사 자리에 올 수 없다.
The blank is a noun modified by the adjective financial, so compensation is correct. Compensate is a verb, and compensated and compensating are participles, so they can't fill a noun slot.
words/#01-31/exKo: 이 신입 직책은 업무 경험이 적은 최근 졸업생에게 적합하다.
This junior job is perfect for recent graduates with little work experience.
words/#01-31/tip: 명사 앞에서만 쓰이는 형용사로 'no experience required'와 함께 자주 나온다. Part 7에서는 'suitable for those new to the field'처럼 바꿔 표현된다.
It is used only before a noun and often appears with no experience required. In Part 7 it is paraphrased as suitable for those new to the field.
words/#01-31/q/k: 경력이 필요 없고 신입 사원 모두 교육을 받는다고 했으므로 '신입 수준의' entry-level이 정답. senior, executive는 경력이 필요한 상급직이라 문맥과 반대되고, experienced는 직무가 아닌 사람을 수식한다.

No experience is needed and all new hires get training, so entry-level (for beginners) is correct. Senior and executive are higher posts needing experience, the opposite of the context, and experienced describes people, not jobs.
words/#01-32/exKo: 6개월의 수습 기간이 끝난 후 Ahn 씨는 정규직 계약을 제안받았다.
After a six-month trial period, Mr. Ahn was offered a long-term contract.
words/#01-32/tip: temporary(임시의)와 짝으로 자주 나온다. 공지문에서는 'permanently closed(영구 폐점)'처럼 부사형도 쓰인다.
It often appears paired with temporary. In notices, the adverb is used too, as in permanently closed (closed for good).
words/#01-32/q/k: 관사 a와 명사 position 사이에서 명사를 꾸미는 형용사 자리이므로 permanent가 정답. permanence와 permanency는 명사, permanently는 부사다.
The blank is between the article a and the noun position, so it needs an adjective: permanent. Permanence and permanency are nouns, and permanently is an adverb.
words/#01-33/exKo: 그 업체는 휴가 중인 직원의 공백을 메울 임시 직원을 공급한다.
The agency supplies short-term staff to fill in for employees on vacation.
words/#01-33/der/0/m: for a short time; for now
words/#01-33/tip: 공지문에서 부사 temporarily가 'be temporarily closed/unavailable' 형태로 빈출이다. 'on a temporary basis'는 '임시로'라는 덩어리 표현이다.
In notices, the adverb temporarily is very common: be temporarily closed/unavailable. The phrase on a temporary basis (for a limited time) is a set unit.
words/#01-33/q/k: 'on a temporary basis(임시로)'에서 명사 basis를 수식하는 형용사 자리이므로 temporary가 정답. 부사 temporarily는 명사를 꾸밀 수 없다.
In on a temporary basis (for a limited time), the blank is an adjective describing the noun basis, so temporary is correct. The adverb temporarily can't describe a noun.
words/#01-34/exKo: 이사회는 Sato 씨를 회사의 신임 최고재무책임자로 임명했다.
The board named Ms. Sato as the company's new chief financial officer.
words/#01-34/der/0/m: naming (to a post); meeting time, booking
words/#01-34/tip: 'appoint A (as) B'와 수동형 'be appointed (as) B'가 출제된다. 명사 appointment는 '임명' 외에 '(병원 등의) 예약'으로 Part 3에 자주 나온다.
Tested forms: appoint A (as) B and the passive be appointed (as) B. Besides "naming to a post," the noun appointment often means a booked visit (to a doctor, etc.) in Part 3.
words/#01-34/q/k: 'be appointed (as) + 직책(~로 임명되다)' 구문이므로 appointed가 정답. applied(적용된), approved(승인된), applauded(박수를 받은)는 직책을 보어로 취할 수 없다.
The pattern is be appointed (as) + job title, so appointed is correct. Applied, approved, and applauded (clapped for) can't take a job title as a complement.
words/#01-35/exKo: Novak 씨의 직무에는 신입 직원 교육과 재고 관리가 포함된다.
Ms. Novak's responsibilities include training new staff and managing inventory.
words/#01-35/tip: '맡은 업무'의 의미로는 복수형 duties를 주로 쓰며 responsibilities로 바꿔 표현된다. 'on duty(근무 중)', 'off duty(비번)'는 Part 2·3에 자주 나온다.
In the sense of "work tasks" it is mostly plural, duties, and is paraphrased as responsibilities. On duty (working) and off duty (not working) often appear in Part 2·3.
words/#01-35/q/k: 'on duty(근무 중인)'는 고정 표현이므로 duty가 정답. task, job, service는 무관사로 on 뒤에 와서 '근무 중'이라는 뜻을 만들지 못한다.
The phrase on duty (working) is fixed, so duty is correct. The words task, job, and service can't follow on without an article to mean "working".
words/#01-36/m/0: to hire someone for an open post
words/#01-36/exKo: 회사는 이번 달 말 전에 그 자리를 채우기를 바란다.
The company hopes to hire someone for the job before the end of the month.
words/#01-36/col/0/k: to hire for an empty post
words/#01-36/col/1/k: to hire for an open job
words/#01-36/col/2/k: someone has already been hired for the job
words/#01-36/tip: 수동형 'The position has been filled(그 자리는 이미 충원되었다)'가 Part 3·7에서 '더 이상 지원을 받지 않는다'는 근거로 자주 쓰인다.
The passive The position has been filled (someone has already been hired) often appears in Part 3·7 as the reason applications are no longer accepted.
words/#01-36/q/k: has been 뒤에서 자리가 '채워진' 것이므로 수동태를 만드는 과거분사 filled가 정답. 'fill a position(자리를 채우다)'의 수동형이다.
After has been, the job has been filled, so the past participle filled, forming the passive, is correct. It is the passive of fill a position.
words/#01-37/exKo: 본사는 내년 봄에 시내의 더 큰 건물로 이전한다.
The head office will move to a bigger building downtown next spring.
words/#01-37/col/1/k: to move (or transfer) A to B
words/#01-37/col/2/k: to be open to moving for work
words/#01-37/tip: 자동사(relocate to)와 타동사(relocate A to B)로 모두 쓰인다. 채용 공고의 'willing to relocate'는 '근무지 이동이 가능한 사람'을 뜻한다.
It is both intransitive (relocate to) and transitive (relocate A to B). In job ads, willing to relocate means someone who can move to another work location.
words/#01-37/q/k: '싱가포르로 근무지를 옮길 의향이 있어야 한다'는 뜻이므로 relocate to가 정답. remain(머무르다)은 to와 어울리지 않고, register(등록하다), reply(답하다)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
The meaning is "must be willing to move to Singapore," so relocate to is correct. Remain (stay) doesn't go with to, and register (sign up) and reply (answer) don't fit the meaning.
words/#01-38/exKo: Reyes 씨는 주로 이전 상사의 추천 덕분에 채용되었다.
Ms. Reyes got the job mainly because her former supervisor spoke for her.
words/#01-38/col/1/k: on the advice of; because someone suggested it
words/#01-38/tip: 동사 recommend는 'recommend that + 주어 + (should) 동사원형' 구문에서 동사원형 자리를 묻는 문제로 자주 나온다. letter of recommendation은 reference letter로 바꿔 표현된다.
The verb recommend often appears in questions about the base verb in recommend that + subject + (should) + base verb. The phrase letter of recommendation is paraphrased as reference letter.
words/#01-38/q/k: 전치사 of 뒤의 명사 자리이며 'letter of recommendation(추천서)'은 고정 표현이므로 recommendation이 정답.
After the preposition of, the blank needs a noun, and letter of recommendation (reference letter) is a fixed expression, so recommendation is correct.
words/#01-39/exKo: Lin 씨의 자기소개서에는 그녀가 출판 업계에서 일하고 싶은 이유가 명확하게 설명되어 있었다.
Ms. Lin's application letter clearly explained why she wanted to work in publishing.
words/#01-39/tip: 이력서(résumé)와 함께 제출하는 서류로, Part 7 채용 공고에서 'send a résumé and cover letter to ~'가 지원 방법을 묻는 문제의 근거가 된다.
It is sent together with a résumé. In Part 7 job ads, send a résumé and cover letter to … is the basis for questions about how to apply.
words/#01-39/q/k: 이력서와 함께 관련 경력을 설명하는 서류를 보내라고 했으므로 cover letter가 정답. receipt(영수증), price list(가격표), floor plan(평면도)은 지원 서류가 아니다.

You're told to send your CV plus a document describing your experience, so cover letter is correct. Receipt (proof of payment), price list, and floor plan (map of a room's layout) aren't application documents.
words/#01-40/exKo: 인사팀은 모든 지원서를 검토해 선별한 뒤 부서장들에게 전달한다.
The HR team checks and sorts all applications before passing them on to department heads.
words/#01-40/col/1/k: to choose which calls to answer
words/#01-40/tip: 명사 '화면' 외에 동사 '(지원자를) 선별하다', '(영화를) 상영하다'의 뜻이 토익에 나온다. 'initial screening(1차 심사)'처럼 명사형 screening도 빈출이다.
Besides the noun "display surface," TOEIC uses the verbs "to filter (applicants)" and "to show (a film)". The noun screening is also common, as in initial screening (first-round check).
words/#01-40/q/k: 채용 대행사가 최고경영자 후보자를 '심사하다, 선별하다'라는 뜻이므로 screen이 정답. renew(갱신하다), install(설치하다), exhibit(전시하다)은 사람 후보자를 목적어로 취하지 않는다.

The recruiting firm will "check and filter" candidates for the CEO position, so screen is correct. Renew (extend), install (set up), and exhibit (display) can't take people (candidates) as their object.
words/#02-01/m/0: to move up (to a higher post)
words/#02-01/exKo: Garcia 씨는 잡지사에 입사한 지 불과 2년 만에 수석 편집자로 승진했다.
Ms. Garcia became senior editor just two years after joining the magazine.
words/#02-01/der/0/m: moving up (to a higher post); advertising; special offer
words/#02-01/tip: '승진하다'는 수동형 'be promoted to + 직책'으로 쓴다. '홍보하다'의 뜻도 빈출이며 형용사 promotional은 'promotional materials(홍보물)'로 자주 나온다.
"To be moved up" is the passive be promoted to + job title. The meaning "to advertise" is also common, and the adjective promotional often appears in promotional materials (ads, flyers).
words/#02-01/q/k: 새 스포츠웨어 제품군을 '홍보하기' 위해 영상을 만들었다는 뜻이므로 promote가 정답. inform과 notify는 사람을 목적어로 취하고, appoint(임명하다)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
The video was made to "advertise" the new sportswear line, so promote is correct. Inform and notify take a person as their object, and appoint (to name to a post) doesn't fit the meaning.
words/#02-02/exKo: Evans 씨는 지난달 지역 본부장으로 승진했다.
Mr. Evans was moved up to regional director last month.
words/#02-02/col/0/k: to be moved up (to a higher post)
words/#02-02/der/0/m: to move up (to a higher post); to advertise
words/#02-02/tip: 'promotion to + 직책'처럼 전치사 to와 함께 쓴다. 상점 공지에서는 '판촉 행사(special promotion)'의 뜻으로 Part 4에 자주 나온다.
Used with the preposition to, as in promotion to + job title. In store notices it means a sales event (special promotion), common in Part 4.
words/#02-02/q/k: 전치사 for 뒤의 명사 자리이므로 promotion이 정답. promotional은 형용사, promote와 promoted는 동사 형태라 전치사의 목적어가 될 수 없다.
After the preposition for, the blank needs a noun, so promotion is correct. Promotional is an adjective, and promote and promoted are verb forms, so they can't be the object of a preposition.
words/#02-03/m/0: to move (to another office); to reassign
words/#02-03/exKo: Patel 씨는 9월에 도쿄 지사로 전근을 간다.
Mr. Patel is moving to our Tokyo office in September.
words/#02-03/der/0/m: can be passed on or moved
words/#02-03/tip: 동사와 명사의 형태가 같으며(request a transfer), 'transfer to + 장소' 전치사 짝이 핵심이다. Part 2·3에서는 '전화를 연결하다', '환승하다'의 뜻으로도 나온다.
The verb and noun have the same form (request a transfer), and the key preposition is transfer to + place. In Part 2·3 it also means "to put a call through" or "to change trains/flights".
words/#02-03/q/k: 가족과 가까이 지내기 위해 밴쿠버 지점으로 '전근되기'를 요청한 것이므로 transferred가 정답. transformed(변형된), translated(번역된), transmitted(전송된)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.

She asked to "be moved" to the Vancouver branch to be closer to her family, so transferred is correct. Transformed (changed in form), translated (put into another language), and transmitted (sent by signal) don't fit the meaning.
words/#02-04/m/1: to leave one's job for good
words/#02-04/exKo: Simmons 박사는 그 병원에서 30년간 근무한 뒤 은퇴할 계획이다.
Dr. Simmons plans to stop working after 30 years at the hospital.
words/#02-04/col/0/k: to stop working at; to leave (a career)
words/#02-04/der/0/m: stopping work for good; later life after work
words/#02-04/tip: 자동사이므로 'retire from + 회사/직위' 형태로 쓴다. 명사 retirement는 'retirement party(퇴임 기념 파티)', 'retirement plan(퇴직 연금)'으로 자주 나온다.
It is intransitive, so it is used as retire from + company/post. The noun retirement often appears in retirement party (farewell party) and retirement plan (pension plan).
words/#02-04/q/k: 관계대명사 who 뒤의 동사 자리이고 last year가 있으므로 과거형 retired가 정답. retirement와 retiree는 명사, retiring은 동사 역할을 하려면 be동사가 필요하다.
The blank is the verb after the relative pronoun who, and last year signals the past, so retired is correct. Retirement and retiree are nouns, and retiring would need a be-verb to work as a verb.
words/#02-05/exKo: The chief financial officer suddenly stepped down last week.
words/#02-05/tip: 'resign from + 직위/회사', 'resign as + 직책' 형태로 쓴다. 명사 resignation은 'submit one's resignation(사직서를 제출하다)'으로 빈출이다.
Used as resign from + post/company and resign as + job title. The noun resignation is common in submit one's resignation (to hand in a letter of notice).
words/#02-05/q/k: 주어 Mr. Okoro 뒤의 동사 자리이고 last month가 있으므로 과거형 resigned가 정답. resignation은 명사, resigning과 to resign은 문장의 동사가 될 수 없다.
The blank is the verb after the subject Mr. Okoro, and last month signals the past, so resigned is correct. Resignation is a noun, and resigning and to resign can't be the main verb.
words/#02-06/exKo: 이사회는 아직 퇴임하는 CEO의 후임자를 지명하지 않았다.
The board has not yet chosen who will take over from the retiring CEO.
words/#02-06/der/0/m: to follow, take over from; to do well
words/#02-06/tip: 'successor to + 사람/직위'처럼 전치사 to를 쓴다. 반의어 predecessor(전임자)와 짝으로 출제되며, 동사 succeed에는 '뒤를 잇다'라는 뜻도 있다.
Use the preposition to, as in successor to + person/post. It is often tested with its opposite predecessor (the person before), and the verb succeed also means "to take over from".
words/#02-06/q/k: 회사를 떠나기 전에 교육하는 대상은 자신의 뒤를 이을 '후임자'이므로 successor가 정답. predecessor는 '전임자'라 문맥과 반대이고, success와 succession은 사람이 아니다.
The person she trains before leaving is the one who will take over her job, so successor is correct. Predecessor (the person before) is the opposite, and success and succession aren't people.
words/#02-07/m/0: to take over from; to fill in for
words/#02-07/m/1: to swap, change (for a new one)
words/#02-07/exKo: Moreno 씨가 Stein 씨의 뒤를 이어 법무부장을 맡는다.
Ms. Moreno will take over from Mr. Stein as head of the legal department.
words/#02-07/col/1/k: to take over from A as B
words/#02-07/der/0/m: new item; person who takes over
words/#02-07/tip: 'replace A with B(A를 B로 교체하다)'의 전치사 with를 묻는 문제가 자주 나온다. 명사 replacement는 '후임자' 또는 '교체품'을 뜻한다.
Questions often test the preposition with in replace A with B (swap A for B). The noun replacement means a person who takes over or a new item.
words/#02-07/q/k: 'replace A with B(A를 B로 교체하다)' 구문이므로 replace가 정답. repair(수리하다), return(반납하다), remove(제거하다)는 with B와 함께 '교체하다'의 뜻을 만들지 못한다.
The pattern is replace A with B (swap A for B), so replace is correct. Repair (fix), return (give back), and remove (take away) don't mean "swap" with with B.
words/#02-08/m/0: to assess; to judge the value of
words/#02-08/exKo: 관리자들은 연말에 직원 개개인의 업무 성과를 평가한다.
Managers assess each employee's work at the end of the year.
words/#02-08/tip: 명사 evaluation은 'performance evaluation(인사 고과)'으로 자주 나온다. to 뒤의 동사 자리와 관사 뒤의 명사 자리를 구분하는 품사 문제에 유의할 것.
The noun evaluation often appears as performance evaluation (staff review). Watch part-of-speech questions that test a verb slot after to vs. a noun slot after an article.
words/#02-08/q/k: to부정사를 만드는 to 뒤에 동사원형이 와야 하며 목적어 the safety를 취하므로 evaluate가 정답. evaluation과 evaluator는 명사, evaluative는 형용사다.
After to (forming a to-infinitive), a base verb is needed, and it takes the object the safety, so evaluate is correct. Evaluation and evaluator are nouns, and evaluative is an adjective.
words/#02-09/exKo: 보너스는 개인 성과와 회사 수익을 기준으로 지급된다.
Bonuses depend on each person's results and the company's profits.
words/#02-09/der/0/m: to carry out; to act or play on stage
words/#02-09/der/1/m: actor, singer; person who carries out a task
words/#02-09/tip: '실적, 성과'의 의미에서는 주로 불가산명사로 쓴다. 'performance review/evaluation(인사 고과)'이 빈출이며 Part 4에서는 '공연'의 뜻으로 나온다.
In the sense of "results" it is mostly uncountable. Performance review/evaluation (staff review) is common, and in Part 4 it means a show.
words/#02-09/q/k: 소유격과 형용사 뒤의 명사 자리이며 '올해의 뛰어난 성과'라는 뜻이므로 performance가 정답. performer는 사람명사라 Ms. Bauer's performer는 의미가 통하지 않는다.
The blank follows a possessive and an adjective, so it needs a noun meaning "excellent results this year": performance. Performer is a person noun, so Ms. Bauer's performer makes no sense.
words/#02-10/exKo: 모든 직원은 상사와 함께 연례 평가 면담을 한다.
Every staff member has a yearly review meeting with his or her supervisor.
words/#02-10/tip: performance appraisal은 performance evaluation, performance review로 바꿔 쓰인다. 동사 appraise를 apprise(알리다)와 혼동하지 말 것.
Performance appraisal is paraphrased as performance evaluation or performance review. Don't confuse the verb appraise with apprise (to inform).
words/#02-10/q/k: 직원의 강점과 개선점을 파악하기 위해 1년에 두 번 실시하는 것은 '인사 고과'이므로 appraisals가 정답. approvals(승인), applause(박수), appliances(가전제품)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.

What is done twice a year to find employees' strengths and weak points is a staff review, so appraisals is correct. Approvals (permissions), applause (clapping), and appliances (household machines) don't fit the meaning.
words/#02-11/exKo: Cho 씨는 탁월한 고객 서비스로 상을 받았다.
Ms. Cho won an award for her excellent customer service.
words/#02-11/tip: '뛰어난' 외에 '미지불의(outstanding balance/payment)'라는 뜻이 Part 7 청구서 지문에 자주 나오며 unpaid, overdue로 바꿔 표현된다.
Besides "excellent," the meaning "unpaid" (outstanding balance/payment) is common in Part 7 bills and is paraphrased as unpaid or overdue.
words/#02-11/q/k: 연체료를 피하려면 '미지불' 잔액을 내야 하므로 outstanding이 정답. outgoing(외향적인, 떠나는), outdated(구식의), outlying(외딴)은 balance와 어울리지 않는다.
To avoid a late fee you must pay the "unpaid" amount, so outstanding is correct. Outgoing (sociable; leaving), outdated (old-fashioned), and outlying (remote) don't go with balance.
words/#02-12/exKo: Silva 씨는 팀을 돕기 위해 자주 늦게까지 남는 헌신적인 직원이다.
Mr. Silva is a committed employee who often stays late to help his team.
words/#02-12/tip: 'be dedicated to + 명사/동명사'에서 to는 전치사이므로 동사원형이 아니라 -ing가 온다. '전용의(a dedicated parking area)'라는 뜻도 나온다.
In be dedicated to + noun/gerund, to is a preposition, so use -ing, not a base verb. It also means "for one use only" (a dedicated parking area).
words/#02-12/q/k: 빈칸 뒤 to providing(전치사 to + 동명사)과 결합하는 것은 'be dedicated to -ing'이므로 dedicated가 정답. eager, willing, able은 to 뒤에 동사원형이 온다.
The blank combines with to providing (preposition to + gerund) in be dedicated to -ing, so dedicated is correct. The adjectives eager, willing, and able are followed by to + base verb.
words/#02-13/m/1: to know (someone) when you see them
words/#02-13/exKo: The company honored Ms. Ito for ten years of loyal service.
words/#02-13/col/1/k: to be accepted as; to be known as
words/#02-13/tip: 'recognize A for B(B의 공로로 A를 표창하다)' 구문이 시상식 지문에 자주 나온다. 'be recognized as(~로 인정받다)'도 함께 기억할 것.
The pattern recognize A for B (honor A for B) often appears in award texts. Also remember be recognized as (to be accepted as).
words/#02-13/q/k: 연례 연회에서 합병에 기여한 공로로 직원들을 '표창했다'는 뜻이므로 recognized가 정답. realized(깨달았다), reminded(상기시켰다), remarked(언급했다)는 'A for B' 구조와 의미상 어울리지 않는다.

At the annual banquet the CEO "honored" employees for their part in the merger, so recognized is correct. Realized (understood), reminded, and remarked (commented) don't fit the A for B structure in meaning.
words/#02-14/exKo: Grant 씨는 혁신적인 디자인을 인정받아 상을 받았다.
Mr. Grant received an award for his innovative designs.
words/#02-14/col/0/k: in honor of; as thanks for
words/#02-14/tip: 'in recognition of(~을 인정하여, ~의 공로로)'는 시상 관련 Part 5·6의 단골 표현이다. 'brand recognition'은 '브랜드 인지도'를 뜻한다.
The phrase in recognition of (in honor of, as thanks for) is a regular in award-related Part 5·6. Brand recognition means how well-known a brand is.
words/#02-14/q/k: 전치사 in 뒤의 명사 자리이며 'in recognition of(~을 기려)'는 고정 표현이므로 recognition이 정답.
After the preposition in, the blank needs a noun, and in recognition of (in honor of) is fixed, so recognition is correct.
words/#02-15/m/0: to give a prize or bonus to
words/#02-15/exKo: 그 회사는 최우수 영업 사원들에게 전액 회사 부담 여행으로 보상한다.
The company gives its top sales staff a trip with all costs paid as a prize.
words/#02-15/col/0/k: to give A B as a prize
words/#02-15/col/1/k: to give A something for B
words/#02-15/tip: 'reward A for B(이유) / reward A with B(보상 수단)'의 전치사 구분이 핵심이다. 형용사 rewarding은 '보람 있는(a rewarding career)'이라는 뜻이니 '보상받는'으로 착각하지 말 것.
The key is the preposition: reward A for B (the reason) vs. reward A with B (what is given). The adjective rewarding means "satisfying" (a rewarding career), not "being paid".
words/#02-15/q/k: 직원은 현금 보너스로 '보상받는' 대상이므로 will be 뒤에 수동태를 만드는 과거분사 rewarded가 정답. rewarding은 '보람 있는'이라는 형용사로 with와 어울리지 않는다.
Employees "are given" a cash bonus, so after will be, the past participle rewarded, forming the passive, is correct. Rewarding is an adjective meaning "satisfying" and doesn't go with with.
words/#02-16/exKo: 그 회사는 판매 목표를 달성한 직원들에게 금전적 장려금을 제공한다.
The firm offers bonus payments to employees who reach their sales targets.
words/#02-16/tip: 'an incentive to do', 'an incentive for + 대상' 형태로 쓰며 가산명사다. Part 7에서는 bonus, reward로 바꿔 표현된다.
Used as an incentive to do and an incentive for + person; it is countable. In Part 7 it is paraphrased as bonus or reward.
words/#02-16/q/k: 카풀을 장려하기 위해 기업에 제공하는 것은 세금 '혜택(장려책)'이므로 incentives가 정답. inventories(재고), instances(사례), intentions(의도)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
To encourage carpooling, the city gives companies tax "benefits", so incentives is correct. Inventories (stock), instances (examples), and intentions (plans) don't fit the meaning.
words/#02-17/exKo: Jung 씨는 추가 업무를 맡게 된 후 상사에게 임금 인상을 요청했다.
After taking on extra duties, Ms. Jung asked her manager for higher pay.
words/#02-17/tip: 명사 raise는 '임금 인상'으로 Part 3에 자주 나온다. 동사 raise(타동사, ~을 올리다)와 rise(자동사, 오르다)의 구분은 Part 5 단골 문제다.
The noun raise (pay increase) is common in Part 3. Telling apart the verbs raise (transitive, to lift something) and rise (intransitive, to go up) is a regular Part 5 question.
words/#02-17/q/k: 뛰어난 판매 실적 덕분에 받은 것은 '임금 인상'이므로 명사 raise가 정답. refund(환불), receipt(영수증), reduction(감소)은 실적에 대한 보상이 될 수 없다.

What he received for his excellent sales record is a pay increase, so the noun raise is correct. Refund (money back), receipt (proof of payment), and reduction (decrease) can't be a reward for results.
words/#02-18/exKo: 우리 회사의 승진은 연공서열이 아니라 실력에 따라 이루어진다.
Promotions at our company depend on ability, not on years of service.
words/#02-18/tip: 'based on merit(실력에 따라)', 'merit-based pay(성과급)'가 인사 문맥의 핵심 표현이다. 'the merits of(~의 장점)' 형태로 제안서 지문에도 나온다.
The phrases based on merit (according to ability) and merit-based pay (pay based on results) are key HR phrases. The form the merits of (the advantages of) also appears in proposal texts.
words/#02-18/q/k: 근속 기간(length of service)과 대조되는 기준이므로 '실력, 공적'을 뜻하는 merit가 정답. seniority, tenure, duration은 모두 근속 기간과 같은 뜻이라 rather than 앞에 올 수 없다.

It is the standard contrasted with length of service, so merit (ability, achievement) is correct. The words seniority, tenure, and duration all relate to time served, so they can't come before rather than here.
words/#02-19/exKo: 이사는 그 프로젝트에 기여한 모든 사람의 노고를 인정했다.
The director thanked everyone who worked hard on the project.
words/#02-19/tip: 'acknowledge receipt of(~을 받았음을 알리다)'는 이메일·서신 지문의 빈출 표현이다. 타동사이므로 뒤에 바로 목적어나 that절이 온다.
The phrase acknowledge receipt of (to confirm you got something) is common in e-mails and letters. It is transitive, so an object or that-clause follows directly.
words/#02-19/q/k: 'acknowledge receipt of(~을 받았음을 확인하다)'는 고정 표현이므로 acknowledge가 정답. recognize, admit, appreciate는 receipt와 결합해 수령 확인의 뜻을 만들지 못한다.
The phrase acknowledge receipt of (to confirm you received) is fixed, so acknowledge is correct. The verbs recognize, admit, and appreciate don't combine with receipt to mean "confirm receipt".
words/#02-20/exKo: 그 상은 회사 성장에 대한 Ross 씨의 기여를 기리는 것이다.
The award honors Mr. Ross for the part he played in the company's growth.
words/#02-20/col/0/k: to help bring about; to give to
words/#02-20/der/0/m: to help bring about; to donate
words/#02-20/der/1/m: person who helps; writer (for a publication)
words/#02-20/tip: 'contribution to + 명사'와 'contribute to + 명사/동명사'의 전치사 to가 핵심이다. '기부금'의 뜻으로도 쓰인다.
The key is the preposition to in contribution to + noun and contribute to + noun/gerund. It also means "donation".
words/#02-20/mq/k: 소유격 her와 형용사 significant 뒤의 명사 자리이며 '재생 에너지 분야에 대한 기여'라는 뜻이므로 contribution이 정답. contributor는 사람명사라 의미가 맞지 않는다.

After the possessive her and the adjective significant, the blank needs a noun meaning "input to the field of renewable energy", so contribution is correct. Contributor is a person noun and doesn't fit the meaning.
words/#02-21/exKo: Ahmed 씨는 유용한 연구 기사를 동료들과 자주 공유한다.
Ms. Ahmed often passes on useful research articles to her coworkers.
words/#02-21/tip: Part 2·3에서 coworker, associate로 자주 바꿔 표현된다. 가산명사이므로 a colleague of mine 또는 colleagues 형태로 쓴다.
In Part 2·3 it is often paraphrased as coworker or associate. It is countable: a colleague of mine, colleagues.
words/#02-21/q/k: 교육에 참석하는 동안 근무를 대신 맡아 달라고 부탁할 대상은 '동료'이므로 colleague가 정답. 철자가 비슷한 college(대학), collection(수집품), collector(수집가)와 혼동하지 말 것.

The person you'd ask to cover your shift while you're at a training session is a coworker, so colleague is correct. Don't confuse it with the look-alikes college (university), collection (set of collected items), and collector (person who collects).
words/#02-22/exKo: 모든 장비 문제는 즉시 관리자에게 보고해야 한다.
All equipment problems should be reported to a manager right away.
words/#02-22/tip: 사람명사 supervisor와 행위명사 supervision(감독)을 구분하는 문제가 자주 나온다. 'under the supervision of(~의 감독하에)'도 빈출이다.
Questions often test the person noun supervisor vs. the action noun supervision (oversight). The phrase under the supervision of (overseen by) is also common.
words/#02-22/q/k: 휴가 요청을 승인하는 주체는 사람이므로 '직속 상사'를 뜻하는 supervisor가 정답. supervision은 '감독'이라는 행위명사라 승인의 주체가 될 수 없다.
The one who approves vacation requests is a person, so supervisor (direct boss) is correct. Supervision is an action noun (oversight) and can't be the one approving.
words/#02-23/exKo: 좋은 관리자는 부하 직원들에게 명확한 지시와 유용한 피드백을 준다.
A good manager gives clear instructions and useful feedback to the people under them.
words/#02-23/col/0/k: person who reports directly to you
words/#02-23/tip: 형용사로 'be subordinate to(~보다 하위인)'로도 쓰인다. Part 7에서는 direct report, team member로 바꿔 표현된다.
As an adjective it is also used in be subordinate to (ranking below). In Part 7 it is paraphrased as direct report or team member.
words/#02-23/q/k: 팀장으로서 교육하고 업무를 검토하는 대상은 '부하 직원'이므로 subordinates가 정답. superiors(상관), predecessors(전임자), shareholders(주주)는 팀장이 교육하는 대상이 아니다.

The people a team leader trains and whose work he checks are those under him, so subordinates is correct. Superiors (bosses), predecessors (people who held the job before), and shareholders (stock owners) aren't people a team leader trains.
words/#02-24/exKo: 허가받은 직원만 실험실에 출입할 수 있다.
Only staff with permission may enter the laboratory.
words/#02-24/tip: personnel은 집합명사로 복수 취급하며, 철자가 비슷한 personal(개인의)과 혼동하지 말 것. 'personnel department'는 human resources와 같은 뜻이다.
Personnel is a collective noun treated as plural; don't confuse it with the look-alike personal (private, individual). The personnel department means the same as human resources.
words/#02-24/q/k: 형용사 authorized의 수식을 받는 명사 자리이며 '허가받은 직원'이라는 뜻이므로 personnel이 정답. personal은 형용사, personally는 부사이고 personality(성격)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.

The blank is a noun modified by the adjective authorized, meaning "staff with permission", so personnel is correct. Personal is an adjective, personally is an adverb, and personality (character) doesn't fit the meaning.
words/#02-25/exKo: 그 회사는 내년에 인력을 15퍼센트 늘릴 계획이다.
The company plans to grow its staff by 15 percent next year.
words/#02-25/tip: 회사 전체 직원을 하나로 묶는 단수 명사다(the entire workforce). Part 7에서는 staff, employees로 바꿔 표현된다.
It is a singular noun for all of a company's workers as one group (the entire workforce). In Part 7 it is paraphrased as staff or employees.
words/#02-25/q/k: 원격으로 '일하는' 주체는 사람이므로 회사의 '전체 인력'을 뜻하는 workforce가 정답. workplace(직장), workshop(연수회), workload(업무량)는 일하는 주체가 될 수 없다.
The ones who "work" remotely are people, so workforce (all the workers) is correct. Workplace (place of work), workshop (training session), and workload (amount of work) can't be the ones working.
words/#02-26/exKo: 새로운 유연 근무제는 직원들의 사기를 크게 높였다.
The new flexible schedule has greatly lifted employees' spirits.
words/#02-26/tip: 철자가 비슷한 moral(도덕적인, 교훈)과 혼동하지 말 것. 'boost/improve morale'이 대표 연어이며 불가산명사다.
Don't confuse it with the look-alike moral (ethical; lesson). The key collocation is boost/improve morale, and it is uncountable.
words/#02-26/q/k: 힘든 한 해를 보낸 직원들의 '사기'를 높이기 위한 행사이므로 morale이 정답. moral(도덕, 교훈), mortal(죽을 운명의), model(모델)은 boost와 의미상 어울리지 않는다.
The event was to lift the "spirits" of staff after a hard year, so morale is correct. Moral (ethics; lesson), mortal (not living forever), and model don't fit with boost in meaning.
words/#02-27/m/0: to give a reason to act
words/#02-27/exKo: 유능한 관리자는 바쁜 시기에 팀에 동기를 부여하는 방법을 안다.
Good managers know how to keep their teams driven during busy periods.
words/#02-27/tip: 'motivate A to do' 형태로 쓴다. 채용 공고의 'highly motivated individuals(의욕이 넘치는 인재)'처럼 형용사 motivated도 빈출이다.
Used as motivate A to do. The adjective motivated is also common, as in job ads seeking highly motivated individuals (very driven people).
words/#02-27/q/k: to 뒤 동사원형 자리이며 'motivate A to do(A가 ~하도록 동기를 부여하다)' 구조이므로 motivate가 정답. motivation은 명사, motivational과 motivated는 형용사다.
The blank is a base verb after to, in the pattern motivate A to do (encourage A to do), so motivate is correct. Motivation is a noun, and motivational and motivated are adjectives.
words/#02-28/m/0: to speak well of; to commend
words/#02-28/exKo: 비평가들은 그 호텔 레스토랑의 창의적인 메뉴를 칭찬했다.
Critics spoke highly of the hotel restaurant's creative menu.
words/#02-28/tip: 'praise A for B(B에 대해 A를 칭찬하다)'의 전치사 for를 기억할 것. 명사로도 쓰이며 'receive praise from'처럼 불가산으로 쓴다.
Remember the preposition for in praise A for B. It is also an uncountable noun, as in receive praise from.
words/#02-28/q/k: 목적어 the staff와 for B를 함께 취하는 'praise A for B' 구문이므로 praised가 정답. complain, apologize, object는 자동사라 목적어를 바로 받을 수 없다.
The blank takes the object the staff plus for B, in the pattern praise A for B, so praised is correct. The verbs complain, apologize, and object are intransitive and can't take an object directly.
words/#02-29/exKo: Park 씨는 동료들에 의해 올해의 직원상 후보로 추천되었다.
Ms. Park's coworkers put her forward for the Employee of the Year award.
words/#02-29/col/0/k: to put A forward for B
words/#02-29/tip: 'be nominated for + 상/직책' 형태가 빈출이다. 사람명사 nominee(후보자)와 행위명사 nomination(추천)을 구분할 것.
The form be nominated for + award/post is common. Tell apart the person noun nominee (candidate) and the action noun nomination (putting forward).
words/#02-29/q/k: 조동사 may 뒤의 동사원형 자리이므로 nominate가 정답. nomination과 nominee는 명사, nominal(명목상의)은 형용사다.
After the modal may, the blank needs a base verb, so nominate is correct. Nomination and nominee are nouns, and nominal (in name only) is an adjective.
words/#02-30/exKo: 정부 계약을 따낸 것은 올해 그 팀의 가장 큰 성과였다.
Winning the government contract was the team's biggest achievement this year.
words/#02-30/der/0/m: to achieve; to manage to do
words/#02-30/tip: 형용사 accomplished는 '숙련된, 뛰어난(an accomplished pianist)'이라는 뜻이니 '완료된'으로만 해석하지 말 것. accomplishment는 가산명사다.
The adjective accomplished means "highly skilled" (an accomplished pianist), not just "completed". Accomplishment is countable.
words/#02-30/q/k: 관사 a와 형용사 remarkable 뒤의 명사 자리이므로 accomplishment가 정답. accomplish는 동사, accomplished는 형용사라 명사 자리에 올 수 없다.
After the article a and the adjective remarkable, the blank needs a noun, so accomplishment is correct. Accomplish is a verb and accomplished is an adjective, so they can't fill a noun slot.
words/#02-31/exKo: Hong 씨는 물류 분야에서 수년간 경력을 쌓은 매우 유능한 관리자다.
Mr. Hong is a very competent manager with years of experience in logistics.
words/#02-31/tip: 'be capable of + -ing'로 쓰며 to부정사를 쓰지 않는다. 같은 뜻의 able은 'be able to do'이므로 두 형태를 혼동시키는 문제가 나온다.
Use be capable of + -ing, not a to-infinitive. The similar able is be able to do, and questions try to mix up the two forms.
words/#02-31/q/k: 빈칸 뒤 of producing과 결합하는 것은 'be capable of -ing'이므로 capable이 정답. able은 to부정사와 쓰고, possible과 available은 of -ing와 쓰지 않는다.
The blank combines with of producing in be capable of -ing, so capable is correct. Able is used with a to-infinitive, and possible and available aren't used with of -ing.
words/#02-32/exKo: Ford 씨는 항상 보고서를 꼼꼼히 재확인하는 성실한 직원이다.
Ms. Ford is a hardworking employee who always checks her reports twice.
words/#02-32/tip: 부사 diligently가 동사를 수식하는 자리, 형용사 diligent가 명사를 수식하는 자리를 구분하는 문제로 출제된다. Part 7에서는 hardworking으로 바꿔 표현된다.
Questions test the adverb diligently (describing a verb) vs. the adjective diligent (describing a noun). In Part 7 it is paraphrased as hardworking.
words/#02-32/q/k: 정관사 the와 명사 efforts 사이에서 명사를 수식하는 형용사 자리이므로 diligent가 정답. diligently와 most diligently는 부사라 명사를 꾸밀 수 없다.
Between the article the and the noun efforts, the blank needs an adjective, so diligent is correct. Diligently and most diligently are adverbs and can't describe a noun.
words/#02-33/exKo: 직원들은 모든 고객 회의에 시간을 지켜야 한다.
Employees must be on time for all client meetings.
words/#02-33/der/1/m: on time; exactly at the set time
words/#02-33/tip: be punctual은 Part 7에서 'arrive on time'으로 바꿔 표현된다. 명사 punctuality는 인사 평가 항목(attendance and punctuality)으로 자주 나온다.
In Part 7, be punctual is paraphrased as arrive on time. The noun punctuality often appears as an item in staff reviews (attendance and punctuality).
words/#02-33/q/k: 20분 늦게 도착해서 팀이 놀랐다고 했으므로 평소에 '시간을 잘 지키는' 사람이라는 뜻의 punctual이 정답. generous(관대한), talkative(수다스러운), cautious(신중한)는 지각과 대조되지 않는다.
The team was surprised when he came 20 minutes late, so he is usually "on time": punctual is correct. Generous (giving), talkative (chatty), and cautious (careful) don't contrast with being late.
words/#02-34/exKo: Kerr 씨가 자리를 비운 동안 Diaz 씨가 고객 전화를 처리한다.
Ms. Diaz will take client calls while Mr. Kerr is away.
words/#02-34/tip: 'in(during) one's absence(~가 없는 동안)' 형태로 업무 대행 문맥에 자주 나온다. 형용사 absent는 'be absent from(~에 결석하다)'으로 쓴다.
The form in (during) one's absence (while someone is away) often appears when someone covers another's work. The adjective absent is used as be absent from (to be away from).
words/#02-34/q/k: 정관사 the 뒤, 전치사 of 앞의 명사 자리이며 'in the absence of(~가 없을 때)'는 고정 표현이므로 absence가 정답. absentee는 '결석자'라 의미가 맞지 않는다.

After the article the and before the preposition of, the blank needs a noun, and in the absence of (when there is no) is fixed, so absence is correct. Absentee (a person who is away) doesn't fit the meaning.
words/#02-35/exKo: Burke 씨는 아버지를 돌보기 위해 6개월간 휴직했다.
Mr. Burke took six months off work to care for his father.
words/#02-35/col/1/k: to ask for extended time off
words/#02-35/tip: 'on leave(휴가 중인)', 'maternity leave(출산 휴가)'처럼 leave는 명사 '휴가'로 쓰인다. Part 7에서 장기간 자리를 비우는 이유를 묻는 문제의 근거가 된다.

Leave is also a noun meaning "time off", as in on leave (away on time off) and maternity leave (time off after having a baby). In Part 7 it is the basis for questions about why someone is away for a long time.
words/#02-35/q/k: 대학원 공부를 마치기 위해 1년간 허락받은 것은 '휴직'이므로 leave of absence가 정답. turnover(이직률), attendance(출석)는 의미가 맞지 않고 step down은 동사구라 관사 뒤에 올 수 없다.

What she was granted for a year to finish graduate school is extended time off, so leave of absence is correct. Turnover (rate of staff leaving) and attendance (being present) don't fit the meaning, and step down is a verb phrase, so it can't follow an article.
words/#02-36/exKo: The company's founder will leave the post of chairman at the end of the year.
words/#02-36/tip: 'step down as + 직책', 'step down from + 직위' 형태로 쓰며 Part 7에서 resign, retire로 바꿔 표현된다. 자동사구라 수동태로 쓰지 않는다.
Used as step down as + job title and step down from + post; in Part 7 it is paraphrased as resign or retire. It is an intransitive phrasal verb, so it isn't used in the passive.
words/#02-36/q/k: 적합한 후임자가 정해지면 CEO 자리에서 '물러나겠다'는 뜻이므로 step down이 정답. step up(나서다), step in(개입하다, 대신 맡다), step out(잠시 자리를 비우다)은 후임자 문맥과 맞지 않는다.

He will "leave" the CEO post once a suitable successor is found, so step down is correct. Step up (to take action), step in (to get involved; to fill in), and step out (to leave briefly) don't fit the successor context.
words/#02-37/exKo: 고위 임원 여러 명이 신규 투자자들과의 회의에 참석했다.
Several top managers attended the meeting with the new investors.
words/#02-37/col/1/k: head of the whole company; CEO
words/#02-37/tip: executive는 명사(임원)와 형용사(경영의, 임원의: executive committee)로 모두 쓰인다. -ive로 끝나지만 명사 자리에 올 수 있다는 점을 노린 문제가 나온다.
Executive is both a noun (senior manager) and an adjective (managerial: executive committee). Questions use the fact that it ends in -ive but can fill a noun slot.
words/#02-37/q/k: as a sales 뒤 '영업 담당자'라는 직책을 나타내는 명사 자리이므로 executive가 정답. -ive로 끝나지만 사람을 뜻하는 명사로 쓰인다.
After as a sales, the blank is a noun naming a job (sales representative), so executive is correct. It ends in -ive but works as a noun for a person.
words/#02-38/exKo: 그 부서는 늘어난 업무량을 처리하기 위해 보조 직원 두 명을 채용했다.
The department hired two assistants to help with the extra work.
words/#02-38/col/1/k: to manage the amount of work
words/#02-38/col/2/k: to lighten the amount of work
words/#02-38/tip: 'heavy workload(과중한 업무)'가 Part 3에서 도움을 요청하는 이유로 자주 나온다. 셀 때는 a heavy workload처럼 단수로 쓴다.
Heavy workload (too much work) often appears in Part 3 as the reason someone asks for help. It is singular when counted: a heavy workload.
words/#02-38/q/k: 워크숍에 참석하지 못한 이유로 '과중한 업무량'이 적절하므로 workload가 정답. workforce(인력), workplace(직장), workstation(작업 공간)은 heavy와 함께 이유가 되지 않는다.
Too much work is a fitting reason for missing the workshop, so workload is correct. Workforce (all the workers), workplace (place of work), and workstation (work area) don't give a reason with heavy.
words/#02-39/exKo: 시장은 홍수 기간 동안 보여 준 노고에 대해 자원봉사자들을 칭찬했다.
The mayor praised the volunteers for their hard work during the flood.
words/#02-39/tip: 'commend A for B'는 praise A for B와 같은 구조로, for 뒤에 칭찬의 이유가 온다. 형용사 commendable(칭찬받을 만한)은 주로 effort, achievement 같은 명사를 수식한다.
The pattern commend A for B has the same structure as praise A for B, with the reason after for. The adjective commendable (deserving praise) usually describes nouns like effort or achievement.
words/#02-39/q/k: 투숙객의 호평을 받은 것에 대해 객실 관리 직원들을 '칭찬했다'는 뜻이므로 commended가 정답. 형태가 비슷한 commanded(명령했다), commenced(시작했다), committed(저질렀다)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.

The manager "praised" the housekeeping staff for getting great guest reviews, so commended is correct. The look-alikes commanded (ordered), commenced (began), and committed (carried out) don't fit the meaning.
words/#02-40/exKo: 그 회사는 더 나은 교육 기회를 제공해 직원 이직률을 낮췄다.
The company cut the rate of staff leaving by offering better training opportunities.
words/#02-40/tip: 인사 문맥에서는 '이직률', 영국식 재무 문맥에서는 '매출액'을 뜻한다. 'high/low turnover rate' 형태가 Part 7에 자주 나온다.
In HR contexts it means how often staff leave; in British finance contexts it means sales revenue. The form high/low turnover rate often appears in Part 7.
words/#02-40/q/k: 직원 중 학생이 많아 직원 '이직'이 잦다는 뜻이므로 turnover가 정답. takeover(인수), overturn(전복), turnout(참석자 수)은 의미가 맞지 않는다.
Many of the workers are students, so staff "leave" often: turnover is correct. Takeover (buying a company), overturn (reversal), and turnout (number of people who attend) don't fit the meaning.
words/#03-01/m/0: task, piece of work (given to you)
words/#03-01/exKo: Doyle 씨의 첫 업무는 고객 데이터베이스를 업데이트하는 것이었다.
Mr. Doyle's first task was to update the client database.
words/#03-01/tip: 가산명사(an assignment)이며 'on assignment(업무로 파견 중인)'가 Part 7에 나온다. 동사 assign과 품사를 구분하는 문제가 자주 출제된다.
It is countable (an assignment), and on assignment (sent away for work) appears in Part 7. Part-of-speech questions often test it against the verb assign.
words/#03-01/q/k: 관사 a와 형용사 different 뒤의 명사 자리이므로 assignment가 정답. assign은 동사, assigned와 assigning은 분사라 명사 자리에 올 수 없다.
After the article a and the adjective different, the blank needs a noun, so assignment is correct. Assign is a verb, and assigned and assigning are participles, so they can't fill a noun slot.
words/#03-02/m/1: to place (a person in a role)
words/#03-02/exKo: 관리자는 Henderson 거래처 업무를 Park 씨에게 배정했다.
The manager gave the Henderson account to Ms. Park.
words/#03-02/col/0/k: to give A to B (as a task)
words/#03-02/tip: 'assign A to B'와 수동형 'be assigned to + 부서/업무'가 빈출이다. 'assigned seating(지정 좌석)'처럼 과거분사가 명사를 수식하기도 한다.
The patterns assign A to B and the passive be assigned to + department/task are common. The past participle also describes nouns, as in assigned seating (reserved seats).
words/#03-02/q/k: 신입 직원이 첫 3개월 동안 멘토에게 '배정된다'는 뜻이므로 'be assigned to'의 assigned가 정답. designed(설계된), signed(서명된), resigned(체념한)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.

New employees will "be matched" with a mentor for their first three months, so assigned, from be assigned to, is correct. Designed (planned, drawn up), signed (with a signature), and resigned (accepting something bad) don't fit the meaning.
words/#03-03/exKo: Reed 씨는 회사 연례 회의 준비를 담당하고 있다.
Ms. Reed is responsible for planning the company's annual conference.
words/#03-03/col/2/k: to put A in control of B
words/#03-03/tip: 'be in charge of + 명사/동명사'는 be responsible for로 바꿔 표현되며 Part 3·4에서 화자의 담당 업무를 묻는 문제의 근거가 된다. 'free of charge(무료로)'와 구분할 것.
The phrase be in charge of + noun/gerund is paraphrased as be responsible for and, in Part 3·4, is the basis for questions about a speaker's job. Don't confuse it with free of charge (at no cost).
words/#03-03/q/k: 'be in charge of(~을 담당하다)'는 고정 표현이므로 charge가 정답. responsible은 'be responsible for'로 쓰며, in duty of와 in order of는 이 의미로 쓰이지 않는다.
The phrase be in charge of (to be responsible for) is fixed, so charge is correct. Responsible is used as be responsible for, and in duty of and in order of aren't used with this meaning.
words/#03-04/exKo: 우리 고객 서비스팀은 하루에 500통이 넘는 전화를 처리한다.
Our customer service team takes care of over 500 calls a day.
words/#03-04/tip: handle은 타동사라 전치사 없이 바로 목적어를 받는다. 같은 뜻의 deal with는 전치사 with가 필요하다는 점을 이용한 문제가 나온다.
Handle is transitive, so it takes an object directly with no preposition. Questions use the fact that deal with (same meaning) needs the preposition with.
words/#03-04/q/k: 빈칸 뒤 목적어 all inquiries를 바로 취하는 타동사가 필요하므로 handle이 정답. deal은 with, respond와 reply는 to가 있어야 목적어를 받을 수 있다.
The blank needs a transitive verb that takes the object all inquiries directly, so handle is correct. Deal needs with, and respond and reply need to before an object.
words/#03-05/exKo: 새 관리자는 배송 문제를 신속하고 침착하게 처리했다.
The new manager sorted out the shipping problem quickly and calmly.
words/#03-05/tip: 과거형·과거분사형은 dealt with이다. 같은 뜻의 handle, address는 타동사라 전치사 없이 쓴다는 점을 구분할 것.
The past and past participle are dealt with. Remember that handle and address (same meaning) are transitive and need no preposition.
words/#03-05/q/k: 'deal with(~을 처리하다)'는 전치사 with와 짝을 이루므로 with가 정답. deal은 for, about, to와 결합해 '처리하다'의 뜻을 만들지 않는다.
The verb deal pairs with the preposition with to mean "handle", so with is correct. Deal doesn't combine with for, about, or to to mean "handle".
words/#03-06/exKo: 모든 직원은 휴가를 신청할 때 정해진 절차를 따라야 한다.
All staff must follow the official steps when asking for time off.
words/#03-06/tip: 'follow/observe the procedure'가 대표 연어다. 형태가 비슷한 동사 proceed(진행하다), 명사 proceeds(수익금)와 혼동하지 말 것.
The key collocation is follow/observe the procedure. Don't confuse it with the look-alikes proceed (to go ahead) and proceeds (money raised).
words/#03-06/q/k: 새 장비를 작동하기 전에 읽어야 하는 것은 '안전 수칙(절차)'이므로 procedures가 정답. proceeds(수익금), processions(행렬), professions(직업)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
What you read before using new equipment is the safety rules (steps), so procedures is correct. Proceeds (money raised), processions (parades), and professions (careers) don't fit the meaning.
words/#03-07/exKo: Lee 씨는 고객 회의에 서류를 가져오는 것을 잊었다.
Mr. Lee forgot to bring the papers to the client meeting.
words/#03-07/tip: 동사로 '기록하다, 문서화하다'라는 뜻도 있다. 불가산명사 documentation(증빙 서류 일체)과 가산명사 document를 구분할 것.
As a verb it means "to record in writing". Tell apart the uncountable documentation (all supporting papers) and the countable document.
words/#03-07/q/k: 형용사 required 뒤에서 동사 submit의 목적어가 되는 명사 자리이므로 documents가 정답. documentary는 형용사, documented와 documenting은 분사다.
After the adjective required, the blank is a noun as the object of submit, so documents is correct. Documentary is an adjective, and documented and documenting are participles.
words/#03-08/exKo: Kato 씨는 퇴임하는 이사를 위한 송별회를 준비했다.
Ms. Kato planned a farewell party for the director who was retiring.
words/#03-08/tip: 행사를 '준비하다'와 서류를 '정리하다'의 두 뜻으로 모두 쓰인다. 사람명사 organizer(주최자)와 organization(단체)을 구분하는 문제가 나온다.
It means both "to plan (an event)" and "to sort (papers)". Questions test the person noun organizer vs. organization (group).
words/#03-08/q/k: be동사와 부사 well 뒤에서 회의가 '준비된' 것이므로 수동의 과거분사 organized가 정답. organizer와 organization은 명사라 well의 수식을 받을 수 없다.
After the be-verb and the adverb well, the conference "was planned", so the passive past participle organized is correct. Organizer and organization are nouns and can't be modified by well.
words/#03-09/exKo: 접수원이 입구에서 방문객들에게 이름표를 나누어 준다.
The receptionist will hand out name tags to visitors at the entrance.
words/#03-09/col/0/k: to hand out A to B
words/#03-09/tip: 'distribute A to B(A를 B에게 배포하다)' 구조가 핵심이며 Part 1·7에서 hand out으로 바꿔 표현된다. 명사 distributor는 '유통업체'를 뜻한다.
The key structure is distribute A to B, and in Part 1·7 it is paraphrased as hand out. The noun distributor means a supply company.
words/#03-09/q/k: 수정된 일정표 사본이 팀원들에게 '배포된다'는 뜻이므로 distributed가 정답. contributed(기여된), attributed(~의 덕분으로 여겨지는), described(설명된)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
Copies of the new schedule will be "handed out" to team members, so distributed is correct. Contributed (given to help), attributed (credited to), and described (explained) don't fit the meaning.
words/#03-10/exKo: 관리자는 회의 안건을 모든 참석자에게 미리 회람시켰다.
The manager sent the meeting agenda around to all participants beforehand.
words/#03-10/der/0/m: flow; spread; number of copies sold
words/#03-10/tip: 문서를 여러 사람에게 '돌리다'라는 뜻으로 distribute와 바꿔 쓸 수 있다. 명사 circulation은 신문·잡지의 '발행 부수'라는 뜻으로도 나온다.
In the sense of "passing a document around" it can replace distribute. The noun circulation also means the number of copies a newspaper or magazine sells.
words/#03-10/q/k: 의견을 받기 위해 제안서 초안을 부서장들 사이에 '회람시켰다'는 뜻이므로 circulated가 정답. calculated(계산된), complicated(복잡한), cultivated(재배된)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
The draft was "passed around" department heads for comments, so circulated is correct. Calculated (worked out with numbers), complicated (complex), and cultivated (grown) don't fit the meaning.
words/#03-11/exKo: 회람에 따르면, 엘리베이터는 월요일에 수리를 위해 운행을 중단한다.
According to the staff notice, the elevator will be shut for repairs on Monday.
words/#03-11/tip: memorandum의 줄임말로 Part 6·7 지문 유형으로 자주 나온다. 회람의 '목적'을 묻는 문제는 대개 첫 단락에 근거가 있다.
Short for memorandum, it is a common text type in Part 6·7. Questions about a memo's purpose usually find their answer in the first paragraph.
words/#03-11/q/k: 새 보안 정책을 상기시키기 위해 전 직원에게 보낸 것은 '회람'이므로 memo가 정답. 철자가 비슷한 menu(메뉴), meter(계량기), memory(기억)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
What she sent to all staff to remind them of the new security policy is a staff notice, so memo is correct. The look-alikes menu, meter (measuring device), and memory don't fit the meaning.
words/#03-12/exKo: 고객은 주문품이 발송되면 이메일로 통지를 받는다.
Customers will get an e-mail when their orders have shipped.
words/#03-12/tip: notify는 사람을 목적어로 취해 'notify A of B', 'notify A that' 형태로 쓴다. announce, explain처럼 사람을 바로 목적어로 받지 못하는 동사와 구분하는 문제가 나온다.
Notify takes a person as its object: notify A of B, notify A that. Questions contrast it with verbs like announce and explain, which can't take a person as a direct object.
words/#03-12/q/k: 사람 목적어(their supervisor) 뒤에 of B가 이어지는 'notify A of B' 구조이므로 notify가 정답. announce, explain, mention은 사람을 직접 목적어로 취하지 않는다.
The person object (their supervisor) is followed by of B, in the pattern notify A of B, so notify is correct. The verbs announce, explain, and mention don't take a person as a direct object.
words/#03-13/exKo: 항공사는 승객들에게 항공편이 지연될 것이라고 알렸다.
The airline told passengers that the flight would be late.
words/#03-13/col/1/k: to keep A up to date
words/#03-13/tip: 'inform A of(about) B', 'inform A that' 구조로 사람 목적어가 먼저 온다. 형용사 informative(유익한)와 informed(잘 아는)의 의미 차이도 자주 묻는다.
The patterns are inform A of (about) B and inform A that, with the person first. Questions often test the difference between informative (useful) and informed (knowing a lot).
words/#03-13/q/k: 사람 목적어 you 뒤에 that절이 오는 'inform A that' 구조이므로 inform이 정답. explain, describe, announce는 사람을 직접 목적어로 취하지 않는다.
The person object you is followed by a that-clause, in the pattern inform A that, so inform is correct. The verbs explain, describe, and announce don't take a person as a direct object.
words/#03-14/exKo: 비서는 Shaw 씨에게 2시 약속을 다시 알려 주었다.
The assistant reminded Mr. Shaw of his two o'clock appointment.
words/#03-14/col/0/k: to tell A not to forget to do
words/#03-14/col/1/k: to make A think of B; to jog A's memory about B
words/#03-14/der/0/m: note to help you remember; payment notice
words/#03-14/tip: 'remind A to do', 'remind A of B', 'remind A that' 세 구조가 모두 출제된다. 명사 reminder는 '알림, 독촉장'으로 이메일 지문에 자주 나온다.
All three patterns are tested: remind A to do, remind A of B, remind A that. The noun reminder (alert; payment notice) is common in e-mails.
words/#03-14/q/k: 'remind A to do(A에게 ~할 것을 상기시키다)' 구조이므로 reminded가 정답. remember는 '사람 목적어 + to부정사' 구조를 취하지 않으며, reviewed와 memorized는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
The pattern is remind A to do, so reminded is correct. Remember doesn't take person object + to-infinitive, and reviewed and memorized don't fit the meaning.
words/#03-15/m/0: to bring up to date; to renew
words/#03-15/exKo: IT 부서는 매달 보안 소프트웨어를 업데이트한다.
The IT department installs the newest version of the security software every month.
words/#03-15/col/0/k: A에게 B의 최신 상황을 알려 주다
to give A the latest news on B
words/#03-15/col/1/k: A에게 계속 최신 정보를 알려 주다
words/#03-15/col/2/k: to bring a database up to date
words/#03-15/tip: 'update A on B(A에게 B의 최신 상황을 알려 주다)'의 전치사 on이 출제 포인트다. 명사로도 쓰여 'an update on the project(프로젝트 진행 상황 보고)'처럼 쓴다.
The test point is the preposition on in update A on B (give A the latest news on B). It is also a noun: an update on the project (a progress report).
words/#03-15/q/k: 사람 목적어 the team 뒤에 on B가 오는 'update A on B(A에게 B의 최신 상황을 알려 주다)' 구조이므로 update가 정답. announce, report, speak는 사람을 직접 목적어로 취하지 않는다.
The person object the team is followed by on B, in the pattern update A on B, so update is correct. The verbs announce, report, and speak don't take a person as a direct object.
words/#03-16/exKo: 편집자는 저자에게 설명서의 마지막 장을 수정해 달라고 요청했다.
The editor asked the author to rework the last chapter of the manual.
words/#03-16/tip: 과거분사 revised가 명사를 수식하는 형태(revised schedule, revised policy)가 Part 5·7에 매우 자주 나온다.
The past participle revised describing a noun (revised schedule, revised policy) appears very often in Part 5·7.
words/#03-16/q/k: 정관사 the와 명사 version 사이의 형용사 자리이며 계약서가 '수정된' 것이므로 과거분사 revised가 정답. revising은 능동의 의미라 맞지 않는다.

Between the article the and the noun version, the blank needs an adjective, and the contract "has been changed", so the past participle revised is correct. Revising has an active meaning and doesn't fit.
words/#03-17/exKo: Byrne 씨는 보도 자료 초안을 검토받기 위해 관리자에게 보냈다.
Mr. Byrne sent the first version of the press release to his manager to check.
words/#03-17/tip: 동사로도 쓰여 'draft a proposal(제안서 초안을 작성하다)'처럼 쓴다. Part 7에서 문서가 아직 최종본이 아니라는 단서가 된다.
It is also a verb: draft a proposal (to write a first version). In Part 7 it is a clue that a document is not yet final.
words/#03-17/q/k: 목요일까지 의견을 보내기 위해 검토하는 대상은 연설문 '초안'이므로 draft가 정답. deposit(보증금), delay(지연), demand(수요)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
What you review in order to send comments by Thursday is the first version of the speech, so draft is correct. Deposit (money paid in advance), delay, and demand don't fit the meaning.
words/#03-18/exKo: 이사회는 새 연구 시설 예산을 승인했다.
The board gave the go-ahead for the new research facility's budget.
words/#03-18/col/1/k: to think well of; to agree with
words/#03-18/tip: 타동사 approve(승인하다)와 자동사 'approve of(~을 좋게 여기다)'의 차이에 유의할 것. 명사 approval은 'subject to approval(승인을 조건으로)'로 자주 나온다.
Note the difference between transitive approve (to authorize) and intransitive approve of (to think well of). The noun approval often appears in subject to approval (only if approved).
words/#03-18/q/k: must be 뒤에서 출장 경비가 '승인되는' 것이므로 수동태를 만드는 과거분사 approved가 정답. approving은 능동, approval은 명사다.
After must be, travel expenses "are authorized", so the past participle approved, forming the passive, is correct. Approving is active, and approval is a noun.
words/#03-19/exKo: 1만 달러가 넘는 지급은 재무 이사만 승인할 수 있다.
Only the finance director can approve payments over $10,000.
words/#03-19/col/0/k: to give A permission to do
words/#03-19/tip: 'be authorized to do(~할 권한이 있다)'와 과거분사형 형용사 authorized(공인된, 허가받은)가 빈출이다. 명사 authorization(허가)과 authority(권한, 당국)를 구분할 것.

Common forms: be authorized to do (to have permission to do) and the participle adjective authorized (official, permitted). Tell apart the nouns authorization (permission) and authority (power; officials).
words/#03-19/q/k: 'be authorized to do(~할 권한이 있다)' 구문이므로 authorized가 정답. authoritative(권위 있는)는 to부정사와 이 의미로 쓰이지 않고, authorities와 authorization은 명사다.

The pattern is be authorized to do (to have permission to do), so authorized is correct. Authoritative (reliable, commanding) isn't used with a to-infinitive in this sense, and authorities and authorization are nouns.
words/#03-20/m/0: your name written by hand (to approve)
words/#03-20/exKo: 그 계약서는 고객의 서명 없이는 효력이 없다.
The contract has no legal force unless the client signs it.
words/#03-20/col/2/k: dish a restaurant is best known for
words/#03-20/tip: 'signature dish/product(대표 메뉴, 대표 상품)'처럼 '대표적인'이라는 의미로도 쓰인다. 동사 sign과 명사 signature의 품사 구분 문제가 나온다.
It also means "best-known, typical", as in signature dish/product (a place's best-known item). Questions test the verb sign vs. the noun signature.
words/#03-20/q/k: 관사 a 뒤 동사 requires의 목적어 자리이며 택배 수령 시 '서명'이 필요하다는 뜻이므로 signature가 정답. 명사 sign(표지판)과 signal(신호)은 의미가 맞지 않고 signed는 분사다.

After the article a, the blank is the object of requires, and the package needs someone to "sign" for it, so signature is correct. The nouns sign (board with information) and signal don't fit the meaning, and signed is a participle.
words/#03-21/m/0: stationery; items used in an office
