It means "a large group of readers among engineers and architects," so the collective noun readership is correct. The singular reader doesn't go with large, reading means "the act of reading," and readable is an adjective.
words/#26-29/exKo: 그 식당은 매일 아침 소셜 미디어에 오늘의 특선 요리를 홍보한다.
The restaurant promotes its daily specials on social media every morning.
words/#26-29/tip: 'on social media'처럼 전치사 on과 함께 무관사로 쓴다. 'SNS'는 영어권에서 잘 쓰지 않으므로 social media로 기억해 둔다.
It is used with the preposition on and no article, as in on social media. The term SNS is rarely used in English, so remember social media.
words/#26-29/q/k: 고객이 '팔로우하여(follow)' 신제품 사진을 볼 수 있는 곳은 소셜 미디어이므로 social media가 정답. 나머지는 팔로우하거나 사진을 볼 수 있는 공간이 아니다.
The place where customers can "follow" the bakery and see photos of new products is social media, so it is correct. The others aren't places where you can follow someone or see photos.
words/#26-30/exKo: 그 회사의 유머러스한 광고는 게시된 지 몇 시간 만에 급속히 퍼졌다.
The company's humorous advertisement went viral within hours of being posted.
words/#26-30/tip: 'go viral(인터넷에서 급속히 퍼지다)'처럼 2형식 동사 go 뒤 보어로 쓰인다. Part 7에서는 'spread rapidly online'으로 바꿔 표현된다.
It is used as a complement after the linking verb go, as in go viral (to spread fast online). Part 7 paraphrases it as spread rapidly online.
words/#26-30/q/k: 300만 회 넘게 조회되었다는 내용과 이어지는 'go viral(급속히 퍼지다)'이므로 viral이 정답. exclusive, anonymous, editorial은 go와 결합해 조회 수 급증을 나타내지 않는다.

It connects with "viewed more than three million times," so go viral (to spread fast online) fits: viral is correct. The words exclusive, anonymous, and editorial don't combine with go to describe a sudden rise in views.
words/#26-31/m/0: single unit (of a book or newspaper)
words/#26-31/exKo: 그랜트 씨는 회의가 시작되기 전에 안건을 열 부 복사했다.
Ms. Grant made ten copies of the agenda before the meeting started.
words/#26-31/tip: 책·신문을 셀 때 'a copy of the book(책 한 부)'처럼 copy를 쓴다. 광고 업계에서는 '광고 문안(copy)'이라는 뜻으로도 쓰인다.
To count books or newspapers, use copy, as in a copy of the book (one book). In advertising it also means "ad text."
words/#26-31/q/k: 참석자가 받는 '저자 서명이 든 소설 한 부'이므로 copy가 정답. author는 사람, circulation은 발행 부수, layout은 지면 구성이라 받을 수 있는 대상이 아니다.
Attendees receive "one signed book" of the novel, so copy is correct. Author is a person, circulation the number of copies sold, and layout the page design, so none is something you receive.
words/#26-32/exKo: 그 출판사는 내년에 그 책을 12개 언어로 출간할 계획이다.
The publisher plans to release the book in twelve languages next year.
words/#26-32/tip: 사람·회사를 뜻하는 publisher와 사물·행위를 뜻하는 publication을 구분하는 품사 문제가 자주 나온다.
Part-of-speech questions often test publisher (a person or company) vs. publication (a thing or action).
words/#26-32/q/k: 원고를 읽고 계약을 '제안한' 주체이므로 사람·회사를 뜻하는 publisher가 정답. publication은 사물이라 제안할 수 없고, published와 publishing은 주어 자리에 맞지 않는다.

The one who "offered" a contract after reading the manuscript is a person or company, so publisher is correct. Publication is a thing and can't make an offer, and published and publishing don't fit the subject slot.
words/#26-33/exKo: 그 작가는 토요일에 머서 서점에서 신간에 사인을 해 줄 예정이다.
The author will sign copies of her new book at Mercer Bookstore on Saturday.
words/#26-33/tip: Part 4 공지에서 'book signing(사인회)'과 함께 자주 나오며, 동사로는 '(책·보고서를) 쓰다(author a report)'라는 뜻도 있다.
It often appears in Part 4 notices together with book signing (event where an author signs books), and as a verb it also means "to write (a book or report)" (author a report).
words/#26-33/q/k: 자신의 신작 소설에 대해 이야기하는 사람이므로 author가 정답. authority(권한, 당국), authorship(저자임)은 의미가 맞지 않고, authorize는 동사다.
The person discussing her own new novel is the writer, so author is correct. Authority (power; officials) and authorship (being the writer) don't fit, and authorize is a verb.
words/#26-34/exKo: 그 보고서는 재택근무와 생산성의 관계에 관한 여러 연구를 인용한다.
The report cites several studies on the link between remote work and productivity.
words/#26-34/tip: 'cite A as the reason(A를 이유로 들다)'처럼 이유를 언급할 때 자주 쓰인다. 발음이 같은 site(장소), sight(시야)는 LC 함정이 된다.
It is often used to state a reason, as in cite A as the reason (to give A as the reason). The same-sounding site (place) and sight (view) are listening traps.
words/#26-34/q/k: 'cite A as B(A를 B로 들다)' 구조이므로 cite가 정답. insist는 on/that절과 쓰고, refer는 'refer to A as B'처럼 to가 필요하며, speak은 목적어를 취하지 않는다.
It is the structure cite A as B (to give A as B), so cite is correct. Insist goes with on or a that-clause, refer needs to (refer to A as B), and speak doesn't take an object.
words/#26-35/exKo: 그 전기는 창업자가 작은 차고에서 어떻게 회사를 일으켰는지를 그린다.
The biography describes how the founder built the company from a small garage.
words/#26-35/tip: 행사 연사 소개 지문에서 'brief biography(약력)'의 뜻으로도 나오며, 자서전 autobiography와 구분해야 한다.
In texts introducing event speakers it also means "short profile" (brief biography), and you should tell it apart from autobiography (life story written by oneself).
words/#26-35/q/k: 학회 프로그램에 실리는 각 연사의 '약력'이므로 biography가 정답. biographer는 사람, biographical은 형용사, biology는 '생물학'이다.
It is each speaker's "short profile" printed in the conference program, so biography is correct. Biographer is a person, biographical an adjective, and biology the study of living things.
words/#26-36/exKo: 안내서의 마지막 장은 경비 보고서를 제출하는 방법을 설명한다.
The final chapter of the guide explains how to file expense reports.
words/#26-36/tip: 책의 '장' 외에 협회·단체의 '지부(local chapter)'라는 뜻으로 Part 7에 나온다.
Besides a section of a book, it also means a branch of an association (local chapter) in Part 7.
words/#26-36/q/k: 협회의 보스턴 '지부'가 행사를 연다는 내용이므로 '지부'의 뜻이 있는 chapter가 정답. edition(판), manuscript(원고), headline(표제)은 행사를 주최할 수 없다.
The association's Boston "branch" is hosting an event, so chapter, which can mean "branch," is correct. Edition (version), manuscript (unpublished text), and headline (title) can't host an event.
words/#26-37/exKo: 그 소식지는 쓰레기를 줄이기 위해 재생 용지에 인쇄된다.
The newsletter is printed on recycled paper to reduce waste.
words/#26-37/tip: 명사로 'in print(출간되어)', 'out of print(절판된)', 'fine print(작은 글씨의 세부 조항)'가 빈출이다.
As a noun, in print (available, published), out of print (no longer published), and fine print (small-type details of a contract) are common.
words/#26-37/q/k: 안내 책자가 '인쇄되어' 배달되어야 하므로 수동태를 만드는 과거분사 printed가 정답. printing은 능동 진행, printer와 prints는 be동사 뒤에서 의미가 맞지 않는다.

The brochures must "be produced on paper" and delivered, so the past participle printed, forming the passive, is correct. Printing is active progressive, and printer and prints don't make sense after the be verb.
words/#26-38/exKo: 그 자선 콘서트는 국내외에서 폭넓게 언론에 보도되었다.
The charity concert received extensive media coverage both at home and abroad.
words/#26-38/tip: cover가 '취재하다, 보도하다'의 뜻으로 쓰인다는 점이 핵심이며, extensive(광범위한), favorable(호의적인) 같은 형용사와 함께 나온다.
The key is that cover means "to report on," and it appears with adjectives like extensive (wide) and favorable (positive).
words/#26-38/q/k: media와 결합해 '언론 보도(media coverage)'를 이루는 명사 coverage가 정답. covering은 '덮개', cover는 '표지, 덮개'의 뜻이라 맞지 않고, covered는 명사 자리에 올 수 없다.

With media it forms media coverage (news reporting), so the noun coverage is correct. Covering means "a layer on top" and cover "front of a book; lid," which don't fit, and covered can't fill a noun slot.
words/#26-39/exKo: 직원들은 회사의 온라인 설문 조사를 통해 익명으로 의견을 제출할 수 있다.
Employees can submit anonymous feedback through the company's online survey.
words/#26-39/tip: 부사 anonymously('submit anonymously' 익명으로 제출하다)와 구분하는 품사 문제, 'remain anonymous'처럼 2형식 동사 뒤 보어 자리 문제가 나온다.
Part-of-speech questions test it against the adverb anonymously (submit anonymously: to submit without a name), and questions ask for the complement after a linking verb, as in remain anonymous.
words/#26-39/q/k: 2형식 동사 remain 뒤 보어 자리이므로 형용사 anonymous가 정답. anonymously는 부사라 보어가 될 수 없고, anonymity는 명사라 사람의 상태를 나타내지 못한다.

After the linking verb remain, the blank is a complement, so the adjective anonymous is correct. Anonymously is an adverb and can't be a complement, and anonymity is a noun that can't describe a person's state.
words/#26-40/m/1: date (a product or film) comes out
words/#26-40/exKo: The release date for the new smartphone has been moved up to September 5.
words/#26-40/tip: 'push back/postpone(연기하다)', 'move up(앞당기다)' 같은 일정 변경 표현과 함께 Part 3·7에 나온다.
It appears in Part 3·7 with schedule-change expressions such as push back/postpone (to delay) and move up (to bring forward).
words/#26-40/q/k: 제작 지연으로 12월로 '연기된(pushed back)' 것은 영화의 개봉일이므로 release date가 정답. 독자층, 표제, 전기는 연기될 수 있는 일정이 아니다.
What was "pushed back" to December because of production delays is the film's opening date, so release date is correct. Readership, headline, and biography aren't schedules that can be delayed.
words/#27-01/exKo: 모든 방문객은 실험실에 있는 동안 직원과 동행해야 한다.
All visitors must be accompanied by a staff member while in the laboratory.
words/#27-01/der/0/m: something that comes with; musical backing
words/#27-01/tip: 타동사이므로 'accompany with'는 틀리고 목적어를 바로 쓴다. 수동태 'be accompanied by(~이 동반되다, ~이 첨부되다)'가 빈출이다.
It is transitive, so accompany with is wrong; the object follows directly. The passive be accompanied by (to come with; to be attached to) is common.
words/#27-01/q/k: 환불 요청서에 영수증이 '첨부되어야' 하므로 'be accompanied by'의 과거분사 accompanied가 정답. accompanying은 능동 진행이라 by와 맞지 않고, accompaniment는 명사, accompany는 원형이다.

The receipt must "be attached" to the refund request, so accompanied, the past participle in be accompanied by, is correct. Accompanying is active and doesn't go with by, accompaniment is a noun, and accompany the base form.
words/#27-02/exKo: The sales team achieved its quarterly target two weeks early.
words/#27-02/tip: goal, target, objective 같은 목표 명사와 짝을 이루는 어휘 문제가 나오며, 명사형 achievement(업적)도 품사 문제로 출제된다.
Vocabulary questions pair it with goal nouns like goal, target, and objective, and the noun form achievement (accomplishment) is also tested in part-of-speech questions.
words/#27-02/q/k: to부정사 뒤 동사원형 자리이므로 achieve가 정답. achievement와 achiever는 명사, achievable은 형용사다.
After the to of an infinitive, you need a base verb, so achieve is correct. Achievement and achiever are nouns, and achievable is an adjective.
words/#27-03/exKo: 옆면의 버튼을 누르면 책상 높이를 조절할 수 있다.
You can adjust the height of the desk by pressing the button on the side.
words/#27-03/tip: 자동사로 쓰일 때는 'adjust to(~에 적응하다)'처럼 전치사 to가 필요하다. 형용사 adjustable('adjustable chairs' 높이 조절 의자)이 품사 문제로 나온다.
When intransitive, it needs to, as in adjust to (to get used to). The adjective adjustable (adjustable chairs: chairs whose height can be changed) appears in part-of-speech questions.
words/#27-03/q/k: 전치사 to와 함께 '~에 적응하다'라는 뜻을 이루는 자동사 adjust가 정답. adopt(채택하다), advise(조언하다), attribute(~의 탓으로 돌리다)는 목적어가 필요한 타동사라 이 자리에 맞지 않는다.

Adjust is an intransitive verb that forms "to get used to" with the preposition to, so it is correct. Adopt (to take up), advise (to give advice), and attribute (to credit to) are transitive verbs that need an object, so they don't fit.
words/#27-04/exKo: 시의회는 내년에 새 재활용 정책을 채택하기로 의결했다.
The city council voted to adopt the new recycling policy next year.
words/#27-04/tip: adapt(적응하다, 각색하다)와 철자를 혼동시키는 어휘 문제가 나오며, policy, plan, approach 같은 명사와 짝을 이룬다.
Vocabulary questions use spelling confusion with adapt (to adjust; to rewrite), and it pairs with nouns like policy, plan, and approach.
words/#27-04/q/k: 제안을 수정 없이(without any changes) '채택하다'라는 뜻이므로 adopt가 정답. adapt는 '(용도에 맞게) 고치다, 적응하다'라 '수정 없이'와 모순되고, adept는 '능숙한'이라는 형용사, adhere는 'adhere to(~을 고수하다)'로 써야 한다.

It means "to accept" the proposal without any changes, so adopt is correct. Adapt means "to modify, adjust," which contradicts "without any changes"; adept is an adjective meaning "skilled"; and adhere must be adhere to (to stick to).
words/#27-05/exKo: 승객은 적어도 두 시간 일찍 공항에 도착하도록 권고된다.
Passengers are advised to arrive at the airport at least two hours early.
words/#27-05/tip: 'be advised to do(~하도록 권고받다)'와 공지문 'Please be advised that ~(~임을 알려 드립니다)'이 빈출이다. 명사 advice는 불가산이라 an advice, advices는 틀린다.

The pattern be advised to do (to be recommended to do) and the notice phrase Please be advised that ~ (please note that ~) are common. The noun advice is uncountable, so an advice and advices are wrong.
words/#27-05/q/k: 'be advised to do(~하도록 권고받다)' 수동태 구조이므로 과거분사 advised가 정답. advice와 advisor는 명사, advisory는 형용사로 to부정사와 연결되지 않는다.

It is the passive structure be advised to do (to be recommended to do), so the past participle advised is correct. Advice and advisor are nouns, and advisory is an adjective, so none connects to the to-infinitive.
words/#27-06/exKo: 도로 공사로 인해 앞으로 2주간 배송 시간에 영향이 있을 수 있다.
The road construction may affect delivery times for the next two weeks.
words/#27-06/tip: affect는 동사, effect는 주로 명사(효과, 영향)로 쓰여 둘을 구분하는 문제가 자주 나온다. 타동사이므로 'affect on'은 틀린다.
Questions often test affect (verb) vs. effect (mostly a noun: result, impact). It is transitive, so affect on is wrong.
words/#27-06/q/k: 항공편이 폭설의 '영향을 받는' 것이므로 affected가 정답. effected는 '(변화를) 초래된', effective는 '효과적인', affection은 '애정'이라 의미가 맞지 않는다.

The flights will "be influenced" by the snowstorm, so affected is correct. Effected means "brought about (a change)," effective means "successful; in force," and affection means "fondness," so none fits.
words/#27-07/exKo: 새 주차 빌딩이 경기장 주변의 혼잡을 완화할 것이다.
The new parking garage should alleviate congestion around the stadium.
words/#27-07/tip: congestion, burden, concern, shortage 같은 부정적 명사를 목적어로 취하며, Part 7에서는 ease, relieve로 바꿔 표현된다.
Its objects are negative nouns like congestion, burden, concern, and shortage, and Part 7 paraphrases it as ease or relieve.
words/#27-07/q/k: 직원을 더 고용하면 업무 부담이 '덜어지므로' alleviate가 정답. elevate(높이다), accelerate(가속하다), appreciate(감사하다, 인정하다)는 workload와 어울려 이런 의미를 만들지 못한다.

Hiring more staff "lightens" the workload, so alleviate is correct. Elevate (to raise), accelerate (to speed up), and appreciate (to value; to be grateful for) don't create this meaning with workload.
words/#27-08/exKo: 매니저는 고객들에게 결함 있는 제품을 무료로 교환해 주겠다고 장담했다.
The manager assured customers that the defective items would be replaced free of charge.
words/#27-08/tip: assure는 사람을 목적어로 취해 'assure + 사람 + that절/of 명사'로 쓰이고, ensure는 사물이나 that절을 바로 목적어로 취한다. 이 차이가 Part 5 단골이다.
Assure takes a person as its object, as in assure + person + that-clause/of + noun, while ensure takes a thing or a that-clause directly. This difference is a Part 5 regular.
words/#27-08/q/k: '사람(the guests) + that절'을 목적어로 취하는 동사는 assure이므로 assured가 정답. ensure와 secure는 사람 목적어 뒤에 that절을 쓰지 않고, insure는 '보험에 들다'라는 뜻이다.

The verb that takes "person (the guests) + that-clause" as its object is assure, so assured is correct. Ensure and secure don't take a that-clause after a person object, and insure means "to cover with insurance."
words/#27-09/exKo: CEO는 회사의 빠른 성장을 충성 고객 덕분으로 돌렸다.
The CEO attributed the company's rapid growth to its loyal customers.
words/#27-09/tip: 'attribute A to B'의 전치사 to와 수동태 'be attributed to(~ 덕분이다, ~ 때문이다)'가 핵심이다. 명사로는 '속성, 자질'이라는 뜻이며 강세가 앞에 온다.
The key points are the preposition to in attribute A to B and the passive be attributed to (to be due to, because of). As a noun it means "quality, feature," with the stress on the first syllable.
words/#27-09/q/k: 'A(매출 감소)를 B(경쟁 심화) 탓으로 돌리다'라는 'attribute A to B' 구조이므로 attribute가 정답. contribute(기여하다), distribute(배분하다), consider(고려하다)는 이 구조로 원인을 나타내지 않는다.

It is the structure attribute A to B: "to blame A (the drop in sales) on B (more competition)," so attribute is correct. Contribute (to help bring about), distribute (to hand out), and consider (to think about) don't express a cause in this structure.
words/#27-10/exKo: The factory will cease operations at the end of the year.
words/#27-10/tip: to부정사와 동명사를 모두 목적어로 취할 수 있으며, Part 7에서는 stop, discontinue로 바꿔 표현된다. 발음이 비슷한 seize(붙잡다)와 혼동하지 말 것.
It can take both a to-infinitive and a gerund as its object, and Part 7 paraphrases it as stop or discontinue. Don't confuse it with the similar-sounding seize (to grab).
words/#27-10/q/k: 수요가 낮아 생산을 '중단한다'는 흐름이므로 cease가 정답. seize는 '붙잡다'라는 발음 함정이고, resume(재개하다)은 수요 감소와 논리가 맞지 않으며, cite는 '인용하다'다.
Demand is low, so the company will "stop" production: cease is correct. Seize (to grab) is a sound-alike trap, resume (to start again) contradicts low demand, and cite means "to quote."
words/#27-11/exKo: 관리자는 새 휴가 정책을 명확히 설명하기 위해 이메일을 보냈다.
The manager sent an e-mail to clarify the new vacation policy.
words/#27-11/tip: 명사형 clarification('ask for clarification' 설명을 요청하다)이 품사 문제로 자주 나오며, Part 7에서는 explain으로 바꿔 표현된다.
The noun form clarification (ask for clarification: to ask for an explanation) often appears in part-of-speech questions, and Part 7 paraphrases it as explain.
words/#27-11/q/k: to부정사 뒤 동사원형 자리이므로 clarify가 정답. clarification과 clarity는 명사, clarified는 과거(분사)다.
After the to of an infinitive, you need a base verb, so clarify is correct. Clarification and clarity are nouns, and clarified is a past tense or past participle.
words/#27-12/exKo: Construction of the new terminal will commence in early spring.
words/#27-12/tip: begin, start의 격식체로 공지문에 자주 쓰인다. 명사 commencement는 '시작' 외에 미국에서 '졸업식'을 뜻한다.
A formal word for begin or start, common in notices. The noun commencement means "start" but in the U.S. also "graduation ceremony."
words/#27-12/q/k: 탑승이 예정 출발 시각 30분 전에 '시작된다'는 뜻이므로 commence가 정답. commend(칭찬하다), comment(논평하다), commute(통근하다)는 철자가 비슷한 함정이다.
Boarding "begins" 30 minutes before departure, so commence is correct. Commend (to praise), comment (to remark), and commute (to travel to work) are look-alike traps.
words/#27-13/exKo: 샤 씨는 대량 구매 할인을 제공하는 공급업체 목록을 작성하고 있다.
Mr. Shah is compiling a list of suppliers that offer bulk discounts.
words/#27-13/tip: list, data, report, statistics 같은 목적어와 함께 쓰이며, Part 7에서는 'put together'로 바꿔 표현된다.
Used with objects like list, data, report, and statistics; Part 7 paraphrases it as put together.
words/#27-13/q/k: 연례 보고서를 위해 자료를 '수집하는' 데 2주를 보낸 것이므로 compiling이 정답. complying(준수하는), complaining(불평하는), competing(경쟁하는)은 data를 목적어로 취하지 않는다.

The assistant spent two weeks "collecting" data for the yearly report, so compiling is correct. Complying (obeying), complaining (expressing dissatisfaction), and competing (trying to win) don't take data as an object.
words/#27-14/m/0: consist of, be made up of
words/#27-14/exKo: 위원회는 여러 부서에서 온 12명의 위원으로 구성된다.
The committee comprises twelve members from different departments.
words/#27-14/tip: comprise는 타동사라 전치사 없이 바로 목적어를 취하며(comprise A), 'be comprised of'도 쓰인다. 'consist of'와 바꿔 쓰는 문제가 나온다.
Comprise is transitive and takes an object directly without a preposition (comprise A), and be comprised of is also used. Questions ask you to swap it with consist of.
words/#27-14/q/k: 전치사 없이 구성원을 목적어로 취해 '~로 구성되다'를 뜻하는 comprises가 정답. consists는 of가 필요하고, composes는 'is composed of'로 써야 하며, constitutes는 부분이 전체를 '구성하다'라는 뜻이라 방향이 반대다.

Comprises takes the members directly as its object without a preposition, meaning "is made up of," so it is correct. Consists needs of, composes must be is composed of, and constitutes means a part "makes up" the whole, which is the opposite direction.
words/#27-15/exKo: 그 교육 과정은 온라인 강좌 세 개와 최종 시험으로 구성된다.
The training program consists of three online modules and a final exam.
words/#27-15/tip: 자동사구이므로 수동태(be consisted of)로 쓸 수 없다. be composed of, be made up of, comprise와 같은 의미로 패러프레이징된다.
It is an intransitive phrase, so it can't be passive (be consisted of). It is paraphrased with the same meaning as be composed of, be made up of, and comprise.
words/#27-15/q/k: 빈칸 뒤 전치사 of와 짝을 이루는 자동사는 consist뿐이므로 consists가 정답. comprises, includes, contains는 타동사라 of 없이 목적어를 바로 취한다.

Consist is the only intransitive verb that pairs with the preposition of after the blank, so consists is correct. The verbs comprises, includes, and contains are transitive and take an object directly without of.
words/#27-16/exKo: 발표자는 복잡한 재무 정보를 전달하기 위해 간단한 도표를 사용했다.
The speaker used simple charts to convey complex financial information.
words/#27-16/tip: 'convey A to B(A를 B에게 전달하다)'로 쓰이며, Part 7에서는 communicate나 express로 바꿔 표현된다. Part 1의 conveyor belt(컨베이어 벨트)도 같은 어원이다.
Used as convey A to B (to pass A on to B); Part 7 paraphrases it as communicate or express. The conveyor belt in Part 1 comes from the same root.
words/#27-16/q/k: 감사의 뜻을 '전하다'라는 뜻이므로 convey가 정답. convert(전환하다), convene(소집하다), conceive(구상하다)는 thanks를 목적어로 취하지 않는다.
It means "to express" thanks, so convey is correct. Convert (to change), convene (to call together), and conceive (to come up with) don't take thanks as an object.
words/#27-17/exKo: 사용자는 가장 자주 쓰는 보고서가 표시되도록 대시보드를 맞춤 설정할 수 있다.
Users can customize the dashboard to display the reports they use most.
words/#27-17/tip: 과거분사형 형용사 customized('customized service' 맞춤 서비스)가 품사 문제로 나오며, Part 7에서는 tailor로 바꿔 표현된다.
The past-participle adjective customized (customized service: tailored service) appears in part-of-speech questions, and Part 7 paraphrases it as tailor.
words/#27-17/q/k: 조동사 can 뒤 동사원형 자리이므로 customize가 정답. customer(고객)와 customs(세관)는 명사, customary(관례적인)는 형용사다.
After the modal can, you need a base verb, so customize is correct. Customer (buyer) and customs (border control) are nouns, and customary (usual) is an adjective.
words/#27-18/exKo: 검사관은 그 건물이 입주하기에 안전하다고 판단했다.
The inspector deemed the building safe for occupancy.
words/#27-18/tip: 5형식 동사로 'deem + 목적어 + 형용사/명사' 구조를 취하며, 수동태 'be deemed (to be) + 형용사'가 Part 5에 나온다.
It takes the structure deem + object + adjective/noun, and the passive be deemed (to be) + adjective appears in Part 5.
words/#27-18/q/k: 'be deemed + 형용사(~하다고 여겨지다)' 구조이므로 deemed가 정답. regarded, thought of, seen은 'be regarded as'처럼 as가 있어야 형용사 보어를 취할 수 있다.
It is the structure be deemed + adjective (to be considered ~), so deemed is correct. The forms regarded, thought of, and seen need as to take an adjective complement, as in be regarded as.
words/#27-19/exKo: The lounge on the second floor has been designated as a quiet work area.
words/#27-19/tip: 'designated parking area(지정 주차 구역)'처럼 과거분사가 명사를 수식하는 형태가 빈출이며, 'designate A as B' 구조도 함께 출제된다.
A past participle describing a noun, as in designated parking area (assigned parking area), is common, and the structure designate A as B is also tested.
words/#27-19/q/k: 명사 areas를 수식하여 '지정된 구역'을 뜻하는 과거분사 designated가 정답. designing은 '설계하는', designate는 동사원형, designation은 명사라 맞지 않는다.
The past participle designated describes the noun areas to mean "assigned areas," so it is correct. Designing means "creating plans," designate is the base form, and designation is a noun.
words/#27-20/exKo: 어떤 기능이 가장 인기 있는지 알아내기 위해 고객 설문 조사가 실시된다.
A customer survey will be conducted to determine which features are most popular.
words/#27-20/tip: 'determine the cause(원인을 알아내다)'처럼 '알아내다'의 뜻이 Part 7 동의어 문제로 나온다. 'be determined to do(~하기로 결심하다)'도 빈출이다.
The meaning "to find out," as in determine the cause (to find out the cause), appears in Part 7 synonym questions. The pattern be determined to do (to be resolved to do) is also common.
words/#27-20/q/k: to부정사 뒤 동사원형 자리이므로 determine이 정답. determination은 명사, determined는 과거(분사)/형용사, determining은 동명사/현재분사다.
After the to of an infinitive, you need a base verb, so determine is correct. Determination is a noun, determined a past tense/participle or adjective, and determining a gerund or present participle.
words/#27-21/exKo: 웡 씨는 경력의 대부분을 환자 치료 개선에 바쳤다.
Ms. Wong devoted most of her career to improving patient care.
words/#27-21/tip: 'devote A to B'의 to는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사가 온다(devote time to improving). 수동태 'be devoted to(~에 할애되다)'도 빈출이다.
The to in devote A to B is a preposition, so a gerund follows (devote time to improving). The passive be devoted to (to be set aside for) is also common.
words/#27-21/q/k: 회의 둘째 날이 워크숍에 '할애된다'는 뜻으로 'be devoted to'를 이루는 devoted가 정답. provided는 '제공되다'라 to workshops와 의미가 맞지 않고, involved는 in, engaged는 in과 짝을 이룬다.
The conference's second day is "set aside for" workshops, forming be devoted to, so devoted is correct. Provided ("supplied") doesn't fit with to workshops, and involved and engaged pair with in.
words/#27-22/exKo: 정전으로 몇 시간 동안 공장 생산에 차질이 생겼다.
The power outage disrupted production at the plant for several hours.
words/#27-22/tip: 명사 disruption('service disruption' 서비스 중단)이 공지 지문에 자주 나오며, 'minimize disruption(지장을 최소화하다)' 표현이 빈출이다.
The noun disruption (service disruption: interruption of service) often appears in notices, and minimize disruption (to keep interruptions to a minimum) is common.
words/#27-22/q/k: 'so as not to + 동사원형' 구조이므로 disrupt가 정답. disruption은 명사, disruptive는 형용사, disruptively는 부사다.
The structure is so as not to + base verb, so disrupt is correct. Disruption is a noun, disruptive an adjective, and disruptively an adverb.
words/#27-23/exKo: 일부 사용자는 업데이트 후 로그인하려다가 문제를 겪었다.
Some users encountered problems when they tried to log in after the update.
words/#27-23/tip: 타동사이므로 'encounter with'가 아니라 바로 목적어를 쓴다. problem, difficulty, delay 같은 명사와 함께 쓰이며, Part 7에서 experience로 바꿔 표현된다.
It is transitive, so use the object directly, not encounter with. It is used with nouns like problem, difficulty, and delay, and Part 7 paraphrases it as experience.
words/#27-23/q/k: 결제 시스템에서 어려움을 '겪는' 고객이므로 encounter가 정답. encourage(격려하다), enclose(동봉하다), entail(수반하다)은 difficulties를 목적어로 이 의미를 만들지 못한다.

These are customers who "run into" difficulties with the payment system, so encounter is correct. Encourage (to support), enclose (to include in an envelope), and entail (to involve) don't create this meaning with difficulties.
words/#27-24/exKo: 감독관은 모든 주문이 제때 발송되도록 하나하나 확인한다.
The supervisor checks every order to ensure that it is shipped on time.
words/#27-24/tip: ensure는 that절이나 사물 명사를 바로 목적어로 취하고, assure는 사람 목적어를 취한다(assure + 사람 + that). 철자가 비슷한 insure(보험에 들다)도 함정으로 나온다.

Ensure takes a that-clause or a thing noun directly as its object, while assure takes a person as its object (assure + person + that). The look-alike insure (to cover with insurance) also appears as a trap.
words/#27-24/q/k: 사람 목적어 없이 that절을 바로 취해 '반드시 ~하게 하다'를 뜻하는 ensure가 정답. remind, reassure, notify는 모두 'remind + 사람 + that'처럼 사람 목적어가 먼저 와야 한다.
Ensure takes a that-clause directly without a person object to mean "make sure," so it is correct. The verbs remind, reassure, and notify all need a person object first, as in remind + person + that.
words/#27-25/exKo: 이 쿠폰을 소지한 사람은 구매 시 음료 한 잔을 무료로 받을 수 있다.
This coupon entitles the holder to a free drink with any purchase.
words/#27-25/tip: 'be entitled to + 명사/동사원형(~할 자격이 있다)'이 빈출이며, 'a lecture entitled ~(~라는 제목의 강연)'처럼 '제목을 붙이다'의 뜻도 나온다.
The pattern be entitled to + noun/base verb (to have the right to) is common, and the meaning "to give a title to" also appears, as in a lecture entitled ~ (a lecture called ~).
words/#27-25/q/k: 'be entitled to + 명사(~을 받을 자격이 있다)'이므로 entitled가 정답. eligible은 'eligible for + 명사'로 쓰고, qualified와 allowed는 'to + 명사' 형태로 혜택을 받을 자격을 나타내지 않는다.

It is be entitled to + noun (to have the right to receive), so entitled is correct. Eligible is used as eligible for + noun, and qualified and allowed don't express the right to a benefit with to + noun.
words/#27-26/exKo: 모든 회의실에는 프로젝터와 화상 회의 시스템이 갖춰져 있다.
All meeting rooms are equipped with projectors and video conferencing systems.
words/#27-26/tip: 'be equipped with(~을 갖추다)'의 전치사 with가 핵심이며, 명사 equipment는 불가산이라 an equipment, equipments는 틀린다.
The key is the preposition with in be equipped with (to have, to be fitted with). The noun equipment is uncountable, so an equipment and equipments are wrong.
words/#27-26/q/k: 'be equipped with(~을 갖추고 있다)' 수동태 구조이므로 과거분사 equipped가 정답. equipment는 명사, equipping은 능동 진행, equips는 be동사 뒤에 올 수 없다.

It is the passive structure be equipped with (to be fitted with), so the past participle equipped is correct. Equipment is a noun, equipping is active progressive, and equips can't follow the be verb.
words/#27-27/exKo: 새 소프트웨어는 서울과 런던 사무소 간의 의사소통을 원활하게 해 줄 것이다.
The new software will facilitate communication between our offices in Seoul and London.
words/#27-27/tip: 사람이 아닌 일·과정을 목적어로 취한다(facilitate the process). 'help + 사람 + do'와 혼동시키는 문제가 나오며, 사람명사 facilitator(진행자)도 출제된다.
It takes a task or process as its object, not a person (facilitate the process). Questions use confusion with help + person + do, and the person noun facilitator (session leader) is also tested.
words/#27-27/q/k: to부정사 뒤 동사원형 자리이므로 facilitate가 정답. facility(시설), facilitator(진행자), facilitation(촉진)은 모두 명사다.
After the to of an infinitive, you need a base verb, so facilitate is correct. Facility (building, equipment), facilitator (session leader), and facilitation (making easier) are all nouns.
words/#27-28/exKo: 팀워크 향상 행사는 직원들 사이에 신뢰감을 키우는 데 도움이 된다.
Team-building events help foster a sense of trust among employees.
words/#27-28/tip: cooperation, growth, innovation, relationship 같은 긍정적 명사를 목적어로 취하며, Part 7에서는 encourage, promote로 바꿔 표현된다.
It takes positive nouns like cooperation, growth, innovation, and relationship as objects, and Part 7 paraphrases it as encourage or promote.
words/#27-28/q/k: 선후배 직원 간에 더 가까운 관계를 '증진하다'라는 뜻이므로 foster가 정답. fasten(고정하다), forecast(예측하다), forbid(금지하다)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
It means "to build" closer relationships between senior and junior staff, so foster is correct. Fasten (to attach firmly), forecast (to predict), and forbid (to prohibit) don't fit.
words/#27-29/exKo: 새 제품군은 작년에 300만 달러가 넘는 매출을 올렸다.
The new product line generated over $3 million in revenue last year.
words/#27-29/tip: revenue, profit, sales, interest 같은 목적어와 짝을 이루는 어휘 문제가 나온다. 'generate interest(관심을 끌다)'도 Part 7에서 자주 쓰인다.
Vocabulary questions pair it with objects like revenue, profit, sales, and interest. Generate interest (to attract attention) is also common in Part 7.
words/#27-29/q/k: 조동사 will 뒤 동사원형 자리이고 '전기를 생산하다(generate electricity)'라는 뜻이므로 generate가 정답. generation과 generator는 명사, generous는 '관대한'이라는 형용사다.

After the modal will, you need a base verb, and it means "to produce electricity" (generate electricity), so generate is correct. Generation and generator are nouns, and generous is an adjective meaning "giving, kind."
words/#27-30/exKo: 안 씨는 도쿄 사무소의 일자리 제안을 망설임 없이 받아들였다.
Ms. Ahn did not hesitate to accept the job offer from the Tokyo office.
words/#27-30/tip: 이메일 맺음말 'Please do not hesitate to contact me'가 Part 6·7 단골이며, to부정사를 취한다는 점이 출제된다. 명사구 'without hesitation(망설임 없이)'도 나온다.

The email closing Please do not hesitate to contact me is a Part 6·7 regular, and the fact that it takes a to-infinitive is tested. The noun phrase without hesitation (immediately, without doubt) also appears.
words/#27-30/q/k: 조동사 should not 뒤 동사원형 자리이므로 hesitate가 정답. hesitation은 명사, hesitant는 형용사, hesitantly는 부사다.
After the modal should not, you need a base verb, so hesitate is correct. Hesitation is a noun, hesitant an adjective, and hesitantly an adverb.
words/#27-31/exKo: 회계 감사를 통해 운영비를 줄일 수 있는 몇 가지 방법을 찾아냈다.
The audit helped identify several ways to reduce operating costs.
words/#27-31/tip: 'identify the cause(원인을 찾아내다)'처럼 '파악하다'의 뜻이 Part 7 동의어 문제로 나오며, 명사 identification(신분증)과의 품사 구분이 출제된다.
The meaning "to pinpoint," as in identify the cause (to find the cause), appears in Part 7 synonym questions, and questions test it against the noun identification (ID document).
words/#27-31/q/k: to부정사 뒤 동사원형 자리이므로 identify가 정답. identity(신원)와 identification(확인)은 명사, identical(동일한)은 형용사다.
After the to of an infinitive, you need a base verb, so identify is correct. Identity (who someone is) and identification (recognition) are nouns, and identical (exactly the same) is an adjective.
words/#27-32/exKo: 초기 판매 수치는 신모델이 예상보다 인기가 높다는 것을 보여 준다.
Early sales figures indicate that the new model is more popular than expected.
words/#27-32/tip: Part 7 질문 'What is indicated about ~?(~에 대해 언급된 것은?)'의 핵심 동사다. 'as indicated in the brochure(안내 책자에 명시된 대로)'도 빈출이다.
It is the key verb in the Part 7 question What is indicated about ~? (What is stated about ~?). The phrase as indicated in the brochure (as stated in the brochure) is also common.
words/#27-32/q/k: Please 뒤 명령문의 동사원형 자리이므로 indicate가 정답. indication과 indicator는 명사, indicative는 형용사다.
After Please, the blank is the base verb of an imperative, so indicate is correct. Indication and indicator are nouns, and indicative is an adjective.
words/#27-33/exKo: 방문객은 경비실에서 주차 허가증을 받아야 한다.
Visitors must obtain a parking permit from the security office.
words/#27-33/tip: permission, approval, permit, information 같은 목적어와 쓰이며, 'obtain A from B(B에게서 A를 얻다)'의 전치사 from이 함께 나온다.
Its objects are words like permission, approval, permit, and information, often with the preposition from: obtain A from B (get A from B).
words/#27-33/q/k: 상사로부터 승인을 '받아야' 한다는 뜻이므로 obtain이 정답. contain(포함하다), retain(보유하다), maintain(유지하다)은 'approval from ~'과 어울려 이런 의미를 만들지 못한다.

The sentence means employees must "get" approval from their supervisor, so obtain is correct. Contain (hold inside), retain (keep), and maintain (keep up) don't make this meaning with "approval from ~".
words/#27-34/m/1: to carry on with (a career or studies)
words/#27-34/exKo: 임 씨는 경제학 석사 학위를 취득하기 위해 회사를 그만두었다.
Ms. Lim left the company to pursue a master's degree in economics.
words/#27-34/der/0/m: the act of seeking or striving for
words/#27-34/tip: career, degree, goal, opportunity를 목적어로 취하며, 명사 pursuit('in pursuit of' ~을 추구하여)도 Part 5에 나온다.
Its objects include career, degree, goal, and opportunity. The noun pursuit (in pursuit of = seeking) also appears in Part 5.
words/#27-34/q/k: 마케팅 분야의 경력을 '추구하다'라는 뜻이므로 pursue가 정답. persuade(설득하다), purchase(구매하다)는 의미가 맞지 않고, pursuit는 명사다.
The meaning is to "go after" a career in marketing, so pursue is correct. Persuade (convince) and purchase (buy) don't fit the meaning, and pursuit is a noun.
words/#27-35/exKo: 가격 인상은 원자재 비용 상승을 반영한다.
The price increase reflects the rising cost of raw materials.
words/#27-35/tip: 'reflect the changes(변경 사항을 반영하다)'처럼 수정 공지에 자주 쓰이며, Part 1에서는 'be reflected in the water(물에 비치다)'로 나온다.
It is common in update notices, as in reflect the changes (include or show the changes). In Part 1 it appears as be reflected in the water (mirrored on the water).
words/#27-35/q/k: 조동사 will 뒤 동사원형 자리이므로 reflect가 정답. reflection은 명사, reflective는 형용사, reflectively는 부사다.
After the modal will, a base verb is needed, so reflect is correct. Reflection is a noun, reflective an adjective, and reflectively an adverb.
words/#27-36/m/0: to avoid (doing), to hold back from
words/#27-36/exKo: 관객은 공연 중에 휴대 전화 사용을 삼가 달라는 요청을 받는다.
Audience members are asked to refrain from using mobile phones during the performance.
words/#27-36/tip: from은 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사가 온다(refrain from taking). 공지문의 'Please refrain from ~' 표현이 Part 4·7 단골이다.
From is a preposition, so a gerund follows (refrain from taking). The notice phrase "Please refrain from ~" is a Part 4 and Part 7 regular.
words/#27-36/mq/k: 목적어 없이 바로 from을 취하는 자동사 refrain이 정답. prevent, prohibit, restrict는 타동사라 'prevent + 목적어 + from -ing'처럼 목적어가 먼저 와야 한다.

Refrain is intransitive and takes from directly with no object, so it is correct. The verbs prevent, prohibit, and restrict are transitive, so the object must come first, as in "prevent + object + from -ing".
words/#27-37/exKo: 기술자들은 강철 지지대로 오래된 다리를 보강했다.
The engineers reinforced the old bridge with steel supports.
words/#27-37/tip: 물리적 보강(reinforce a wall)과 추상적 강화(reinforce a brand image) 모두에 쓰이며, Part 7에서 strengthen으로 바꿔 표현된다.
It is used for physical support (reinforce a wall) and for abstract strengthening (reinforce a brand image). In Part 7 it is paraphrased as strengthen.
words/#27-37/q/k: 친환경 브랜드라는 이미지를 '강화하다'라는 뜻이므로 reinforce가 정답. reimburse(상환하다), relocate(이전하다), refund(환불하다)는 image와 어울리지 않는다.
The meaning is to "strengthen" the company's image as an eco-friendly brand, so reinforce is correct. Reimburse (pay back), relocate (move), and refund (give money back) don't go with image.
words/#27-38/exKo: 시는 자전거 전용 도로 설치안에 대해 시민 의견을 구하고 있다.
The city is soliciting public comments on the proposed bike lanes.
words/#27-38/tip: feedback, input, donations, proposals를 목적어로 취하며, Part 7에서 request, ask for로 바꿔 표현된다. 'No soliciting(판매·권유 금지)' 표지로도 나온다.
Its objects include feedback, input, donations, and proposals; in Part 7 it is paraphrased as request or ask for. It also appears on "No soliciting" signs (no selling or canvassing).
words/#27-38/q/k: 직원들에게 제안을 '구하고' 있다는 뜻이므로 soliciting이 정답. resolving(해결하는), consoling(위로하는), isolating(고립시키는)은 suggestions from ~과 의미가 맞지 않는다.
The team is "asking for" suggestions from employees, so soliciting is correct. Resolving (settling), consoling (comforting), and isolating (separating) don't fit with "suggestions from ~".
words/#27-39/m/0: to go through, to experience (a change, an inspection, etc.)
words/#27-39/exKo: 그 사무실 건물은 현재 대규모 보수 공사 중이다.
The office building is currently undergoing major renovations.
words/#27-39/tip: renovation, inspection, training, changes 같은 명사를 목적어로 취하는 타동사다. 불규칙 변화(undergo-underwent-undergone)와 진행형 'be undergoing'이 자주 출제된다.
It is a transitive verb that takes nouns like renovation, inspection, training, and changes. Its irregular forms (undergo-underwent-undergone) and the progressive be undergoing are often tested.
words/#27-39/q/k: 기계가 안전 점검을 '받아야' 하므로 undergo가 정답. undertake는 사람이 일을 '맡다'라는 뜻이라 기계 주어와 맞지 않고, underline(강조하다), underestimate(과소평가하다)도 의미가 맞지 않는다.

The machinery must "go through" a safety inspection, so undergo is correct. Undertake means a person takes on a task, so it doesn't fit a machine as subject, and underline (stress) and underestimate (judge too low) don't fit the meaning either.
words/#27-40/m/0: to use, to make use of
words/#27-40/exKo: 그 회사는 주 창고에 전력을 공급하기 위해 태양광 패널을 활용한다.
The company utilizes solar panels to power its main warehouse.
words/#27-40/tip: use의 격식 표현으로 resources, space, technology 같은 목적어와 쓰인다. 명사 utility는 'utility bills(공과금)'의 뜻으로 따로 출제된다.
It is a formal version of use, with objects like resources, space, and technology. The noun utility is tested separately in utility bills (charges for power, water, gas).
words/#27-40/q/k: to부정사 뒤 동사원형 자리이므로 utilize가 정답. utility와 utilization은 명사, utilitarian은 '실용적인'이라는 형용사다.
After the to of the infinitive, a base verb is needed, so utilize is correct. Utility and utilization are nouns, and utilitarian is an adjective meaning "practical".
words/#28-01/exKo: 그 창고에는 새로 들어온 화물을 보관할 충분한 공간이 없다.
The warehouse does not have adequate space to store the new shipment.
words/#28-01/tip: 명사 앞 형용사 자리에는 adequate, 동사·과거분사를 꾸밀 때는 adequately(adequately trained)를 쓴다.
Use adequate before a noun and adequately to modify a verb or past participle (adequately trained).
words/#28-01/q/k: 명사 parking을 앞에서 꾸미는 형용사 자리이므로 adequate가 정답. adequately는 부사, adequacy는 명사라 명사를 수식할 수 없다.
The blank modifies the noun parking, so it needs an adjective: adequate. Adequately is an adverb and adequacy is a noun, so they can't modify a noun.
words/#28-02/exKo: 할인은 우리 웹사이트를 통해 접수된 주문에만 적용된다.
The discount is applicable only to orders placed through our website.
words/#28-02/der/0/m: to use or put into effect; to request formally (a job, etc.)
words/#28-02/tip: be applicable to(~에 적용되다)로 전치사 to와 짝을 이룬다. 양식·약관의 where applicable(해당되는 경우)도 자주 보인다.
It pairs with to: be applicable to (apply to). Where applicable (if relevant) is also common on forms and in terms and conditions.
words/#28-02/q/k: '정책이 ~에게 적용된다'는 be applicable to가 정답. eligible은 for나 to부정사, capable과 aware는 of와 함께 쓰므로 to + 명사 앞에 올 수 없다.
"A policy applies to someone" is be applicable to, so applicable is correct. Eligible goes with for or a to-infinitive, and capable and aware go with of, so they can't come before to + noun.
words/#28-03/exKo: 그 프로젝트에 추가 인력이 필요하다는 것이 곧 분명해졌다.
It soon became apparent that the project would need additional staff.
words/#28-03/tip: become, seem 뒤 보어 자리에는 형용사 apparent가 온다. 부사 apparently는 '보아하니'라는 뜻으로 문장 전체를 수식한다.
After become or seem, the complement is the adjective apparent. The adverb apparently means "it seems" and modifies the whole sentence.
words/#28-03/q/k: 2형식 동사 became 뒤 보어 자리이므로 형용사 apparent가 정답. 부사 apparently는 보어가 될 수 없다.
After the linking verb became, a complement is needed, so the adjective apparent is correct. The adverb apparently can't be a complement.
words/#28-04/exKo: 모든 방문객은 공장 작업장에서 적절한 안전 장비를 착용해야 한다.
All visitors must wear appropriate safety gear on the factory floor.
words/#28-04/tip: appropriate for + 명사 / appropriate to do 형태로 쓰인다. 'the most ------- + 명사' 자리에는 형용사가 들어가야 한다.
It is used as appropriate for + noun and appropriate to do. In "the most ------- + noun", an adjective is needed.
words/#28-04/q/k: 최상급 the most와 명사 course 사이의 형용사 자리이므로 appropriate가 정답. appropriately는 부사, appropriateness와 appropriation은 명사다.
The blank is between the superlative the most and the noun course, so it needs an adjective: appropriate. Appropriately is an adverb, and appropriateness and appropriation are nouns.
words/#28-05/exKo: 모든 직원은 월요일 전에 새 보안 절차를 숙지하고 있어야 한다.
All staff should be aware of the new security procedures before Monday.
words/#28-05/tip: be aware of + 명사 / be aware that + 절로 쓴다. 공지문의 'Please be aware that ~(~을 유의해 주세요)'은 듣기와 Part 7에 자주 나온다.
Use be aware of + noun or be aware that + clause. The notice phrase "Please be aware that ~" (please note that ~) is common in listening and Part 7.
words/#28-05/q/k: 뒤의 전치사 of와 짝을 이루는 be aware of가 정답. familiar는 with, accustomed는 to, eligible은 for와 쓴다.
The phrase be aware of matches the following of, so aware is correct. Familiar goes with with, accustomed with to, and eligible with for.
words/#28-06/exKo: 열차 안에서는 목소리를 낮춰 다른 승객을 배려해 주기 바란다.
Please be considerate of other passengers by keeping your voice down on the train.
words/#28-06/der/0/m: to think about; to take into account
words/#28-06/tip: considerate(사려 깊은)와 considerable(상당한, 양이 많은)을 구분하는 문제가 대표적이다. be considerate of + 사람 형태로 쓴다.
A classic question contrasts considerate (thoughtful) and considerable (large in amount). It is used as be considerate of + person.
words/#28-06/q/k: 타인을 '배려하라'는 의미이므로 considerate가 정답. considerable은 '(양·정도가) 상당한'이라는 뜻으로 사람의 태도를 나타내지 않는다.
The meaning is "be thoughtful" toward others, so considerate is correct. Considerable means "large (in amount or degree)" and doesn't describe a person's attitude.
words/#28-07/exKo: 고객 의견은 새 앱의 설계에 결정적인 역할을 했다.
Customer feedback played a crucial role in the design of the new app.
words/#28-07/tip: It is crucial that + 주어 + (should) 동사원형 구문이 나온다. essential, imperative, vital과 같은 '필수·중요' 형용사가 이 구문을 이끈다.
It appears in It is crucial that + subject + (should) base verb. Adjectives of necessity or importance like essential, imperative, and vital lead this pattern.
words/#28-07/q/k: that절의 동사가 원형 be이므로 필요·중요를 나타내는 crucial이 정답. possible, probable, likely는 that절에 동사원형을 쓰는 구문을 이끌지 않는다.

The verb in the that-clause is the base form be, so crucial, which expresses necessity or importance, is correct. The adjectives possible, probable, and likely don't take a that-clause with a base verb.
words/#28-08/exKo: 신입 사원이 주간 회의에서 자기소개를 하는 것이 관례다.
It is customary for new employees to introduce themselves at the weekly meeting.
words/#28-08/col/0/e: it is customary (for 사람) to do
it is customary (for someone) to do
words/#28-08/col/0/k: it is customary (for 사람) to do
words/#28-08/tip: 가주어 구문 It is customary (for 사람) to do로 자주 쓰인다. custom(관습), customs(세관), customer(고객)와 형태를 혼동하지 않도록 한다.
It is often used in the dummy-subject pattern It is customary (for someone) to do. Don't confuse its form with custom (tradition), customs (border control), and customer (buyer).
words/#28-08/q/k: be동사 is 뒤 보어 자리이므로 형용사 customary가 정답. customer는 사람명사, customize는 동사, customarily는 부사다.
After the be verb is, a complement is needed, so the adjective customary is correct. Customer is a person noun, customize a verb, and customarily an adverb.
words/#28-09/exKo: 우리는 고객에게 서류를 배달해 줄 믿을 만한 택배 업체가 필요하다.
We need a dependable courier service to deliver documents to our clients.
words/#28-09/tip: dependable(믿을 만한)과 dependent(의존하는, be dependent on)를 구분해야 한다. dependable = reliable 패러프레이징이 Part 7에 나온다.
Distinguish dependable (reliable) from dependent (relying on, be dependent on). The paraphrase dependable = reliable appears in Part 7.
words/#28-09/q/k: 승진의 이유가 되는 긍정적 자질이므로 '믿을 만한' dependable이 정답. dependent는 '의존하는'이라는 뜻으로 문맥에 맞지 않고, depending과 dependence는 형용사 자리에 올 수 없다.

The blank describes a positive quality that led to her promotion, so dependable (reliable) is correct. Dependent means "relying on others" and doesn't fit, and depending and dependence can't fill an adjective slot.
words/#28-10/exKo: 우리 회사는 12개국 이상에서 다양한 고객층에게 서비스를 제공한다.
Our firm serves a diverse group of clients in more than 12 countries.
words/#28-10/der/1/m: to branch out; to vary (a business)
words/#28-10/tip: a diverse range of는 a wide range of와 같은 뜻이다. 명사 diversity, 동사 diversify(사업을 다각화하다)를 구분하는 품사 문제가 나온다.
The phrase a diverse range of means the same as a wide range of. Part-of-speech questions test the noun diversity and the verb diversify (to branch out into new business).
words/#28-10/q/k: 관사 a와 명사 range 사이의 형용사 자리이므로 diverse가 정답. diversity는 명사, diversify는 동사, diversely는 부사다.
The blank is between the article a and the noun range, so it needs an adjective: diverse. Diversity is a noun, diversify a verb, and diversely an adverb.
words/#28-11/exKo: 새로 온 인턴들은 각 부서가 어떻게 운영되는지 몹시 배우고 싶어 한다.
The new interns are eager to learn how each department operates.
words/#28-11/tip: be eager to + 동사원형 / be eager for + 명사로 쓴다. 'eagerly awaited(몹시 기다려지는)'처럼 부사형도 출제된다.
Use be eager to + base verb or be eager for + noun. The adverb also appears, as in eagerly awaited (much looked forward to).
words/#28-11/q/k: be동사 are 뒤 보어 자리이므로 형용사 eager가 정답. eagerness는 명사, eagerly와 more eagerly는 부사라 보어가 될 수 없다.
After the be verb are, a complement is needed, so the adjective eager is correct. Eagerness is a noun, and eagerly and more eagerly are adverbs, so they can't be complements.
words/#28-12/exKo: 모든 해외 출장에는 유효한 여권이 필수다.
A valid passport is essential for all international business trips.
words/#28-12/tip: essential to/for + 명사, It is essential that + 주어 + (should) 동사원형 구문이 자주 나온다. 명사 essentials는 '필수품'이다.
Essential to/for + noun and It is essential that + subject + (should) base verb are common. The plural noun essentials means "necessary items".
words/#28-12/q/k: be동사 is 뒤 보어 자리에서 '~에 필수적인'을 뜻하는 형용사 essential이 정답. essence와 essentials는 명사, essentially는 부사다.
After the be verb is, the complement meaning "necessary for ~" is the adjective essential. Essence and essentials are nouns, and essentially is an adverb.
words/#28-13/exKo: 그 호텔은 탁월한 고객 서비스로 상을 받았다.
The hotel received an award for its exceptional customer service.
words/#28-13/tip: 토익에서는 '예외적인'보다 '뛰어난'의 뜻으로 주로 쓰인다. 'in exceptional circumstances(예외적인 경우에)'와 부사 exceptionally(유난히)도 알아 둔다.
On the TOEIC it mostly means "outstanding" rather than "unusual". Also learn in exceptional circumstances (in special cases) and the adverb exceptionally (unusually).
words/#28-13/q/k: 명사 circumstances를 꾸미는 형용사 자리이므로 exceptional이 정답. exception은 명사, exceptionally는 부사라 명사를 수식할 수 없다.
The blank modifies the noun circumstances, so it needs an adjective: exceptional. Exception is a noun and exceptionally is an adverb, so they can't modify a noun.
words/#28-14/exKo: 그 회사는 어린 자녀가 있는 직원에게 유연 근무 시간제를 제공한다.
The company offers flexible working hours to employees with young children.
words/#28-14/tip: flexible hours/schedule은 채용 공고와 사내 공지에 자주 나온다. 명사 flexibility는 불가산명사다.
Flexible hours/schedule is common in job ads and company notices. The noun flexibility is uncountable.
words/#28-14/q/k: 관사 a와 명사 schedule 사이의 형용사 자리이므로 flexible이 정답. flexibility는 명사, flexibly는 부사다.
The blank is between the article a and the noun schedule, so it needs an adjective: flexible. Flexibility is a noun and flexibly is an adverb.
words/#28-15/exKo: 모든 승객은 이륙하는 동안 반드시 안전벨트를 매고 있어야 한다.
It is imperative that all passengers keep their seat belts fastened during takeoff.
words/#28-15/tip: It is imperative that + 주어 + (should) 동사원형 구문으로, that절 동사에 -s를 붙이거나 과거형을 쓰면 오답이다.
In the pattern It is imperative that + subject + (should) base verb, adding -s to the that-clause verb or using the past tense is wrong.
words/#28-15/q/k: 가주어 It is 뒤 보어 자리이며, that절에 동사원형 be가 쓰였으므로 필요를 나타내는 imperative가 정답. impressive는 형용사지만 that절에 동사원형을 쓰는 구문을 이끌지 않는다.

The blank is the complement after the dummy subject It is, and the that-clause uses the base verb be, so imperative, which expresses necessity, is correct. Impressive is an adjective but doesn't lead a that-clause with a base verb.
words/#28-16/exKo: 건물을 영업시간 중에 보수하면 어느 정도의 지연은 불가피하다.
Some delays are inevitable when a building is renovated during business hours.
words/#28-16/der/0/m: unavoidably; as was bound to happen
words/#28-16/tip: seem, become 등 2형식 동사 뒤 보어 자리에 형용사 inevitable이 온다. 부사 inevitably는 문장 전체를 수식하는 자리로도 출제된다.
After linking verbs like seem and become, the adjective inevitable is the complement. The adverb inevitably is also tested as a sentence modifier.
words/#28-16/q/k: 2형식 동사 seems 뒤 보어 자리이므로 형용사 inevitable이 정답. 부사 inevitably는 보어가 될 수 없고, 명사 inevitability와 inevitableness는 의미상 주어를 설명하는 보어로 맞지 않는다.

After the linking verb seems, a complement is needed, so the adjective inevitable is correct. The adverb inevitably can't be a complement, and the nouns inevitability and inevitableness don't work as a complement describing the subject.
words/#28-17/exKo: 참석자들은 디지털 마케팅 워크숍이 매우 유익했다고 생각했다.
Attendees found the workshop on digital marketing extremely informative.
words/#28-17/tip: informative(유익한)는 사물을, informed(잘 아는)는 사람이나 결정(an informed decision)을 수식한다. 'find + 목적어 + informative' 5형식으로도 쓰인다.
Informative (useful) describes things, while informed (knowledgeable) describes people or decisions (an informed decision). It is also used as find + object + informative.
words/#28-17/q/k: 오디오 가이드가 '유익한'이므로 informative가 정답. informed는 사람이 '잘 아는'이라는 뜻이고, information은 명사, inform은 동사다.
The audio guide is "useful and full of information", so informative is correct. Informed means a person is "knowledgeable", information is a noun, and inform is a verb.
words/#28-18/exKo: 정기적인 직원 교육은 우리 품질 관리 프로그램의 필수적인 부분이다.
Regular staff training is an integral part of our quality control program.
words/#28-18/tip: an integral part of와 be integral to 형태로 출제된다. integrity(정직, 진실성)와 형태를 혼동하지 않도록 한다.
It is tested as an integral part of and be integral to. Don't confuse its form with integrity (honesty).
words/#28-18/q/k: be동사 뒤 보어 자리에서 to와 짝을 이뤄 '~에 필수적인'을 뜻하는 integral이 정답. integrated는 into와 쓰이고, integrity와 integration은 명사다.
After the be verb, the complement that pairs with to to mean "essential to ~" is integral. Integrated goes with into, and integrity and integration are nouns.
words/#28-19/exKo: 그 호텔은 도심 근처에서 적당한 가격에 편안한 객실을 제공한다.
The hotel offers comfortable rooms at moderate prices near the city center.
words/#28-19/tip: moderate growth/increase는 경제 기사에서 '완만한 성장'으로 쓰인다. 동사 moderate(사회를 보다)와 명사 moderator(토론 사회자)는 듣기에도 나온다.
In economic news, moderate growth/increase means "steady, modest growth". The verb moderate (to lead a discussion) and the noun moderator (discussion leader) also appear in listening.
words/#28-19/q/k: 명사 growth를 꾸미는 형용사 자리이므로 moderate가 정답. moderately는 부사, moderation과 moderator는 명사다.
The blank modifies the noun growth, so it needs an adjective: moderate. Moderately is an adverb, and moderation and moderator are nouns.
words/#28-20/exKo: 새 모델에서 가장 눈에 띄는 변화는 더 길어진 배터리 수명이다.
The most notable change in the new model is its longer battery life.
words/#28-20/tip: be notable for(~로 유명하다)로 쓰인다. 부사 notably는 particularly처럼 '특히'라는 뜻으로 예시 앞에 온다.
It is used as be notable for (be famous for). The adverb notably means "especially", like particularly, and comes before examples.
words/#28-20/q/k: be동사 is 뒤 보어 자리이며 for와 함께 '~로 유명한'을 뜻하는 형용사 notable이 정답. notably는 부사, notice와 notation은 명사다.
After the be verb is, the complement that combines with for to mean "famous for ~" is the adjective notable. Notably is an adverb, and notice and notation are nouns.
words/#28-21/exKo: 그 식당은 2018년 개업 이후 수많은 상을 받았다.
The restaurant has received numerous awards since it opened in 2018.
words/#28-21/tip: numerous 뒤에는 반드시 복수 가산명사가 온다. much, a great deal of 같은 불가산 수량 표현과 구분하는 문제가 나온다.
Numerous must be followed by a plural countable noun. Questions contrast it with uncountable quantity words like much and a great deal of.
words/#28-21/q/k: 복수 가산명사 customers를 수식하므로 Numerous가 정답. Much와 A great deal of는 불가산명사, Every는 단수명사와 쓴다.
It modifies the plural countable noun customers, so Numerous is correct. Much and A great deal of go with uncountable nouns, and Every goes with singular nouns.
words/#28-22/exKo: 창고 보조직에는 이전 경력이 필요하지 않다.
No prior experience is required for the warehouse assistant position.
words/#28-22/tip: 형용사 prior는 명사 앞에서 '사전의, 이전의'라는 뜻이다. prior to는 before와 같은 전치사구라 뒤에 명사나 동명사가 온다.
The adjective prior comes before a noun and means "earlier, advance". Prior to is a prepositional phrase meaning before, so a noun or gerund follows.
words/#28-22/q/k: 명사 experience를 꾸미는 형용사 자리이므로 prior가 정답. priority는 명사, prioritize는 동사, primarily는 부사다.
The blank modifies the noun experience, so it needs an adjective: prior. Priority is a noun, prioritize a verb, and primarily an adverb.
words/#28-23/exKo: 환급 신청서에 관련 영수증을 모두 첨부하기 바란다.
Please attach all relevant receipts to your reimbursement request.
words/#28-23/der/0/m: connection; how closely related something is
words/#28-23/tip: be relevant to(~와 관련 있다)로 전치사 to와 짝을 이룬다. relevant experience는 채용 공고 빈출 표현이다.
It pairs with to: be relevant to (be related to). Relevant experience is a common phrase in job ads.
words/#28-23/q/k: 관계절의 be동사 is 뒤 보어 자리이므로 형용사 relevant가 정답. relevance와 relevancy는 명사, relevantly는 부사다.
After the be verb is in the relative clause, a complement is needed, so the adjective relevant is correct. Relevance and relevancy are nouns, and relevantly is an adverb.
words/#28-24/exKo: 많은 쇼핑객은 빠른 배송에 추가 요금을 내기를 꺼린다.
Many shoppers are reluctant to pay extra for express delivery.
words/#28-24/tip: be reluctant to + 동사원형으로 쓴다. Part 7에서는 hesitant, unwilling으로 패러프레이징된다.
It is used as be reluctant to + base verb. In Part 7 it is paraphrased as hesitant or unwilling.
words/#28-24/q/k: be동사 were 뒤 보어 자리이며 to부정사와 짝을 이루는 형용사 reluctant가 정답. reluctance는 명사, reluctantly는 부사다.
After the be verb were, the complement that pairs with a to-infinitive is the adjective reluctant. Reluctance is a noun and reluctantly is an adverb.
words/#28-25/exKo: 회의가 끝난 후 관리자들은 각자의 사무실로 돌아갔다.
After the meeting, the managers returned to their respective offices.
words/#28-25/der/0/m: in the order given; each in turn
words/#28-25/tip: their respective + 복수명사 형태가 전형적이다. respectful(공손한), respectable(존경할 만한)과 뜻을 구분하는 문제가 나온다.
Their respective + plural noun is the typical pattern. Questions test it against respectful (polite) and respectable (worthy of respect).
words/#28-25/q/k: 팀장마다 '각자의' 부서를 뜻하므로 respective가 정답. respectful은 '공손한', respectable은 '존경할 만한'이라 부서를 수식하기에 어색하다.
Each team leader has their "own" department, so respective is correct. Respectful means "polite" and respectable "worthy of respect", which sound odd describing departments.
words/#28-26/exKo: 그 회사는 내년에 지점 두 곳을 새로 열 충분한 자금이 있다.
The company has sufficient funds to open two new branches next year.
words/#28-26/tip: 명사 앞에는 sufficient, 형용사·부사 앞에는 sufficiently(sufficiently large)를 쓴다. insufficient funds(잔액 부족)도 자주 보인다.
Use sufficient before a noun and sufficiently before an adjective or adverb (sufficiently large). Insufficient funds (not enough money in an account) is also common.
words/#28-26/q/k: 명사 time을 꾸미는 형용사 자리이므로 sufficient가 정답. sufficiently는 부사, sufficiency는 명사, suffice는 동사다.
The blank modifies the noun time, so it needs an adjective: sufficient. Sufficiently is an adverb, sufficiency a noun, and suffice a verb.
words/#28-27/exKo: 우리는 아직 연례 회의에 적합한 장소를 찾고 있다.
We are still looking for a suitable venue for the annual conference.
words/#28-27/der/0/m: to fit; to match; to be convenient for
words/#28-27/tip: be suitable for + 명사로 전치사 for와 짝을 이룬다. 동사 suit는 타동사라 suit your needs처럼 목적어를 바로 취한다.
It pairs with for: be suitable for + noun. The verb suit is transitive and takes an object directly, as in suit your needs.
words/#28-27/q/k: for와 짝을 이뤄 '~에 적합한'을 뜻하는 suitable이 정답. capable은 of, accustomed는 to, dependent는 on과 함께 쓴다.
Suitable, which pairs with for to mean "right for ~", is correct. Capable goes with of, accustomed with to, and dependent with on.
words/#28-28/exKo: 이 다용도 프린터는 스캔, 복사, 팩스 전송도 할 수 있다.
This versatile printer can also scan, copy, and send faxes.
words/#28-28/tip: 제품에는 '다용도의', 사람에게는 '다재다능한'이라는 뜻으로 쓴다. 제품 광고에서 multipurpose로 패러프레이징된다.
For products it means "having many uses"; for people it means "talented in many areas". In product ads it is paraphrased as multipurpose.
words/#28-28/q/k: 빵 굽기, 찜, 그릴 요리를 모두 할 수 있다는 결과절이므로 '다용도의' versatile이 정답. durable(내구성 있는), affordable(저렴한), portable(휴대용의)은 결과와 연결되지 않는다.

The clause that follows says it can bake, steam, and grill, so versatile (multipurpose) is correct. Durable (long-lasting), affordable (cheap enough), and portable (easy to carry) don't lead to that result.
words/#28-29/m/0: method, way of dealing with something
words/#28-29/exKo: 그 컨설턴트는 운영비를 줄이는 새로운 방법을 권했다.
The consultant recommended a new approach to reducing operating costs.
words/#28-29/tip: 명사 approach to의 to는 전치사라 뒤에 동명사가 온다(approach to reducing). 반면 동사 approach는 타동사라 approach the problem처럼 to 없이 쓴다.
In the noun phrase approach to, to is a preposition, so a gerund follows (approach to reducing). The verb approach is transitive, so it is used without to: approach the problem.
words/#28-29/q/k: 관사 a와 형용사 cautious 뒤의 명사 자리이므로 approach가 정답. approachable은 형용사, approaching과 approached는 분사다.
After the article a and the adjective cautious, a noun is needed, so approach is correct. Approachable is an adjective, and approaching and approached are participles.
words/#28-30/exKo: 가격은 고객의 구매 결정에서 한 가지 측면일 뿐이다.
Price is only one aspect of a customer's purchasing decision.
words/#28-30/tip: every/each 뒤에는 단수 aspect, various/many 뒤에는 복수 aspects가 온다. 'in every respect(모든 면에서)'와 구분해 둔다.
Use singular aspect after every/each and plural aspects after various/many. Keep it apart from in every respect (in every way).
words/#28-30/q/k: every 뒤에는 단수명사가 오고, '공급망의 모든 측면'이라는 뜻이므로 aspect가 정답. aspects는 복수형이라 every와 쓸 수 없고, respect와 prospect는 of와 함께 이 뜻을 나타내지 못한다.

Every takes a singular noun, and the meaning is "every part of the supply chain", so aspect is correct. Aspects is plural and can't follow every, and respect and prospect can't give this meaning with of.
words/#28-31/exKo: 고객 만족도 향상에 헌신해 준 최 씨에게 감사드린다.
We thank Ms. Choi for her commitment to improving customer satisfaction.
words/#28-31/der/0/m: to dedicate oneself; to promise; to carry out (a crime, etc.)
words/#28-31/tip: commitment to의 to는 전치사라 뒤에 명사나 동명사가 온다(commitment to reducing). 'be committed to -ing'와 함께 출제된다.
In commitment to, to is a preposition, so a noun or gerund follows (commitment to reducing). It is tested together with be committed to -ing.
words/#28-31/q/k: 소유격 The company's 뒤 주어 자리이므로 명사 commitment가 정답. commit과 commits는 동사, committed는 형용사·과거분사다.
After the possessive The company's, a noun is needed as the subject, so commitment is correct. Commit and commits are verbs, and committed is an adjective or past participle.
words/#28-32/exKo: 고객 정보는 서면 동의 없이 제3자와 공유될 수 없다.
Customer data cannot be shared with third parties without written consent.
words/#28-32/tip: 명사와 동사의 형태가 같다. 동사 consent는 자동사라 consent to the terms처럼 to가 필요하다.
The noun and verb have the same form. The verb consent is intransitive and needs to, as in consent to the terms.
words/#28-32/q/k: '사전 동의 없이는 게시하지 않는다'는 의미이므로 consent가 정답. contest(대회), conduct(행동), concept(개념)는 문맥에 맞지 않는다.
The meaning is "won't be published without their prior permission", so consent is correct. Contest (competition), conduct (behavior), and concept (idea) don't fit the context.
words/#28-33/exKo: 모든 제안서는 동일한 기준에 따라 평가된다.
All proposals will be evaluated according to the same criteria.
words/#28-33/tip: criteria는 criterion의 복수형이라 these criteria, criteria are처럼 복수로 받는다. meet the criteria(기준을 충족하다)가 빈출 연어다.
Criteria is the plural of criterion, so treat it as plural: these criteria, criteria are. A common collocation is meet the criteria (satisfy the standards).
words/#28-33/q/k: all of the 뒤에는 복수명사가 와야 하므로 criterion의 복수형 criteria가 정답. criterion은 단수형이고, critic(비평가)과 critique(비평)은 문맥에 맞지 않는다.
The phrase all of the must be followed by a plural noun, so criteria, the plural of criterion, is correct. Criterion is singular, and critic (reviewer) and critique (review) don't fit the context.
words/#28-34/exKo: 시는 주민들의 재활용을 장려하기 위해 새로운 계획을 시작했다.
The city launched a new initiative to encourage residents to recycle.
words/#28-34/tip: '새로운 계획·사업'이라는 뜻과 'take the initiative(솔선하다)'라는 숙어가 모두 출제된다. 동사 initiate와 품사를 구분해야 한다.
Both the meaning "new plan or program" and the idiom take the initiative (act first, on one's own) are tested. Distinguish it from the verb initiate by part of speech.
words/#28-34/q/k: take the initiative to do는 '솔선하여 ~하다'라는 숙어이므로 initiative가 정답. initiation은 '개시, 입회', initial은 형용사, initiate는 동사다.
The idiom take the initiative to do means "act on one's own to do", so initiative is correct. Initiation means "start; admission (to a group)", initial is an adjective, and initiate is a verb.
words/#28-35/exKo: 그 공장은 연례 점검 후 새로운 안전 조치를 도입했다.
The factory introduced new safety measures after the annual inspection.
words/#28-35/tip: 토익에서는 '측정'보다 '조치, 대책'의 뜻으로 주로 복수형 measures로 쓴다. take measures to do(~하기 위해 조치를 취하다)가 빈출이다.
On the TOEIC it usually means "steps, actions" rather than "measurement", mostly in the plural measures. The phrase take measures to do (take steps to do) is very common.
words/#28-35/q/k: take measures는 '조치를 취하다'라는 연어이므로 measures가 정답. measurements는 '치수, 측정값'이라 '지원하기 위한 조치'라는 의미가 되지 않는다.
Take measures is a collocation meaning "take action", so measures is correct. Measurements means "sizes, measured values", so it can't mean "steps to support".
words/#28-36/exKo: 올해 우리의 주요 목표는 온라인 매출을 15퍼센트 늘리는 것이다.
Our main objective this year is to increase online sales by 15 percent.
words/#28-36/tip: 명사(목표)와 형용사(객관적인)의 형태가 같다. Part 7에서 objective는 goal, aim으로 패러프레이징된다.
The noun (goal) and the adjective (unbiased) have the same form. In Part 7, objective is paraphrased as goal or aim.
words/#28-36/q/k: One of the 뒤에는 복수명사가 와야 하고 '합병의 핵심 목표'라는 뜻이므로 objectives가 정답. objection은 '반대'라는 뜻의 단수명사라 맞지 않는다.
One of the must be followed by a plural noun, and the meaning is "the key goals of the merger", so objectives is correct. Objection is a singular noun meaning "disagreement", so it doesn't fit.
words/#28-37/exKo: 다양한 배경의 직원을 채용하면 팀에 새로운 시각이 생긴다.
Hiring staff from different backgrounds brings fresh perspectives to the team.
words/#28-37/tip: from a(n) + 형용사 + perspective(~의 관점에서) 형태가 빈출이다. 형태가 비슷한 prospective(장래의, 유망한)와 혼동하지 않도록 한다.
From a(n) + adjective + perspective (from a ~ point of view) is very common. Don't confuse it with the similar-looking prospective (future, likely).
words/#28-37/q/k: from a financial perspective는 '재정적 관점에서'라는 뜻이므로 perspective가 정답. prospective는 형용사, prospect는 '전망, 가능성', perspire는 동사다.
From a financial perspective means "from a financial point of view", so perspective is correct. Prospective is an adjective, prospect means "outlook, chance", and perspire is a verb.
words/#28-38/exKo: 그 프로젝트의 범위는 두 개 도시를 추가로 포함하도록 확대되었다.
The scope of the project was expanded to include two additional cities.
words/#28-38/tip: within/beyond/outside the scope of가 숙어처럼 쓰인다. 계약서·제안서의 scope of work(업무 범위)는 Part 7 빈출이다.
Within/beyond/outside the scope of is used like an idiom. Scope of work (range of tasks) in contracts and proposals is common in Part 7.
words/#28-38/q/k: outside the scope of는 '~의 범위를 벗어나는'이라는 뜻으로, 오용으로 인한 수리는 보증 범위 밖이라는 문맥이므로 scope가 정답. aim(목표), sight(시야), phase(단계)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.

The phrase outside the scope of means "beyond the range of"; repairs caused by misuse are not covered by the warranty, so scope is correct. Aim (goal), sight (view), and phase (stage) don't fit the meaning.
words/#28-39/exKo: 이 조리법에서는 마가린을 버터 대용으로 쓸 수 있다.
Margarine can be used as a substitute for butter in this recipe.
words/#28-39/tip: 명사는 a substitute for(~의 대체물), 동사는 substitute A for B(B 대신 A를 쓰다) 구조로 쓴다. 사람을 가리킬 때도 쓸 수 있다.
The noun is used as a substitute for (a replacement for), and the verb as substitute A for B (use A instead of B). It can also refer to a person.
words/#28-39/q/k: 관사 a 뒤 명사 자리이며 이 씨를 '대신하는 사람'을 뜻하므로 substitute가 정답. substitution은 '대체(하는 행위)'라는 추상명사라 사람을 가리킬 수 없고, replace와 replacing은 명사 자리에 올 수 없다.

After the article a, a noun is needed, and it means a person "standing in" for Mr. Lee, so substitute is correct. Substitution is an abstract noun for the act of replacing and can't refer to a person, and replace and replacing can't fill a noun slot.
words/#28-40/exKo: 새 회계 소프트웨어로의 전환은 예상보다 순조롭게 진행되었다.
The transition to the new accounting software went more smoothly than expected.
words/#28-40/der/0/m: relating to a period of change; temporary
words/#28-40/tip: transition from A to B(A에서 B로의 전환) 구조와 smooth transition이 자주 나온다. transaction(거래), translation(번역)과 형태가 비슷해 어휘 문제 오답으로 쓰인다.

The patterns transition from A to B (change from A to B) and smooth transition are common. Transaction (deal) and translation (rendering in another language) look similar and are used as wrong options.
words/#28-40/q/k: 새 시스템으로의 '순조로운 전환'을 의미하므로 transition이 정답. translation(번역), transaction(거래), transmission(전송)은 문맥에 맞지 않는다.
The meaning is a "smooth changeover" to the new system, so transition is correct. Translation (rendering in another language), transaction (deal), and transmission (sending) don't fit the context.
words/#29-01/m/0: in a suitable way, to match
words/#29-01/exKo: 일정이 변경되었으니 그에 맞게 출장 계획을 조정하기 바란다.
The schedule has changed, so please adjust your travel plans accordingly.
words/#29-01/der/1/m: as stated by; in line with
words/#29-01/tip: 동사 뒤 문장 끝에서는 '그에 맞게'(adjust accordingly), 문두에서는 '따라서'라는 접속부사로 쓰인다. according to(전치사구)와 형태를 혼동하지 않도록 한다.

After a verb at the end of a sentence it means "to match the situation" (adjust accordingly); at the start of a sentence it is a linking adverb meaning "therefore". Don't confuse it with the prepositional phrase according to.
words/#29-01/q/k: 완전한 문장 뒤에서 동사 revise를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 accordingly가 정답. according은 to와 함께 써야 하고, accordance와 accord는 명사다.
After a complete clause, an adverb is needed to modify the verb revise, so accordingly is correct. According must be used with to, and accordance and accord are nouns.
words/#29-02/exKo: 게다가 워크숍 참가자 전원은 수료증을 받게 된다.
Additionally, all workshop participants will receive a certificate of completion.
words/#29-02/tip: 접속부사 additionally는 마침표나 세미콜론 뒤에서 콤마와 함께 쓴다. 뒤에 명사(구)가 오는 전치사 in addition to와 구분하는 문제가 나온다.
The linking adverb additionally comes after a period or semicolon, with a comma. Questions contrast it with the prepositional phrase in addition to, which takes a noun (phrase).
words/#29-02/q/k: 앞 문장에 혜택을 추가하는 접속부사 자리이므로 Additionally가 정답. In addition to는 뒤에 명사가 와야 하는 전치사구이고, Although와 Because는 접속사라 콤마만 두고 단독으로 쓸 수 없다.

The blank needs a linking adverb that adds another benefit to the previous sentence, so Additionally is correct. In addition to is a prepositional phrase that needs a noun after it, and Although and Because are conjunctions that can't stand alone with just a comma.
words/#29-03/exKo: 안개로 항공편이 지연되었고, 그 결과 몇몇 승객이 연결편을 놓쳤다.
The flight was delayed by fog; consequently, several passengers missed their connections.
words/#29-03/tip: 앞 문장의 '결과'를 이끄는 접속부사다. 접속사 so와 달리 콤마만으로 두 절을 잇지 못하고 세미콜론이나 마침표 뒤에 쓴다.
It is a linking adverb that introduces the result of the previous sentence. Unlike the conjunction so, it can't join two clauses with just a comma; use it after a semicolon or period.
words/#29-03/mq/k: 수요 초과의 '결과'로 인력을 추가 채용했으므로 Consequently가 정답. Nevertheless(그럼에도), Otherwise(그렇지 않으면), Instead(대신에)는 두 문장의 인과 관계에 맞지 않는다.

The company hired more workers as a "result" of demand exceeding expectations, so Consequently is correct. Nevertheless (even so), Otherwise (if not), and Instead (in place of that) don't fit the cause-and-effect link between the sentences.
words/#29-04/exKo: 웹사이트를 새로 단장한 이후 온라인 매출이 상당히 늘었다.
Online sales have increased considerably since we redesigned our website.
words/#29-04/der/1/m: to think about; to take into account
words/#29-04/tip: considerably는 비교급 앞에서 '훨씬'이라는 강조 부사로 쓰인다(considerably lower). very는 비교급을 수식할 수 없다는 점이 함정으로 나온다.
Before a comparative, considerably is an intensifier meaning "much" (considerably lower). A common trap: very can't modify a comparative.
words/#29-04/q/k: 비교급 lighter를 강조하는 부사 자리이므로 considerably가 정답. very는 비교급을 수식할 수 없고, considerable은 형용사, consideration은 명사다.
The blank is an adverb that intensifies the comparative lighter, so considerably is correct. Very can't modify a comparative, considerable is an adjective, and consideration is a noun.
words/#29-05/exKo: 우리는 현재 재무팀에서 함께 일할 경력 있는 회계사를 찾고 있다.
We are currently looking for an experienced accountant to join our finance team.
words/#29-05/tip: 현재시제·현재진행형과 어울리며 과거시제와 함께 쓰면 오답이다. 시제 단서로 previously, formerly 등과 구분하는 문제가 나온다.
It goes with the present simple and present progressive; using it with the past tense is wrong. Questions use tense clues to set it against previously, formerly, etc.
words/#29-05/q/k: 현재시제 is와 '5월에 다시 문을 연다'는 내용으로 보아 '현재' 닫혀 있다는 뜻의 currently가 정답. previously와 formerly는 과거의 일을, lately는 주로 현재완료와 쓰인다.
The present tense is and "will reopen in May" show it is closed "now", so currently is correct. Previously and formerly refer to the past, and lately is mainly used with the present perfect.
words/#29-06/m/0: in person, without anyone in between
words/#29-06/exKo: Please send your application directly to the human resources manager.
words/#29-06/tip: report directly to(~의 직속 부하이다), directly after(~ 직후에)가 빈출이다. 동사를 수식하는 부사 자리에 명사 direction, director를 넣는 오답에 주의한다.

The phrases report directly to (be directly under someone) and directly after (right after) are common. Watch out for wrong options that put the nouns direction or director in an adverb slot modifying a verb.
words/#29-06/q/k: 자동사 report 뒤에서 동사를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 directly가 정답. report directly to는 '~에게 직속으로 보고하다'라는 뜻이다. 나머지는 모두 명사다.
After the intransitive verb report, an adverb is needed to modify the verb, so directly is correct. Report directly to means "be directly under ~ (as a boss)". The other options are all nouns.
words/#29-07/exKo: 처음에는 판매가 부진했지만 그 제품은 결국 회사의 최고 인기 상품이 되었다.
Sales were slow at first, but the product eventually became the company's best seller.
words/#29-07/tip: 오랜 과정이나 어려움 끝에 '결국' 일어난 일을 나타낸다. 수동태 be와 p.p. 사이 부사 자리로 자주 출제된다.
It describes something that happens "in the end" after a long process or difficulties. It is often tested in the adverb slot between be and the past participle in the passive.
words/#29-07/q/k: 수동태 was와 과거분사 completed 사이의 부사 자리이므로 eventually가 정답. eventual과 eventful은 형용사, event는 명사다.
The blank is the adverb slot between the passive was and the past participle completed, so eventually is correct. Eventual and eventful are adjectives, and event is a noun.
words/#29-08/exKo: 이 주차 구역은 오로지 호텔 투숙객만 이용할 수 있다.
This parking area is reserved exclusively for hotel guests.
words/#29-08/tip: exclusively for/to(오로지 ~에게만)가 빈출이다. 명사를 수식할 때는 형용사 exclusive(an exclusive offer)를 쓴다.
Exclusively for/to (only for) is very common. To modify a noun, use the adjective exclusive (an exclusive offer).
words/#29-08/q/k: 형용사 valid 뒤에서 전치사구 for customers를 한정하는 부사 자리이므로 '오로지'를 뜻하는 exclusively가 정답. exclusive는 형용사, exclusion은 명사, exclude는 동사다.
After the adjective valid, an adverb meaning "only" is needed to limit the phrase for customers, so exclusively is correct. Exclusive is an adjective, exclusion a noun, and exclude a verb.
words/#29-09/exKo: 예전에 섬유 공장이었던 그 건물에는 현재 여러 기술 스타트업이 입주해 있다.
The building, formerly a textile factory, now houses several technology start-ups.
words/#29-09/tip: 회사명 변경·합병 기사의 formerly known as(구 ~)가 빈출이다. 철자가 비슷한 formally(공식적으로)와 혼동하지 않도록 한다.
The phrase formerly known as (previously called) is common in articles about name changes and mergers. Don't confuse it with formally (officially), which is spelled similarly.
words/#29-09/q/k: '이전에 ~로 알려진'이라는 뜻의 formerly known as가 정답. formally는 '공식적으로'라는 뜻이고, former는 형용사라 과거분사를 수식할 수 없다.
The phrase formerly known as, meaning "previously called", is correct. Formally means "officially", and former is an adjective, so it can't modify a past participle.
words/#29-10/exKo: 고객 지원팀에 연락하기 전에 자주 묻는 질문 목록을 확인하기 바란다.
Please check the list of frequently asked questions before contacting our support team.
words/#29-10/tip: 자동사 뒤나 과거분사 앞에서 부사 frequently를 쓴다. 형용사 frequent는 frequent customers(단골)처럼 명사를 꾸민다.
Use the adverb frequently after an intransitive verb or before a past participle. The adjective frequent modifies nouns, as in frequent customers (regulars).
words/#29-10/q/k: 자동사 travel을 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 frequently가 정답. frequent는 형용사, frequency는 명사, frequented는 과거분사다.
The blank modifies the intransitive verb travel, so it needs an adverb: frequently. Frequent is an adjective, frequency a noun, and frequented a past participle.
words/#29-11/exKo: 새 소프트웨어는 사용하기 쉽다. 게다가 현재 시스템보다 비용도 적게 든다.
The new software is easy to use. Furthermore, it costs less than our current system.
words/#29-11/tip: 앞 내용과 같은 방향의 정보를 덧붙이는 접속부사다. Part 6 문맥 문제에서 However(역접), Therefore(결과)와 구분해야 한다.
It is a linking adverb that adds information in the same direction as before. In Part 6 context questions, distinguish it from However (contrast) and Therefore (result).
words/#29-11/q/k: 역 근처라는 장점에 쇼핑센터와도 가깝다는 장점을 추가하므로 Furthermore가 정답. However는 대조, Otherwise는 '그렇지 않으면', Instead는 '대신에'라 문맥에 맞지 않는다.

It adds another advantage (near shopping centers) to the first (near the station), so Furthermore is correct. However shows contrast, Otherwise means "if not", and Instead means "in place of that", so they don't fit.
words/#29-12/exKo: 새 복사기는 지난달 설치된 이후로 거의 사용되지 않았다.
The new photocopier has hardly been used since it was installed last month.
words/#29-12/tip: hardly는 그 자체로 부정의 뜻이라 not, never와 함께 쓰지 않는다. hard(열심히, 세게)와 뜻이 전혀 다르다는 점이 함정이다.
Hardly is already negative, so don't use it with not or never. A trap: its meaning is completely different from hard (with effort; strongly).
words/#29-12/q/k: any와 함께 '거의 없는'이라는 부정의 뜻을 나타내는 hardly가 정답. hard는 '열심히, 어려운'이라는 뜻으로 any를 수식할 수 없다.
Hardly is correct because, with any, it gives the negative meaning "almost no". Hard means "with effort; difficult" and can't modify any.
words/#29-13/exKo: 장비 고장은 즉시 상사에게 보고하기 바란다.
Please report any equipment malfunctions to your supervisor immediately.
words/#29-13/tip: immediately after/following(~ 직후에)가 자주 나온다. 형용사 immediate는 immediate supervisor(직속 상사)처럼 명사를 꾸민다.
Immediately after/following (right after) is common. The adjective immediate modifies nouns, as in immediate supervisor (direct boss).
words/#29-13/q/k: after절 앞에서 '~한 직후에'를 만드는 부사 자리이므로 immediately가 정답. immediate는 형용사, immediacy는 명사다.
Before the after-clause, an adverb is needed to make "right after ~", so immediately is correct. Immediate is an adjective and immediacy is a noun.
words/#29-14/exKo: 온라인 식료품 쇼핑은 고령 소비자 사이에서 점점 더 인기를 얻고 있다.
Online grocery shopping has become increasingly popular among older consumers.
words/#29-14/tip: become increasingly + 형용사(점점 더 ~해지다) 형태가 전형적이다. 형용사를 꾸미는 자리에 분사 increasing을 넣는 오답이 자주 쓰인다.
The typical pattern is become increasingly + adjective (become more and more ~). A common wrong option puts the participle increasing in a slot that modifies an adjective.
words/#29-14/q/k: 형용사 common을 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 increasingly가 정답. increasing과 increased는 분사 형용사라 다른 형용사를 꾸밀 수 없다.
The blank modifies the adjective common, so it needs an adverb: increasingly. Increasing and increased are participle adjectives and can't modify another adjective.
words/#29-15/exKo: The project was initially scheduled to be completed in March.
words/#29-15/tip: be initially scheduled/planned to do처럼 수동태 사이에 자주 오며, 뒤에 but으로 변경 사항이 이어지는 경우가 많다.
It often appears inside the passive, as in be initially scheduled/planned to do, and is often followed by a change introduced with but.
words/#29-15/q/k: 수동태 was와 과거분사 planned 사이의 부사 자리이므로 initially가 정답. initial은 형용사, initiate는 동사, initiative는 명사다.
The blank is the adverb slot between the passive was and the past participle planned, so initially is correct. Initial is an adjective, initiate a verb, and initiative a noun.
words/#29-16/m/1: at the same time; on the other hand
words/#29-16/exKo: 다음 주에 사무실을 새로 칠한다. 그동안 직원들은 재택근무를 해도 된다.
The office will be repainted next week. Meanwhile, staff may work from home.
words/#29-16/tip: Meanwhile은 접속부사라 단독으로 콤마와 함께 쓴다. 뒤에 절이 오는 접속사 while, 명사가 오는 전치사 during과 구분하는 문제가 나온다.
Meanwhile is a linking adverb and stands alone with a comma. Questions contrast it with the conjunction while (+ clause) and the preposition during (+ noun).
words/#29-16/q/k: 콤마 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오는 접속부사 자리이며 '공사하는 그동안'이라는 뜻이므로 Meanwhile이 정답. While과 Whereas는 접속사, During은 전치사라 단독으로 쓸 수 없다.

The blank is a linking-adverb slot followed by a comma and a complete sentence, meaning "during that time (while work is going on)", so Meanwhile is correct. While and Whereas are conjunctions and During is a preposition, so they can't stand alone.
words/#29-17/exKo: 그 제안은 너무 비싸다. 게다가 우리의 주요 우려 사항도 다루지 않는다.
The proposal is too expensive. Moreover, it does not address our main concerns.
words/#29-17/tip: 앞 문장과 같은 방향(긍정+긍정, 부정+부정)의 내용을 추가한다. 접속부사라 뒤에 명사만 올 수 없고 완전한 절이 와야 한다.
It adds content in the same direction as the previous sentence (positive + positive, negative + negative). As a linking adverb, it must be followed by a full clause, not just a noun.
words/#29-17/q/k: 콤마 뒤 완전한 문장이 오는 접속부사 자리이며 장점을 추가하므로 Moreover가 정답. Despite는 전치사, Unless와 Whereas는 접속사라 이 자리에 올 수 없다.

The blank is a linking-adverb slot followed by a comma and a complete sentence, and it adds an advantage, so Moreover is correct. Despite is a preposition and Unless and Whereas are conjunctions, so they can't go here.
words/#29-18/exKo: 날씨가 좋지 않았지만, 그럼에도 불구하고 야외 축제에는 수천 명의 방문객이 몰렸다.
The weather was poor; nevertheless, the outdoor festival attracted thousands of visitors.
words/#29-18/tip: 같은 뜻이라도 despite/in spite of는 전치사(+명사), although는 접속사(+절), nevertheless는 접속부사(마침표·세미콜론 뒤)로 쓰임이 다르다.
They share a meaning but differ in use: despite/in spite of are prepositions (+ noun), although is a conjunction (+ clause), and nevertheless is a linking adverb (after a period or semicolon).
words/#29-18/q/k: 앞 문장과 대조되는 내용을 마침표 뒤에서 잇는 접속부사 자리이므로 Nevertheless가 정답. Although는 접속사, Despite와 Because of는 전치사라 콤마 뒤에 바로 절이 올 수 없다.

The blank is a linking-adverb slot after a period that introduces a contrast, so Nevertheless is correct. Although is a conjunction and Despite and Because of are prepositions, so a clause can't follow them after just a comma.
words/#29-19/exKo: 새로 단장한 로비는 다음 주 월요일에 일반에 공개된다.
The newly renovated lobby will be open to the public next Monday.
words/#29-19/tip: newly + 과거분사(newly hired employees) 형태로 쓰인다. 형용사 new는 과거분사를 수식할 수 없다는 점이 품사 문제의 핵심이다.
It is used as newly + past participle (newly hired employees). The key to part-of-speech questions: the adjective new can't modify a past participle.
words/#29-19/q/k: 과거분사 hired를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 newly가 정답. new는 형용사라 분사를 꾸밀 수 없고, newness와 news는 명사다.
The blank modifies the past participle hired, so it needs an adverb: newly. New is an adjective and can't modify a participle, and newness and news are nouns.
words/#29-20/exKo: 엘리베이터가 가끔 층 사이에서 멈춰서 기술자를 불렀다.
The elevator occasionally stops between floors, so a technician has been called.
words/#29-20/tip: 빈도부사로 일반동사 앞, be동사·조동사 뒤에 온다. 형용사 occasional(an occasional visitor)과 품사를 구분해야 한다.
As a frequency adverb, it comes before a main verb and after a be verb or modal. Distinguish it from the adjective occasional (an occasional visitor).
words/#29-20/q/k: 주어와 동사 works 사이에서 동사를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 occasionally가 정답. occasional은 형용사, occasion은 명사다.
Between the subject and the verb works, an adverb is needed to modify the verb, so occasionally is correct. Occasional is an adjective and occasion is a noun.
