It describes amounts and benefits, as in 'generous donation/discount/benefits', and the adverb generously comes in slots that modify verbs, as in 'generously donated'.
words/#88-14/q/k: 관사 a와 명사 donation 사이의 형용사 자리이므로 generous가 정답. generously는 부사, generosity와 generation은 명사다.
The blank is an adjective slot between the article a and the noun donation, so generous is correct. Generously is an adverb, and generosity and generation are nouns.
words/#88-15/m/0: stopping and starting; on and off
words/#88-15/exKo: 주말 내내 간간이 소나기가 내릴 것으로 예보되었으니 우산을 챙기는 것이 좋다.
Forecasters are predicting intermittent showers throughout the weekend, so bring an umbrella.
words/#88-15/der/0/m: on and off; from time to time
words/#88-15/tip: 일기 예보(intermittent showers)와 기술 문제(intermittent connection problems) 문맥에 나오며, 반대말 continuous, constant와 대비된다.
It appears in weather reports (intermittent showers) and tech problems (intermittent connection problems), in contrast to its opposites continuous and constant.
words/#88-15/q/k: 업그레이드 이후 '간헐적인' 접속 문제가 보고되었다는 뜻이므로 intermittent가 정답. impending(임박한)은 이미 발생한 문제와 맞지 않고, inquisitive(호기심 많은), ineligible(자격이 없는)은 의미가 맞지 않는다.

Users have reported "on-and-off" connection problems since the upgrade, so intermittent is correct. Impending (about to happen) doesn't fit problems that have already occurred, and inquisitive (curious) and ineligible (not qualified) don't fit the meaning.
words/#88-16/exKo: 각 팀원은 평가가 끝난 뒤 관리자에게서 개별 피드백을 받는다.
Each team member will receive individual feedback from the manager after the review.
words/#88-16/tip: 형용사(개별의)와 명사(개인) 모두로 쓰이며, 'individually wrapped(개별 포장된)'처럼 부사 individually를 묻는 문제가 나온다.
It is used both as an adjective (separate; personal) and as a noun (a person), and questions test the adverb individually, as in 'individually wrapped' (wrapped one by one).
words/#88-16/q/k: 관사 the와 명사 needs 사이의 형용사 자리이므로 individual이 정답. individually는 부사, individualize는 동사, individualism은 명사다.
The blank is an adjective slot between the article the and the noun needs, so individual is correct. Individually is an adverb, individualize is a verb, and individualism is a noun.
words/#88-17/exKo: 환영회에서 무료 음료는 손님 한 명당 두 잔으로 제한된다.
There is a limit of two free drinks per guest at the reception.
words/#88-17/tip: 'a limit on/of + 명사'와 동사 'limit A to B' 구조가 나오며, limited(제한된), limitation(제약)과의 품사 구분 문제가 빈출이다.
The structures 'a limit on/of + noun' and the verb pattern 'limit A to B' appear, and part-of-speech questions often contrast it with limited (restricted) and limitation (restriction).
words/#88-17/q/k: 관사 a 뒤의 명사 자리이고 'place a limit on(~에 제한을 두다)'을 이루므로 limit이 정답. limited, limiting, limitless는 형용사·분사라 관사 a 뒤에 단독으로 명사처럼 쓸 수 없다.

The blank is a noun slot after the article a, forming 'place a limit on' (to restrict), so limit is correct. Limited, limiting, and limitless are adjectives or participles and can't stand alone as a noun after a.
words/#88-18/exKo: 일부 직원은 여름철에 회사의 엄격한 복장 규정이 불편하다고 느낀다.
Some employees find the company's rigid dress code uncomfortable in summer.
words/#88-18/tip: 규칙·일정에 쓰면 '융통성 없는'이라는 부정적 의미가 강해 flexible(유연한)의 반의어로 출제되며, 포장재 문맥에서는 '단단한(rigid packaging)'의 뜻이 된다.
Used for rules or schedules it has a strongly negative sense of "inflexible" and is tested as the opposite of flexible. In packaging contexts it means "stiff" (rigid packaging).
words/#88-18/q/k: 'prefer A to B' 구조에서 flexible(유연한)과 대비되는 '융통성 없는'이라는 뜻이 필요하므로 rigid가 정답. fragile(깨지기 쉬운), vacant(비어 있는), hollow(속이 빈)는 일정을 수식하기에 맞지 않는다.

In the structure 'prefer A to B', the blank needs a word meaning "inflexible" in contrast to flexible, so rigid is correct. Fragile (easily broken), vacant (empty), and hollow (empty inside) don't fit as descriptions of a schedule.
words/#88-19/exKo: 그 실험실에는 저장실 출입 가능 인원에 관한 엄격한 규칙이 있다.
The laboratory has strict rules about who may enter the storage room.
words/#88-19/tip: 형용사 strict는 명사 앞, 부사 strictly는 'Smoking is strictly prohibited.'처럼 과거분사 앞에 오는 품사 자리 문제가 빈출이다.
A common word-position question: the adjective strict goes before nouns, while the adverb strictly goes before past participles, as in 'Smoking is strictly prohibited.'
words/#88-19/mq/k: 명사구 hygiene rules를 수식하는 형용사 자리이므로 strict가 정답. strictly는 부사, strictness와 stricture는 명사다.
The blank is an adjective slot describing the noun phrase hygiene rules, so strict is correct. Strictly is an adverb, and strictness and stricture are nouns.
words/#88-20/exKo: 평일이면 그 카페는 보통 300명이 넘는 손님을 받는다.
On a typical weekday, the café serves more than 300 customers.
words/#88-20/der/1/m: to be a classic example of
words/#88-20/tip: 'be typical of(~의 전형적인 특징이다)'의 전치사 of가 출제되며, 부사 typically(보통)는 'typically takes two days'처럼 동사를 수식한다.
The preposition of in 'be typical of' (to be characteristic of) is tested, and the adverb typically (usually) modifies verbs, as in 'typically takes two days'.
words/#88-20/q/k: be동사 뒤 보어 자리이고 전치사 of와 함께 '~의 전형적인 특징이다'라는 뜻을 이루는 형용사 typical이 정답. typically는 부사, typify는 동사, type은 명사다.

The blank is the complement after the be verb, and with the preposition of the adjective typical means "characteristic of," so it is correct. Typically is an adverb, typify is a verb, and type is a noun.
words/#88-21/exKo: Fischer 씨는 영업팀의 싱가포르 방문을 위한 출장 준비를 하고 있다.
Ms. Fischer is making travel arrangements for the sales team's visit to Singapore.
words/#88-21/der/0/m: to plan; to set up; to put in order
words/#88-21/tip: 'make arrangements for(~을 준비하다)'처럼 준비의 뜻일 때는 주로 복수형으로 쓰며, 동사 arrange와의 품사 구분 문제가 나온다.
In the sense of "preparations" it is mostly plural, as in 'make arrangements for' (to prepare for), and part-of-speech questions contrast it with the verb arrange.
words/#88-21/q/k: 동사 make의 목적어인 명사 자리이고 'make arrangements for(~을 준비하다)'를 이루므로 arrangements가 정답. arranges, arranged, arranging은 동사 형태다.
The blank is a noun slot that is the object of make, forming 'make arrangements for' (to prepare for), so arrangements is correct. Arranges, arranged, and arranging are verb forms.
words/#88-22/m/1: whether stock or seats are left
words/#88-22/m/2: free time; when you are free
words/#88-22/exKo: 다음 주 후속 회의에 참석 가능한 시간을 알려 주기 바란다.
Please let me know your availability for a follow-up meeting next week.
words/#88-22/tip: 'subject to availability(재고·좌석 상황에 따라)'가 공지문에 빈출이며, 형용사 available과 명사 availability의 품사 구분 문제가 자주 나온다.
The phrase 'subject to availability' (depending on stock or seats) is common in notices, and part-of-speech questions often contrast the adjective available with the noun availability.
words/#88-22/q/k: 'subject to + 명사' 구조에서 '이용 가능 여부에 따라'라는 뜻을 이루는 availability가 정답. available은 형용사, availably는 부사이고, avail은 동사(도움이 되다) 또는 to no avail(보람 없이) 같은 표현에 쓰여 이 자리에 맞지 않는다.

In the structure 'subject to + noun', availability forms the meaning "depending on whether it's available," so it is correct. Available is an adjective, availably is an adverb, and avail is a verb (to help) or used in phrases like to no avail (without success), so it doesn't fit here.
words/#88-23/exKo: 응급 의료 상황 같은 특별한 사정이 아니면 환불되지 않는다.
Refunds are not available except in extraordinary circumstances, such as a medical emergency.
words/#88-23/tip: 'under no circumstances(어떤 경우에도 ~하지 않다)'와 'due to unforeseen circumstances(예기치 못한 사정으로)'가 빈출이며, 주로 복수형으로 쓰고 전치사 under와 짝을 이룬다.

The phrases 'under no circumstances' (never, in any situation) and 'due to unforeseen circumstances' (because of unexpected events) are common. It is mostly plural and pairs with the preposition under.
words/#88-23/q/k: 'Under no circumstances(어떤 경우에도 ~않다)'라는 고정 표현이므로 circumstances가 정답. 이 표현은 부정어구라 뒤에 should employees처럼 도치가 일어난다. occasions, situations, incidents는 under no와 고정 표현을 이루지 않는다.

The set phrase is 'Under no circumstances' (never, in any situation), so circumstances is correct. Because this phrase is negative, it causes inversion after it, as in should employees. Occasions, situations, and incidents don't form a set phrase with under no.
words/#88-24/exKo: 안전 지침을 따르지 않으면 작업자에게 심각한 결과를 초래할 수 있다.
Failure to follow the safety guidelines may have serious consequences for workers.
words/#88-24/tip: 'as a consequence of(~의 결과로)' 구문과 접속부사 consequently(그 결과)를 구분하는 품사 문제가 출제된다.
Part-of-speech questions test the phrase 'as a consequence of' (as a result of) against the conjunctive adverb consequently (as a result).
words/#88-24/q/k: 관사 a 뒤 명사 자리이고 'as a consequence of(~의 결과로)'를 이루므로 consequence가 정답. consequently는 부사, consequent와 consequential은 형용사다.
The blank is a noun slot after the article a, forming 'as a consequence of' (as a result of), so consequence is correct. Consequently is an adverb, and consequent and consequential are adjectives.
words/#88-25/m/0: degree; scope; how far something goes
words/#88-25/exKo: 엔지니어들은 홍수로 인한 피해 규모를 아직 평가하고 있다.
Engineers are still assessing the extent of the damage caused by the flood.
words/#88-25/tip: 'to some/a certain extent(어느 정도)'처럼 전치사 to와 짝을 이루며, 동사 extend, 형용사 extensive와 혼동시키는 품사 문제가 나온다.
It pairs with the preposition to, as in 'to some/a certain extent' (partly), and part-of-speech questions use the verb extend and the adjective extensive as traps.
words/#88-25/q/k: 'to a large extent(상당 부분, 대체로)'를 이루는 명사 extent가 정답. extend는 동사, extensive는 형용사이고, extension(연장)은 이 표현에 쓰지 않는다.
The noun extent forms 'to a large extent' (largely; mostly), so it is correct. Extend is a verb, extensive is an adjective, and extension (lengthening) isn't used in this phrase.
words/#88-26/exKo: 두 회사는 향후 협력의 틀을 마련하는 협정에 서명했다.
The two companies signed an agreement that provides a framework for future cooperation.
words/#88-26/tip: 'a framework for + 명사(~을 위한 틀)'와 'within the framework of'처럼 전치사 for, within과 함께 쓰이며, 정책·협정 문맥에서 structure, basis로 패러프레이즈된다.

It is used with the prepositions for and within, as in 'a framework for + noun' (a structure for) and 'within the framework of'. In policy and agreement contexts it is paraphrased as structure or basis.
words/#88-26/q/k: 신규 투자 제안을 평가하기 위한 명확한 '틀'을 제공한다는 뜻이므로 framework가 정답. workforce(인력), workload(업무량), frequency(빈도)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
The guidelines provide a clear "structure" for evaluating proposals, so framework is correct. Workforce (staff), workload (amount of work), and frequency (how often) don't fit the meaning.
words/#88-27/exKo: 높은 운송비는 여전히 해외 시장 진출의 가장 큰 걸림돌이다.
High shipping costs remain the biggest obstacle to expanding into overseas markets.
words/#88-27/tip: 'an obstacle to + 명사/동명사'에서 to는 전치사라 동명사가 온다. overcome, remove와 짝을 이루며 barrier, hurdle로 패러프레이즈된다.
In 'an obstacle to + noun/gerund', to is a preposition, so a gerund follows. It pairs with overcome and remove and is paraphrased as barrier or hurdle.
words/#88-27/q/k: 관사 the와 형용사 main 뒤의 명사 자리이고 '~에 대한 장애물'이라는 뜻이므로 obstacle이 정답. obstruct는 동사, obstinate(고집 센)와 obsolete(구식의)는 형용사다.

The blank is a noun slot after the article the and the adjective main, meaning "a barrier to," so obstacle is correct. Obstruct is a verb, and obstinate (stubborn) and obsolete (outdated) are adjectives.
words/#88-28/exKo: 소음에 대한 불만이 계속되자 건물 관리인은 새 창문을 설치했다.
Persistent complaints about noise led the building manager to install new windows.
words/#88-28/tip: 문제·불만이 '계속되는'의 뜻과 사람·노력이 '끈질긴'의 뜻이 있으며, 동사 persist는 'persist in -ing'처럼 전치사 in과 쓰인다.
It means "ongoing" for problems and complaints and "determined" for people and efforts. The verb persist is used with the preposition in, as in 'persist in -ing'.
words/#88-28/q/k: 소유격 her와 명사 efforts 사이의 형용사 자리이므로 persistent가 정답. persist는 동사, persistence는 명사, persistently는 부사다.
The blank is an adjective slot between the possessive her and the noun efforts, so persistent is correct. Persist is a verb, persistence is a noun, and persistently is an adverb.
words/#88-29/m/0: too much; more than is reasonable
words/#88-29/exKo: 고객들은 항공편 날짜 변경에 붙는 과도한 수수료에 불만을 제기했다.
Customers complained about excessive fees for changing their flight dates.
words/#88-29/der/1/m: to go beyond; to be more than
words/#88-29/tip: 명사 excess('in excess of ~을 초과하여')와 동사 exceed를 함께 묻는 품사 문제가 나오며, noise, fees, use 등과 결합한다.
Part-of-speech questions test it along with the noun excess (as in 'in excess of', meaning more than) and the verb exceed. It combines with nouns like noise, fees, and use.
words/#88-29/q/k: 명사 use를 수식하는 형용사 자리이므로 Excessive가 정답. Exceed는 동사, Excessively는 부사, Excesses는 복수 명사다.
The blank is an adjective slot describing the noun use, so Excessive is correct. Exceed is a verb, Excessively is an adverb, and Excesses is a plural noun.
words/#88-30/m/0: 매우 귀중한, 값을 매길 수 없는
words/#88-30/exKo: 여러분의 의견은 우리가 고객 서비스를 개선하는 데 매우 귀중한 도움이 되었다.
Your feedback has been invaluable in helping us improve our customer service.
words/#88-30/tip: in-이 붙었지만 '가치 없는'이 아니라 '매우 귀중한'이라는 뜻이라 함정이 된다. 반의어는 worthless, valueless다.
It has the prefix in-, but it doesn't mean "worthless"; it means "extremely useful," which makes it a trap. Its opposites are worthless and valueless.
words/#88-30/q/k: 자원봉사자들의 도움이 '매우 귀중한' 것으로 드러났다는 뜻이므로 invaluable이 정답. invalid(무효인), inevitable(불가피한), inaccessible(접근할 수 없는)은 assistance를 설명하기에 맞지 않는다.

The volunteers' help turned out to be "extremely useful," so invaluable is correct. Invalid (not legally valid), inevitable (unavoidable), and inaccessible (unreachable) don't fit as descriptions of assistance.
words/#88-31/exKo: 새 행사장에는 참석자를 위한 주차 공간이 넉넉해서 카풀할 필요가 없다.
The new venue offers ample parking for attendees, so carpooling is not necessary.
words/#88-31/tip: 'ample + 불가산명사(ample time, ample parking)'로 자주 쓰여 plenty of, enough로 패러프레이즈되며, Part 7에서 '주차 공간이 충분하다' 같은 시설 장점 문제에 나온다.

It is often used as 'ample + uncountable noun' (ample time, ample parking), paraphrased as plenty of or enough. In Part 7 it appears in questions about a facility's advantages, such as having enough parking.
words/#88-31/q/k: 불가산명사 time을 수식할 수 있는 ample이 정답. numerous, many, several은 복수 가산명사와 쓰므로 '시간'이라는 뜻의 불가산명사 time 앞에 올 수 없다.
Ample can describe the uncountable noun time, so it is correct. Numerous, many, and several go with plural countable nouns, so they can't come before time, an uncountable noun here.
words/#88-32/m/0: following one after another; in a row
words/#88-32/exKo: 그 호텔은 5년 연속 지역 서비스상을 받았다.
The hotel has won the regional service award for five consecutive years.
words/#88-32/der/0/m: one after another, without a break
words/#88-32/tip: '숫자 + consecutive + 복수 명사(three consecutive years)' 또는 'for the third consecutive year' 형태로 쓰이며 in a row로 패러프레이즈된다.
It is used as 'number + consecutive + plural noun' (three consecutive years) or 'for the third consecutive year', and is paraphrased as in a row.
words/#88-32/q/k: 'for the fourth consecutive quarter(4분기 연속)'를 이루는 consecutive가 정답. constant(끊임없는), considerable(상당한), conservative(보수적인)는 서수와 함께 '연속'의 뜻을 만들지 못한다.

Consecutive forms 'for the fourth consecutive quarter' (four quarters in a row), so it is correct. Constant (continuous), considerable (large), and conservative (traditional; cautious) don't combine with an ordinal to mean "in a row."
words/#88-33/exKo: 그 박물관은 구조 보수 공사로 인해 당분간 문을 닫는다.
The museum will remain closed for the foreseeable future due to structural repairs.
words/#88-33/tip: 'for the foreseeable future(당분간)'와 'in the foreseeable future(가까운 장래에)'의 고정 표현으로 나오며, 반대 개념의 unforeseen(예기치 못한)과 구분해야 한다.
It appears in the set phrases 'for the foreseeable future' (for now) and 'in the foreseeable future' (soon), and should be told apart from its opposite unforeseen (unexpected).
words/#88-33/q/k: 'for the foreseeable future(당분간)'라는 고정 표현이므로 foreseeable이 정답. foreseen은 '예견된'이라는 과거분사로 future와 쓰지 않고, foresee는 동사, foresight는 명사다.

The set phrase is 'for the foreseeable future' (for now), so foreseeable is correct. Foreseen is a past participle meaning "predicted" and isn't used with future, foresee is a verb, and foresight is a noun.
words/#88-34/exKo: 투자자들은 합병이 임박했다는 보도에 긍정적으로 반응했다.
Investors reacted positively to reports that a merger was imminent.
words/#88-34/tip: 철자가 비슷한 eminent(저명한), prominent(두드러진)와 혼동시키는 어휘 문제가 나오며, impending, upcoming으로 패러프레이즈된다.
Vocabulary questions use the look-alikes eminent (famous; respected) and prominent (noticeable; important) as traps, and it is paraphrased as impending or upcoming.
words/#88-34/q/k: 제품 출시가 '임박해서' 마케팅팀이 초과 근무를 한다는 뜻이므로 imminent가 정답. eminent(저명한), prominent(두드러진), permanent(영구적인)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
With the product launch "about to happen," the team is working overtime, so imminent is correct. Eminent (famous), prominent (noticeable), and permanent (lasting forever) don't fit the meaning.
words/#88-35/exKo: Novak 씨는 현지 규정에 대한 지식 덕분에 프로젝트팀에 없어서는 안 될 인물이다.
Ms. Novak's knowledge of local regulations makes her indispensable to the project team.
words/#88-35/der/0/m: not necessary; easy to do without
words/#88-35/tip: 'indispensable to/for'처럼 전치사 to, for와 함께 쓰이며 essential, vital로 패러프레이즈된다. in-이 붙어 '없어도 되는'으로 오해하기 쉬운 단어다.
It is used with the prepositions to and for, as in 'indispensable to/for', and is paraphrased as essential or vital. Because of the prefix in-, it is easy to misread as "not needed."
words/#88-35/q/k: 재택근무자에게 안정적인 인터넷 연결은 '없어서는 안 될' 것이라는 뜻이므로 indispensable이 정답. unavoidable(불가피한), incapable(~할 수 없는), indifferent(무관심한)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.

A reliable internet connection is "absolutely necessary" for remote workers, so indispensable is correct. Unavoidable (impossible to prevent), incapable (unable), and indifferent (not interested) don't fit the meaning.
words/#88-36/exKo: 우리는 매달 모든 차량을 점검하여 정비에 선제적으로 대응한다.
We take a proactive approach to maintenance by inspecting all vehicles every month.
words/#88-36/tip: 문제가 생긴 뒤 대응하는 reactive와 반대로 '미리 대비하는'이라는 뜻이며 'take a proactive approach/steps' 형태로 자주 쓰인다.
It is the opposite of reactive (responding after a problem occurs), meaning "preparing in advance," and is often used as 'take a proactive approach/steps'.
words/#88-36/q/k: 불만이 접수되기를 기다리지 않는다고 했으므로 '선제적인'이라는 뜻의 proactive가 정답. reactive(사후 대응의)와 passive(수동적인)는 문맥과 반대이고, retroactive(소급 적용되는)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.

The team doesn't wait for complaints, so proactive (acting in advance) is correct. Reactive (responding after the fact) and passive (not acting) are the opposite of the context, and retroactive (applying to the past) doesn't fit the meaning.
words/#88-37/exKo: 면밀한 검토 결과, 소통 부족이 지연의 근본 원인이었던 것으로 드러났다.
A detailed review showed that poor communication was the underlying cause of the delays.
words/#88-37/der/0/m: to be the basis or cause of
words/#88-37/tip: 'underlying cause/problem/issue'처럼 명사 앞에서만 쓰이는 형용사로, root, fundamental로 패러프레이즈된다.
An adjective used only before nouns, as in 'underlying cause/problem/issue', and paraphrased as root or fundamental.
words/#88-37/q/k: 겉으로 드러난 증상은 고쳤지만 '근본적인' 문제는 남아 있다는 뜻이므로 underlying이 정답. undergoing(겪고 있는), understanding(이해심 있는), undertaking(착수하는; 사업)은 의미가 맞지 않는다.

The visible symptoms were fixed but the "root" problem remains, so underlying is correct. Undergoing (going through), understanding (sympathetic), and undertaking (taking on; a project) don't fit the meaning.
words/#88-38/m/0: common over a large area; extensive
words/#88-38/exKo: 새 모바일 뱅킹 앱은 고령 고객층에게도 폭넓게 받아들여졌다.
The new mobile banking app has gained widespread acceptance among older customers.
words/#88-38/tip: support, use, concern 같은 명사를 수식하는 형용사로, 동사·분사를 수식하는 부사 widely와 혼동시키는 품사 문제가 나온다.
An adjective that describes nouns like support, use, and concern. Part-of-speech questions use the adverb widely, which modifies verbs and participles, as a trap.
words/#88-38/q/k: 명사 support를 수식하는 형용사 자리이므로 widespread가 정답. widely는 부사, width는 명사, widen은 동사다.
The blank is an adjective slot describing the noun support, so widespread is correct. Widely is an adverb, width is a noun, and widen is a verb.
words/#88-39/exKo: 그 사무실은 여러 버스 노선과 가까워 직원들이 통근하기 편하다.
The office's proximity to several bus routes makes commuting easy for employees.
words/#88-39/tip: 'proximity to + 장소'와 'in close proximity to(~에 아주 가까이)'의 전치사 to가 출제 포인트이며, Part 7에서 close to, conveniently located로 패러프레이즈된다.
The test point is the preposition to in 'proximity to + place' and 'in close proximity to' (very near). In Part 7 it is paraphrased as close to or conveniently located.
words/#88-39/q/k: 전치사 to와 함께 '~와의 근접성'이라는 뜻을 이루는 proximity가 정답. location(위치), surroundings(주변 환경), approach(접근법)는 'close ~ to'와 결합해 '가까움'의 뜻이 되지 않는다.
Proximity forms "nearness to" with the preposition to, so it is correct. Location (place), surroundings (environment), and approach (method; way in) don't mean "nearness" in 'close ~ to'.
words/#88-40/exKo: 촉박한 마감일을 맞추기는 힘들었지만 팀은 보고서를 제때 제출했다.
Meeting the tight deadline was challenging, but the team delivered the report on time.
words/#88-40/tip: 사물이 '힘들게 만드는'이라는 능동 의미라 현재분사형 challenging을 쓰며, 'find + 목적어 + challenging' 구조에서 challenged와 구분하는 분사 문제가 나온다.
It has the active meaning "making things hard," so the present participle form challenging is used. Participle questions test it against challenged in the structure 'find + object + challenging'.
words/#88-40/q/k: 'find + 목적어 + 형용사' 구조에서 처음 몇 달이 '힘든' 것이므로 능동 의미의 challenging이 정답. challenged는 사람이 어려움을 겪는다는 수동 의미이고, challenge와 challenges는 명사·동사다.

In the structure 'find + object + adjective', the first few months are "difficult," so challenging, with an active meaning, is correct. Challenged has the passive meaning of a person facing difficulty, and challenge and challenges are nouns or verbs.
words/#89-01/exKo: 개막일 밤 좌석은 판매 시작 한 시간 만에 사실상 모두 팔렸다.
Virtually every seat for the opening night was sold within an hour of going on sale.
words/#89-01/tip: 'virtually all/every/no', 'virtually impossible'처럼 수량어나 형용사 앞에서 '거의'라는 뜻으로 쓰이며, almost, nearly로 패러프레이즈된다.
It means "almost" before quantity words or adjectives, as in 'virtually all/every/no' and 'virtually impossible', and is paraphrased as almost or nearly.
words/#89-01/q/k: 형용사 impossible을 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 virtually가 정답. virtual과 virtuous는 형용사, virtue는 명사다.
The blank is an adverb slot modifying the adjective impossible, so virtually is correct. Virtual and virtuous are adjectives, and virtue is a noun.
words/#89-02/exKo: 이 보고서의 수치는 추정치일 뿐이며 바뀔 수 있다.
The figures in this report are merely estimates and may change.
words/#89-02/tip: only, just와 같은 뜻으로 'not merely A but (also) B' 구문이 출제되며, 형용사 mere는 'a mere 5 percent'처럼 명사 앞에 온다.
It means the same as only or just, and the structure 'not merely A but (also) B' is tested. The adjective mere comes before nouns, as in 'a mere 5 percent'.
words/#89-02/q/k: 'not merely A but also B(A뿐만 아니라 B도)' 구문이므로 merely가 정답. mere는 형용사라 관사 앞에 올 수 없고, rarely(좀처럼 ~않는)와 nearly(거의)는 not ~ but also 구문을 이루지 못한다.

The structure is 'not merely A but also B' (not only A but also B), so merely is correct. Mere is an adjective and can't come before an article, and rarely (hardly ever) and nearly (almost) don't form the not ~ but also structure.
words/#89-03/exKo: 사물함에 둔 개인 소지품에 대한 책임은 전적으로 방문객에게 있다.
Visitors are solely responsible for any personal belongings left in the lockers.
words/#89-03/tip: 'be solely responsible for(전적으로 책임이 있다)'와 'based solely on(오로지 ~에 근거하여)'이 빈출이며, 형용사 sole(유일한)과의 품사 구분 문제로도 나온다.

The phrases 'be solely responsible for' (to be fully responsible for) and 'based solely on' (based only on) are common, and it also appears in part-of-speech questions against the adjective sole (only).
words/#89-03/q/k: 팀워크도 고려된다고 했으므로 '오로지 판매 실적 때문에만 주는 것은 아니다'라는 뜻의 solely가 정답. severely(심하게), scarcely(거의 ~않는), steadily(꾸준히)는 not ~ for와 의미가 맞지 않는다.

Teamwork is also considered, so the award is "not given only" for sales figures, and solely is correct. Severely (harshly), scarcely (hardly), and steadily (constantly) don't make sense with not ~ for.
words/#89-04/exKo: Lopez 씨는 바쁜 4분기에는 좀처럼 휴가를 내지 않는다.
Mr. Lopez seldom takes vacation during the busy fourth quarter.
words/#89-04/tip: 부정의 의미를 담고 있어 not과 함께 쓰지 않으며, 문장 맨 앞에 오면 'Seldom does the team miss ~'처럼 주어와 조동사가 도치된다.
It already has a negative meaning, so it isn't used with not. At the start of a sentence, the subject and auxiliary are inverted, as in 'Seldom does the team miss ~'.
words/#89-04/q/k: 문두에서 주어와 조동사의 도치(does the warehouse receive)를 일으키는 부정 부사 Seldom이 정답. Often, Usually, Sometimes는 문두에 와도 도치를 일으키지 않는다.

The negative adverb Seldom at the start of the sentence causes inversion of the subject and auxiliary (does the warehouse receive), so it is correct. Often, Usually, and Sometimes don't cause inversion even at the start of a sentence.
words/#89-05/exKo: 3층 회의실은 거의 사용되지 않으므로 언제든 예약해도 된다.
The conference room on the third floor is rarely used, so you may book it anytime.
words/#89-05/tip: seldom, hardly처럼 이미 부정의 뜻이 있어 not과 함께 쓰지 않으며, be동사·조동사 뒤나 일반동사 앞에 놓인다.
Like seldom and hardly, it already has a negative meaning, so it isn't used with not. It goes after a be verb or auxiliary, or before a main verb.
words/#89-05/q/k: 일반동사 requires를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 rarely가 정답. rare와 rarest는 형용사, rarity는 명사다.
The blank is an adverb slot modifying the main verb requires, so rarely is correct. Rare and rarest are adjectives, and rarity is a noun.
words/#89-06/exKo: 프런트에서 결제할 수 있다. 또는 앱으로 결제를 완료할 수도 있다.
You may pay at the front desk. Alternatively, you can complete payment through our app.
words/#89-06/der/1/m: to take turns; to switch back and forth
words/#89-06/tip: 앞 문장과 다른 '선택지'를 제시하는 접속부사라 Part 6 문장 연결 문제에 나온다. 부사이므로 두 절을 직접 연결할 수 없고 마침표나 세미콜론 뒤에 쓴다.

A conjunctive adverb that presents a different "option" from the previous sentence, so it appears in Part 6 sentence-connection questions. Because it is an adverb, it can't directly join two clauses; it follows a period or semicolon.
words/#89-06/q/k: 우편 제출에 이어 온라인 제출이라는 또 다른 방법을 제시하므로 Alternatively(또는)가 정답. Consequently(그 결과), Conversely(반대로), Nevertheless(그럼에도)는 앞뒤 관계와 맞지 않는다.

After mailing, the next sentence gives another option, submitting online, so Alternatively (or) is correct. Consequently (as a result), Conversely (on the other hand), and Nevertheless (even so) don't fit the relationship between the sentences.
words/#89-07/m/0: on the other hand; the other way around
words/#89-07/exKo: 히터 판매는 겨울에 늘고, 반대로 선풍기 판매는 여름철에 정점을 찍는다.
Sales of heaters rise in winter; conversely, fan sales peak in the summer months.
words/#89-07/tip: 앞 내용과 '정반대'인 경우를 연결하는 접속부사로 on the other hand, in contrast와 같은 역할을 한다. 단순히 다른 선택지를 제시하는 alternatively와 구분해야 한다.
A conjunctive adverb that links a case "exactly opposite" to the previous one, working like on the other hand or in contrast. Tell it apart from alternatively, which simply offers another option.
words/#89-07/q/k: 금리 인상 시 대출 감소와 금리 인하 시 대출 증가라는 정반대 관계를 연결하므로 conversely가 정답. therefore(그러므로)는 인과, moreover(게다가)는 추가, likewise(마찬가지로)는 유사 관계를 나타낸다.

The sentence links the exact opposite cases, borrowing falling when rates rise and rising when rates fall, so conversely is correct. Therefore (so) shows cause and effect, moreover (in addition) adds information, and likewise (in the same way) shows similarity.
words/#89-08/exKo: 베를린 지사는 에너지 사용량을 10퍼센트 줄였고, 파리 지사도 비슷한 성과를 냈다.
The Berlin office cut its energy use by 10 percent, and the Paris office performed similarly.
words/#89-08/tip: 접속부사로 앞 문장과 같은 내용을 덧붙일 때 likewise와 바꿔 쓸 수 있으며, 'similarly priced'처럼 분사를 수식하는 부사 자리에도 나온다.
As a conjunctive adverb that adds a matching point to the previous sentence, it can be swapped with likewise. It also appears in adverb slots modifying participles, as in 'similarly priced'.
words/#89-08/q/k: 과거분사 priced를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 similarly가 정답. similar는 형용사, similarity와 similarities는 명사다.
The blank is an adverb slot modifying the past participle priced, so similarly is correct. Similar is an adjective, and similarity and similarities are nouns.
words/#89-09/m/1: actually; as a matter of fact
words/#89-09/exKo: 새로운 매장 배치는 실제로 쇼핑객이 필요한 물건을 찾기 쉽게 만들었다.
The new store layout has indeed made it easier for shoppers to find what they need.
words/#89-09/tip: 앞 내용을 강조·확인하며 덧붙일 때 쓰는 부사로, Part 6에서 'Indeed, ~'는 앞 문장을 뒷받침하는 사실을 이끈다.
An adverb used to confirm or stress what came before. In Part 6, a sentence beginning with Indeed gives a fact that supports the previous sentence.
words/#89-09/q/k: 인기가 있을 것이라는 예상을 '실제로' 50석이 하루 만에 찼다는 사실로 확인하므로 indeed가 정답. instead(대신에), otherwise(그렇지 않으면), however(그러나)는 앞뒤 관계와 맞지 않는다.

The expectation that it would be popular is "actually" confirmed by all 50 seats filling in a day, so indeed is correct. Instead (in place of that), otherwise (if not), and however (but) don't fit the relationship between the ideas.
words/#89-10/exKo: 그 프로젝트의 성공은 주로 운영팀의 세심한 계획 덕분이었다.
The project's success was largely due to careful planning by the operations team.
words/#89-10/tip: '크게'가 아니라 '주로, 대체로'라는 뜻이라 mainly, primarily로 패러프레이즈되며, 'largely due to/because of'처럼 원인 표현 앞에 자주 온다.
It means "mainly, mostly," not "in a big way," so it is paraphrased as mainly or primarily. It often comes before cause expressions, as in 'largely due to/because of'.
words/#89-10/q/k: be동사와 명사구 the result 사이에서 '주로'라는 뜻으로 문장을 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 largely가 정답. large와 larger는 형용사, largeness는 명사다.
The blank is an adverb slot between the be verb and the noun phrase the result, meaning "mainly," so largely is correct. Large and larger are adjectives, and largeness is a noun.
words/#89-11/exKo: 실험실을 나가기 전에 모든 장비가 제대로 보관되었는지 확인해야 한다.
Make sure all equipment is properly stored before you leave the laboratory.
words/#89-11/tip: 'be properly installed/trained'처럼 be동사와 과거분사 사이, 또는 'work properly'처럼 자동사 뒤의 부사 자리를 묻는 문제가 나온다.
Questions test the adverb slot between a be verb and a past participle, as in 'be properly installed/trained', or after an intransitive verb, as in 'work properly'.
words/#89-11/q/k: 자동사 work를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 properly가 정답. proper는 형용사, property(재산, 부동산)와 propriety(예의 바름)는 명사다.
The blank is an adverb slot modifying the intransitive verb work, so properly is correct. Proper is an adjective, and property (possessions; real estate) and propriety (good manners) are nouns.
words/#89-12/exKo: 소포는 월요일에 발송되었으므로 아마 목요일까지는 도착할 것이다.
The package was sent on Monday, so it will presumably arrive by Thursday.
words/#89-12/tip: 근거를 바탕으로 '아마 ~일 것이다'라고 추측할 때 쓰는 문장 부사로 probably, likely로 패러프레이즈되며, 조동사와 본동사 사이 부사 자리로 출제된다.
A sentence adverb for making a reasonable guess, "probably ~," paraphrased as probably or likely. It is tested in the adverb slot between an auxiliary and the main verb.
words/#89-12/q/k: be동사와 전치사구 사이에서 '아마'라는 뜻으로 문장을 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 presumably가 정답. presume은 동사, presumed는 과거분사, presumption은 명사다.

The blank is an adverb slot between the be verb and the prepositional phrase, meaning "probably," so presumably is correct. Presume is a verb, presumed is a past participle, and presumption is a noun.
words/#89-13/exKo: 올해 무역 박람회 참석자 수는 예상보다 다소 적었다.
Attendance at this year's trade show was somewhat lower than expected.
words/#89-13/tip: 형용사·비교급 앞에서 '다소'라는 뜻으로 slightly, a little과 바꿔 쓸 수 있으며, 형태가 비슷한 some, something과 혼동시키는 문제가 나온다.
Before adjectives and comparatives it means "a bit" and can be swapped with slightly or a little. Questions use the look-alikes some and something as traps.
words/#89-13/q/k: 비교급 faster를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 '다소'라는 뜻의 somewhat이 정답. some은 명사를 수식하는 한정사, something은 대명사, sometime은 '언젠가'라는 시간 부사다.

The blank is an adverb slot modifying the comparative faster, meaning "slightly," so somewhat is correct. Some is a determiner that modifies nouns, something is a pronoun, and sometime is a time adverb meaning "at some point."
words/#89-14/m/0: in contrast; from another point of view
words/#89-14/exKo: 교외는 임대료가 더 저렴하지만, 반면에 통근 비용이 더 든다.
Rent is cheaper in the suburbs; on the other hand, commuting costs are higher.
words/#89-14/col/0/k: on the one hand ~, on the other hand ~
words/#89-14/tip: 앞 내용과 대조되는 내용을 이끄는 접속부사구라 절과 절을 직접 연결할 수 없다. 'on the one hand ~, on the other hand ~' 짝 구문에서 빠진 단어를 묻는 문제가 나온다.

A conjunctive adverbial phrase that introduces a contrasting point, so it can't directly join two clauses. Questions ask for the missing word in the paired structure 'on the one hand ~, on the other hand ~'.
words/#89-14/q/k: 'On the other hand(반면에)'라는 고정 표현이므로 hand가 정답. side, way, part는 on the other와 결합해 대조의 연결어를 만들지 않는다.
The set phrase is 'On the other hand' (in contrast), so hand is correct. Side, way, and part don't combine with on the other to form a contrast linker.
words/#89-15/m/0: by comparison; on the other hand
words/#89-15/exKo: 작년 회의에는 300명이 모였지만, 그에 반해 올해 행사에는 700명이 넘게 참석했다.
Last year's conference drew 300 people; in contrast, this year's event attracted over 700.
words/#89-15/tip: 단독으로는 접속부사처럼 쓰이고, 뒤에 명사가 오면 'in contrast to/with + 명사'처럼 전치사가 필요하다.
On its own it works like a conjunctive adverb, but when a noun follows, it needs a preposition, as in 'in contrast to/with + noun'.
words/#89-15/q/k: 뒤에 to + 명사가 이어지므로 'In contrast to(~와 대조적으로)'를 이루는 In contrast가 정답. Instead는 'instead of', Unlike는 전치사로 to 없이 명사를 취하고, Whereas는 절을 이끄는 접속사다.

To + noun follows, so In contrast, forming 'In contrast to' (unlike), is correct. Instead is used as 'instead of', Unlike is a preposition that takes a noun without to, and Whereas is a conjunction that introduces a clause.
words/#89-16/m/0: that is to say; to put it another way
words/#89-16/exKo: 2분기 매출이 두 배로 늘었다. 다시 말해 우리 광고 캠페인이 효과를 거두었다.
Sales doubled in the second quarter; in other words, our advertising campaign worked.
words/#89-16/tip: 앞 문장을 쉽게 바꿔 말하거나 요약할 때 쓰는 연결어로, Part 6에서 앞뒤 문장이 같은 내용을 다른 표현으로 말하고 있으면 정답이 된다.
A linking phrase used to restate or summarize the previous sentence more simply. In Part 6 it is the answer when two sentences say the same thing in different ways.
words/#89-16/q/k: 'in other words(다시 말해)'라는 고정 표현이므로 words가 정답. means, ways, points는 in other와 결합해 '바꿔 말하면'이라는 연결어를 만들지 않는다.
The set phrase is 'in other words' (that is to say), so words is correct. Means, ways, and points don't combine with in other to form a linker meaning "to put it another way."
words/#89-17/exKo: 보수 공사가 끝났으니 이제 그 카페는 손님을 최대 80명까지 수용할 수 있다.
Now that the renovation is complete, the café can seat up to 80 guests.
words/#89-17/tip: 접속사이므로 뒤에 주어와 동사가 있는 절이 온다. '이제 ~했으니'라는 이유를 나타내며, 같은 자리에 들어가는 전치사 because of, due to와 구분하는 문제가 나온다.
It is a conjunction, so a clause with a subject and verb follows. It gives a reason, "since ~ has now happened," and questions test it against the prepositions because of and due to in the same slot.
words/#89-17/q/k: 뒤에 주어와 동사가 있는 절(the merger has been finalized)이 오므로 접속사 Now that이 정답. Because of는 전치사, As soon은 as가 빠진 불완전한 형태, Even so는 부사구다.

A clause with a subject and verb (the merger has been finalized) follows, so the conjunction Now that is correct. Because of is a preposition, As soon is incomplete without as, and Even so is an adverbial phrase.
words/#89-18/exKo: 예산이 한정되어 있다는 점을 고려하면 웹사이트 개편은 미루는 것이 좋겠다.
Given that the budget is limited, we should postpone the website redesign.
words/#89-18/tip: 접속사로 뒤에 절이 오며, that 없이 given이 전치사처럼 명사를 이끌기도 한다(given the circumstances). considering that으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.
As a conjunction it is followed by a clause, and without that, given can also introduce a noun like a preposition (given the circumstances). It can be swapped with considering that.
words/#89-18/q/k: that절과 함께 '~을 고려하면'이라는 접속사를 이루는 Given이 정답. Despite와 Regarding은 that절을 바로 취하지 않는 전치사이고, Although는 접속사라 뒤에 that을 쓰지 않는다.

Given forms the conjunction "considering that" with a that-clause, so it is correct. Despite and Regarding are prepositions that don't take a that-clause directly, and Although is a conjunction, so that doesn't follow it.
words/#89-19/exKo: 그 호텔은 비쌌다. 그렇다 하더라도 대부분의 투숙객은 그만한 가치가 있다고 말했다.
The hotel was expensive. Even so, most guests said it was worth the price.
words/#89-19/tip: nevertheless와 같은 뜻의 접속부사구로 문장 앞에 쓰며, 접속사 even though(비록 ~이지만)와 달리 절을 직접 이끌 수 없다.
A conjunctive adverbial phrase meaning the same as nevertheless, used at the start of a sentence. Unlike the conjunction even though (although), it can't directly introduce a clause.
words/#89-19/q/k: 앞 문장과 대조되는 내용을 콤마 뒤 독립된 문장으로 연결하므로 접속부사구 Even so가 정답. Even though, Even if, As if는 접속사라 콤마로 끊어 단독으로 쓸 수 없다.

A contrasting point is linked as a separate sentence after a comma, so the adverbial phrase Even so is correct. Even though, Even if, and As if are conjunctions and can't stand alone followed by a comma.
words/#89-20/m/1: anyway; you have to remember that
words/#89-20/exKo: 일기 예보가 좋아져서 야외 콘서트는 결국 예정대로 열린다.
The outdoor concert will go ahead after all, since the forecast has improved.
words/#89-20/tip: 문장 끝에서는 '(예상과 달리) 결국'이라는 뜻이고, 문장 앞에서는 '어쨌든 ~이니까'처럼 이유를 덧붙이는 뜻이라 위치에 따라 의미가 달라진다.
At the end of a sentence it means "in the end (contrary to expectations)," and at the start it adds a reason, "anyway, because ~," so its meaning depends on its position.
words/#89-20/q/k: 예상과 달리 '결국' 제때 도착했다는 뜻이므로 'after all'을 이루는 all이 정답. at last(마침내)는 전치사 at과 쓰며, after whole, after most는 성립하지 않는다.

Contrary to expectations, the shipment arrived on time "in the end," so all, forming 'after all', is correct. At last (finally) uses the preposition at, and after whole and after most are not phrases.
words/#89-21/exKo: 지금까지 500명이 넘는 사람이 온라인 세미나에 등록했다.
So far, more than 500 people have registered for the online seminar.
words/#89-21/tip: 현재완료 시제와 함께 쓰이는 시간 표현으로, so far가 있으면 동사 자리에 have p.p.가 정답인 경우가 많다.
A time expression used with the present perfect, so when so far appears, have p.p. is often the answer for the verb slot.
words/#89-21/q/k: 현재완료와 함께 '지금까지'라는 뜻을 이루는 'so far'의 far가 정답. so long(오랫동안), so many(아주 많은), so near(아주 가까운)는 문맥과 문법에 맞지 않는다.
With the present perfect, far forms 'so far' (up to now), so it is correct. So long (for a long time), so many (a lot of), and so near (very close) don't fit the context or grammar.
words/#89-22/exKo: 새 지하철 노선은 의심할 여지 없이 도심 교통 체증을 줄일 것이다.
The new subway line will undoubtedly reduce traffic congestion downtown.
words/#89-22/der/0/m: uncertainty; feeling of not being sure
words/#89-22/tip: 조동사와 본동사 사이(will undoubtedly benefit)나 최상급 앞(undoubtedly the best)에 오는 부사 자리 문제가 나온다.
Questions test its adverb position between an auxiliary and the main verb (will undoubtedly benefit) or before a superlative (undoubtedly the best).
words/#89-22/q/k: be동사와 최상급 명사구 사이에서 '의심할 여지 없이'라는 뜻으로 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 undoubtedly가 정답. undoubted와 doubtful은 형용사, doubting은 현재분사다.

The blank is an adverb slot between the be verb and the superlative noun phrase, meaning "without question," so undoubtedly is correct. Undoubted and doubtful are adjectives, and doubting is a present participle.
words/#89-23/m/0: it seems; from what I've heard
words/#89-23/exKo: 듣자 하니 회의가 금요일로 옮겨졌다는데 아무도 영업팀에 알려 주지 않았다.
The meeting was apparently moved to Friday, but nobody informed the sales team.
words/#89-23/tip: '분명히'가 아니라 '(보거나 들은 바로는) ~인 것 같다'는 뜻이라 seemingly, reportedly로 패러프레이즈된다. 형용사 apparent(명백한)와 의미 차이에 주의한다.
It means "it seems (from what was seen or heard)," not "clearly," so it is paraphrased as seemingly or reportedly. Note the difference in meaning from the adjective apparent (clear).
words/#89-23/q/k: be동사와 과거분사 lost 사이에서 문장을 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 apparently가 정답. apparent는 형용사, appearance는 명사, appear는 동사다.
The blank is an adverb slot between the be verb and the past participle lost, modifying the sentence, so apparently is correct. Apparent is an adjective, appearance is a noun, and appear is a verb.
words/#89-24/exKo: 투표에 앞서 Adams 씨는 그 제안의 핵심 조건을 간단히 검토했다.
Before the vote, Mr. Adams briefly reviewed the key terms of the proposal.
words/#89-24/tip: 'briefly discuss/review'처럼 동사 앞이나 뒤의 부사 자리에 오며, 형용사 brief('a brief meeting')와 품사를 구분하는 문제가 나온다.
It comes in adverb slots before or after verbs, as in 'briefly discuss/review', and part-of-speech questions contrast it with the adjective brief ('a brief meeting').
words/#89-24/q/k: 조동사 will과 본동사 review 사이에서 동사를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 briefly가 정답. brief는 형용사, briefing은 명사·동명사, briefed는 과거분사다.
The blank is an adverb slot between the modal will and the main verb review, so briefly is correct. Brief is an adjective, briefing is a noun or gerund, and briefed is a past participle.
words/#89-25/exKo: 위치가 훌륭하므로 새 매장은 틀림없이 많은 손님을 끌어모을 것이다.
With its excellent location, the new store will certainly attract many customers.
words/#89-25/tip: Part 2에서 요청에 대한 긍정 응답 'Certainly.'로 자주 나오며, Part 5에서는 'almost certainly'처럼 조동사 뒤 부사 자리로 출제된다.
In Part 2 it often appears as a positive reply to a request, 'Certainly.' In Part 5 it is tested in the adverb slot after an auxiliary, as in 'almost certainly'.
words/#89-25/q/k: 조동사 will과 본동사 sell 사이에서 almost의 수식을 받는 부사 자리이므로 certainly가 정답. certain은 형용사, certainty는 명사, certify는 동사다.
The blank is an adverb slot between the modal will and the main verb sell, modified by almost, so certainly is correct. Certain is an adjective, certainty is a noun, and certify is a verb.
words/#89-26/exKo: 임대 계약서는 세입자가 아파트에서 반려동물을 기르는 것을 명시적으로 금지하고 있다.
The lease expressly prohibits tenants from keeping pets in the apartment.
words/#89-26/tip: 'expressly prohibited/forbidden'처럼 금지 문구와 계약서의 'unless expressly stated(명시되지 않는 한)'에 자주 쓰이며, explicitly로 패러프레이즈된다.
It is often used in prohibitions like 'expressly prohibited/forbidden' and in contracts as 'unless expressly stated' (unless clearly stated), and is paraphrased as explicitly.
words/#89-26/q/k: 과거분사 described를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 expressly(명시적으로)가 정답. express는 동사·형용사, expression은 명사, expressive는 형용사다.
The blank is an adverb slot modifying the past participle described, so expressly (explicitly) is correct. Express is a verb or adjective, expression is a noun, and expressive is an adjective.
words/#89-27/exKo: 우리 엔지니어들은 제품 품질을 유지하기 위해 공급업체와 긴밀히 협력한다.
Our engineers work closely with suppliers to maintain product quality.
words/#89-27/tip: 'work closely with(~와 긴밀히 협력하다)', 'closely monitor(면밀히 감시하다)'가 빈출이다. close도 부사로 쓰이지만 '가까이'라는 물리적 거리만 뜻하고 '긴밀히, 면밀히'의 뜻은 closely만 가능하다.

The phrases 'work closely with' (to cooperate tightly with) and 'closely monitor' (to watch carefully) are common. Close can also be an adverb, but it only means physical nearness; only closely means "tightly; carefully."
words/#89-27/q/k: 조동사 will과 본동사 monitor 사이에서 '면밀히'라는 뜻으로 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 closely가 정답. close는 '면밀히'라는 뜻의 부사로 쓰지 않으며, closing과 closure는 명사·분사라 동사를 수식할 수 없다.

The blank is an adverb slot between the modal will and the main verb monitor, meaning "carefully," so closely is correct. Close isn't used as an adverb meaning "carefully," and closing and closure are nouns or participles that can't modify a verb.
words/#89-28/exKo: 남은 예산은 세 부서에 균등하게 배분될 것이다.
The remaining budget will be divided equally among the three departments.
words/#89-28/der/0/m: the same (in size, value, or rights)
words/#89-28/tip: 'divided equally among(~에게 균등하게 나뉘다)', 'equally important(똑같이 중요한)'처럼 동사 뒤나 형용사 앞의 부사 자리를 묻는다.
Questions test adverb slots after verbs or before adjectives, as in 'divided equally among' (shared evenly between) and 'equally important' (just as important).
words/#89-28/q/k: 형용사 important를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 equally가 정답. equal은 형용사, equality는 명사, equalize는 동사다.
The blank is an adverb slot modifying the adjective important, so equally is correct. Equal is an adjective, equality is a noun, and equalize is a verb.
words/#89-29/exKo: 북부 교외의 주택은 젊은 가족에게 여전히 비교적 저렴하다.
Housing in the northern suburbs remains comparatively affordable for young families.
words/#89-29/der/2/m: judging how things are alike or different
words/#89-29/tip: relatively와 같은 뜻으로 형용사 앞에 쓰이며, 형용사 comparable(비슷한), comparative(비교의)와의 품사·의미 구분 문제가 나온다.
It means the same as relatively and is used before adjectives. Questions test the forms and meanings of the adjectives comparable (similar) and comparative (relative).
words/#89-29/q/k: 형용사 easy를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 comparatively가 정답. comparative와 comparable은 형용사, comparison은 명사다.
The blank is an adverb slot modifying the adjective easy, so comparatively is correct. Comparative and comparable are adjectives, and comparison is a noun.
words/#89-30/exKo: 호텔 신관에는 에너지 효율이 높은 조명이 완비되어 있다.
The hotel's new wing is fully equipped with energy-efficient lighting.
words/#89-30/tip: 'fully booked(예약이 다 찬)', 'fully refundable(전액 환불 가능한)'처럼 과거분사·형용사 앞의 부사 자리로 출제된다.
It is tested in adverb slots before past participles and adjectives, as in 'fully booked' (with no rooms left) and 'fully refundable' (100% refundable).
words/#89-30/q/k: 과거분사 booked를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 fully가 정답. full은 형용사, fullness는 명사, fill은 동사다.
The blank is an adverb slot modifying the past participle booked, so fully is correct. Full is an adjective, fullness is a noun, and fill is a verb.
words/#89-31/exKo: 지역 농장들은 가을 수확기에 계절 노동자에게 크게 의존한다.
Local farms rely heavily on seasonal workers during the autumn harvest.
words/#89-31/tip: 'rely heavily on', 'invest heavily in', 'heavily discounted'처럼 동사·분사와 결합하는 부사 자리 문제가 나온다.
Questions test the adverb slot combined with verbs and participles, as in 'rely heavily on', 'invest heavily in', and 'heavily discounted'.
words/#89-31/q/k: 과거분사 discounted를 수식해 '대폭 할인된'이라는 뜻을 이루는 부사 heavily가 정답. heavy는 형용사, heaviness와 heavyweight는 명사다.
The adverb heavily modifies the past participle discounted to mean "greatly reduced in price," so it is correct. Heavy is an adjective, and heaviness and heavyweight are nouns.
words/#89-32/exKo: 두 교육 세션은 A실과 B실에서 동시에 진행된다.
The two training sessions will run concurrently in Rooms A and B.
words/#89-32/tip: simultaneously와 같은 뜻으로 'run/take place concurrently'처럼 자동사 뒤에 쓰이며, 형용사 concurrent와의 품사 구분 문제가 나온다.
It means the same as simultaneously and is used after intransitive verbs, as in 'run/take place concurrently'. Part-of-speech questions contrast it with the adjective concurrent.
words/#89-32/q/k: 수동태 are held 뒤에서 동사를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 concurrently가 정답. concurrent는 형용사, concurrence는 명사, concur는 동사다.
The blank is an adverb slot modifying the verb after the passive are held, so concurrently is correct. Concurrent is an adjective, concurrence is a noun, and concur is a verb.
words/#89-33/m/0: by many people; over a large area
words/#89-33/exKo: Ahmed 씨는 공급망 관리 분야의 전문가로 널리 인정받는다.
Ms. Ahmed is widely regarded as an expert in supply chain management.
words/#89-33/der/0/m: broad; large from side to side
words/#89-33/tip: 'widely regarded/known/used'처럼 과거분사나 형용사 앞에 쓰여 '널리'를 뜻한다. wide도 부사로 쓰이지만 'wide open'처럼 물리적 폭에 한정된다.
It means "by many people" and is used before past participles or adjectives, as in 'widely regarded/known/used'. Wide is also an adverb, but it is limited to physical width, as in 'wide open'.
words/#89-33/q/k: 형용사 available을 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 widely가 정답. wide는 형용사(또는 물리적 의미의 부사), width는 명사, widen은 동사다.
The blank is an adverb slot modifying the adjective available, so widely is correct. Wide is an adjective (or an adverb with a physical meaning), width is a noun, and widen is a verb.
words/#89-34/exKo: Park 씨는 언제나 8시 전에 사무실에 도착한다.
Ms. Park invariably arrives at the office before eight o'clock.
words/#89-34/tip: always의 격식어로 '예외 없이 늘'이라는 뜻이며, in-이 붙어 '변하는'으로 착각하기 쉬운 단어다.
A formal word for always, meaning "every time, without exception." Because of the prefix in-, it is easy to mistake it for "changing."
words/#89-34/q/k: 주어와 동사 rank 사이에서 동사를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 invariably가 정답. invariable은 형용사, variance와 variety는 명사다.
The blank is an adverb slot between the subject and the verb rank, modifying the verb, so invariably is correct. Invariable is an adjective, and variance and variety are nouns.
words/#89-35/exKo: 귀하의 요청은 정식으로 접수되었으며, 곧 관리자가 연락할 것이다.
Your request has been duly noted, and a manager will contact you shortly.
words/#89-35/tip: 'duly noted', 'duly signed/authorized'처럼 과거분사 앞에서 '정식으로, 적절한 절차에 따라'라는 뜻이며, 형용사 due와 품사를 구분하는 문제로 나온다.
Before past participles, as in 'duly noted' and 'duly signed/authorized', it means "properly, following the correct procedure." Part-of-speech questions contrast it with the adjective due.
words/#89-35/q/k: 과거분사 signed를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 duly가 정답. due는 형용사, dues(회비)와 dueness는 명사다.
The blank is an adverb slot modifying the past participle signed, so duly is correct. Due is an adjective, and dues (membership fees) and dueness are nouns.
words/#89-36/exKo: 회사는 직원들이 온라인으로 휴가를 신청할 수 있는 제도를 도입했다.
The company introduced a system whereby employees can request leave online.
words/#89-36/tip: 'by which'와 같은 관계부사로 앞의 명사(system, agreement, process)를 설명하는 완전한 절을 이끈다. 뒤에 불완전한 절이 오는 관계대명사 which와 구분해야 한다.

A relative adverb meaning the same as 'by which', introducing a complete clause that describes the noun before it (system, agreement, process). Tell it apart from the relative pronoun which, which is followed by an incomplete clause.
words/#89-36/q/k: 뒤에 주어와 목적어를 갖춘 완전한 절(they will share research facilities)이 오므로 관계부사 whereby가 정답. which는 불완전한 절을 이끌고, whose는 뒤에 명사가 필요하며, what은 선행사를 취하지 않는다.

A complete clause with a subject and object (they will share research facilities) follows, so the relative adverb whereby is correct. Which introduces an incomplete clause, whose needs a noun after it, and what doesn't take an antecedent.
words/#89-37/exKo: 회원 가입 첫 달은 무료이고, 그 이후로는 20달러의 요금이 적용된다.
The first month of membership is free, and a fee of 20 dollars applies thereafter.
words/#89-37/tip: afterward와 같은 뜻의 격식어로 'shortly thereafter(그 직후)'처럼 쓰인다. 형태가 비슷한 thereby(그로 인해), therefore(그러므로)와 구분하는 어휘 문제가 나온다.
A formal word for afterward, used as in 'shortly thereafter' (soon after that). Vocabulary questions use the look-alikes thereby (as a result of that) and therefore (so) as traps.
words/#89-37/q/k: 처음 30일은 무료이고 '그 이후로는' 월 9.99달러라는 뜻이므로 thereafter가 정답. therefore(그러므로), thereby(그로 인해), therein(그 안에)은 시간 순서를 나타내지 않는다.
The first 30 days are free and the cost is $9.99 per month "after that," so thereafter is correct. Therefore (so), thereby (as a result of that), and therein (in that) don't show time order.
words/#89-38/exKo: 단 한 명의 지원자, 즉 Rossi 씨만이 모든 자격 요건을 충족했다.
Only one candidate, namely Ms. Rossi, met all of the job requirements.
words/#89-38/tip: 앞에서 말한 대상을 구체적으로 밝힐 때 쓰며 'two cities, namely Paris and Rome'처럼 콤마 뒤에 명사가 온다. 일부를 예로 드는 for example과 달리 해당 대상을 빠짐없이 밝힌다.
It is used to name exactly what was just mentioned, with nouns after a comma, as in 'two cities, namely Paris and Rome'. Unlike for example, which gives only some examples, it names all of the items.
words/#89-38/q/k: 앞의 two Asian cities가 구체적으로 어디인지 밝히므로 '즉'이라는 뜻의 namely가 정답. likewise(마찬가지로), otherwise(그렇지 않으면), instead(대신에)는 앞 명사를 구체화하지 못한다.
It specifies which two Asian cities are meant, so namely (that is) is correct. Likewise (similarly), otherwise (if not), and instead (in place of that) can't specify the noun before them.
words/#89-39/exKo: 여러 부서, 특히 마케팅과 영업 부서가 올해 목표를 초과 달성했다.
Several departments, notably marketing and sales, exceeded their targets this year.
words/#89-39/tip: 'most notably'처럼 여러 대상 중 특히 두드러진 것을 덧붙일 때 쓰여 particularly, especially로 패러프레이즈되며, 형용사 notable과의 품사 구분 문제가 나온다.
It adds a standout item from a group, as in 'most notably', and is paraphrased as particularly or especially. Part-of-speech questions contrast it with the adjective notable.
words/#89-39/q/k: most와 함께 '가장 두드러지게는'이라는 뜻으로 삽입구를 이끄는 부사 자리이므로 notably가 정답. notable은 형용사, notice는 명사·동사, noted는 과거분사다.
With most, the blank is an adverb slot leading an inserted phrase meaning "most especially," so notably is correct. Notable is an adjective, notice is a noun or verb, and noted is a past participle.
words/#89-40/m/0: according to reports; it is said
words/#89-40/exKo: 보도에 따르면 그 소매업체는 내년에 매장 20곳을 폐쇄할 계획이다.
The retailer is reportedly planning to close twenty stores next year.
words/#89-40/der/0/m: to tell (news); to give an account of
words/#89-40/tip: 확인되지 않은 보도 내용을 전할 때 쓰는 문장 부사로 according to reports로 패러프레이즈되며, be동사와 -ing/p.p. 사이의 부사 자리로 출제된다.
A sentence adverb for passing on unconfirmed reports, paraphrased as according to reports. It is tested in the adverb slot between a be verb and -ing/p.p.
words/#89-40/q/k: be동사와 전치사구 in talks 사이에서 '보도에 따르면'이라는 뜻으로 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 reportedly가 정답. reported는 'be reported to be'로 써야 하고, reporting과 reporter는 문맥에 맞지 않는다.

The blank is an adverb slot between the be verb and the prepositional phrase in talks, meaning "according to reports," so reportedly is correct. Reported must be used as 'be reported to be', and reporting and reporter don't fit the context.
words/#90-01/m/0: to be probably going to; to be expected to
words/#90-01/exKo: 축제 출연진이 발표되면 티켓 가격이 오를 가능성이 높다.
Ticket prices are likely to rise once the festival lineup is announced.
words/#90-01/tip: likely는 -ly로 끝나지만 형용사라 be동사 뒤에 오며 to부정사가 이어진다. 'be highly/more likely to'처럼 부사의 수식을 받는 형태로 출제된다.
Likely ends in -ly but is an adjective, so it comes after a be verb and is followed by a to-infinitive. It is tested with modifying adverbs, as in 'be highly/more likely to'.
words/#90-01/q/k: be동사 뒤 보어 자리에서 to부정사와 함께 '~할 것 같다'는 뜻을 이루는 형용사 likely가 정답. likelihood와 likeness는 명사이고, like는 to부정사와 이런 구조를 이루지 않는다.

In the complement slot after the be verb, the adjective likely forms "probably will" with the to-infinitive, so it is correct. Likelihood and likeness are nouns, and like doesn't form this structure with a to-infinitive.
words/#90-02/m/0: to come from; to use as a basis
words/#90-02/exKo: 연간 상여금은 각 직원의 성과 평가를 바탕으로 한다.
Annual bonuses are based on each employee's performance review.
words/#90-02/tip: 'be based on + 근거'와 'be based in + 장소(~에 본사를 두다)'의 전치사를 구분하는 문제가 빈출이다.
A common question tests the prepositions in 'be based on + grounds' and 'be based in + place' (to have headquarters in).
words/#90-02/q/k: 근거를 나타내는 'be based on(~에 근거하다)'이므로 on이 정답. 'be based in'은 '~에 본사를 두다'라는 장소 표현이고, at과 with는 based와 짝을 이루지 않는다.
To show grounds, the phrase is 'be based on' (to rest on), so on is correct. The phrase 'be based in' means "to have headquarters in" a place, and at and with don't pair with based.
words/#90-03/m/0: to formally request (a job, loan, permit)
words/#90-03/exKo: Silva 씨는 회사의 토론토 지사로 전근을 신청했다.
Mr. Silva applied for a transfer to the company's Toronto office.
words/#90-03/tip: 'apply for + 직책·대상(job, loan, permit)'과 'apply to + 기관·적용 대상'의 전치사를 구분하는 문제가 출제된다.
Questions test the prepositions in 'apply for + position or item (job, loan, permit)' and 'apply to + organization or thing affected'.
words/#90-03/q/k: 전치사 for와 함께 '~을 신청하다'라는 뜻을 이루는 자동사 apply가 정답. request, obtain, submit은 목적어를 바로 취하는 타동사라 for와 쓰지 않는다.
The intransitive verb apply forms "to request" with the preposition for, so it is correct. Request, obtain, and submit are transitive verbs that take a direct object and aren't used with for.
words/#90-04/exKo: 경비 보고서는 금요일까지 회계 부서에 제출하기 바란다.
Please hand in your expense reports to the accounting office by Friday.
words/#90-04/tip: submit, turn in과 같은 뜻으로 Part 7에서 서로 패러프레이즈된다. 목적어가 대명사일 때는 'hand it in'처럼 동사와 부사 사이에 넣는다.
It means the same as submit and turn in, which paraphrase each other in Part 7. When the object is a pronoun, it goes between the verb and the adverb, as in 'hand it in'.
words/#90-04/q/k: 'hand in(제출하다)'을 이루는 부사 in이 정답. at, for, by는 hand와 결합해 '제출하다'라는 뜻을 만들지 않는다.
The adverb in forms 'hand in' (to submit), so it is correct. At, for, and by don't combine with hand to mean "to submit."
words/#90-05/m/0: to deal with (work that has piled up)
words/#90-05/exKo: 지난주에 밀린 서류 작업을 처리하려고 오늘 밤 늦게까지 남아 있을 것이다.
I'm staying late tonight to catch up on paperwork I missed last week.
words/#90-05/tip: 'catch up on + 밀린 일(work, sleep, emails)'과 'catch up with + 사람·경쟁사(따라잡다)'의 전치사가 다르다는 점이 출제 포인트다.
The test point is the difference in prepositions between 'catch up on + backlog (work, sleep, emails)' and 'catch up with + person or competitor' (to reach the same level as).
words/#90-05/q/k: 밀린 일을 처리한다는 뜻의 'catch up on'이므로 on이 정답. 'catch up to'는 앞서가는 대상을 따라잡는다는 뜻이고, at과 for는 catch up과 짝을 이루지 않는다.
The meaning is dealing with a backlog, 'catch up on', so on is correct. The phrase 'catch up to' means reaching someone who is ahead, and at and for don't pair with catch up.
words/#90-06/exKo: 항공 교통 관제사 부족으로 여러 항공편이 지연되었다.
Several flights were delayed owing to a shortage of air traffic controllers.
words/#90-06/der/0/m: to need to pay back; to have thanks to
words/#90-06/tip: due to, because of와 같은 전치사구라 뒤에 명사가 오며, 절이 올 때는 'owing to the fact that'으로 써야 한다.
It is a prepositional phrase like due to and because of, so a noun follows. When a clause follows, you must write 'owing to the fact that'.
words/#90-06/q/k: 뒤에 명사구(a sudden drop in demand)만 있으므로 전치사구 Owing to가 정답. Because, Although, Since는 접속사로 쓰여 뒤에 절이 와야 한다.
Only a noun phrase (a sudden drop in demand) follows, so the prepositional phrase Owing to is correct. Because, Although, and Since are used as conjunctions and need a clause after them.
words/#90-07/exKo: 두 사무소 간의 데이터는 보안 네트워크를 통해 전송된다.
Data is transferred between the two offices by means of a secure network.
words/#90-07/tip: 수단·방법을 나타내는 전치사구로 means는 단수·복수 형태가 같다. 'by no means(결코 ~이 아닌)'와 의미가 전혀 달라 구분해야 한다.
A prepositional phrase showing method, and means has the same form in the singular and plural. Tell it apart from 'by no means' (not at all), which has a completely different meaning.
words/#90-07/q/k: 'by means of(~을 통해)'라는 고정 표현이므로 means가 정답. mean, meaning, meant는 by ~ of와 결합해 수단을 나타내지 못한다.
The set phrase is 'by means of' (through), so means is correct. Mean, meaning, and meant don't combine with by ~ of to show a method.
words/#90-08/exKo: 그 안전 캠페인은 지역 경찰서와 연계하여 진행되고 있다.
The safety campaign is being run in conjunction with the regional police department.
words/#90-08/tip: 전치사 in과 with를 묻는 문제가 나오며, together with, in partnership with로 패러프레이즈된다.
Questions test the prepositions in and with, and it is paraphrased as together with or in partnership with.
words/#90-08/q/k: 'in conjunction with(~와 연계하여)'라는 고정 표현이므로 with가 정답. to, for, by는 이 표현에 쓰지 않는다.
The set phrase is 'in conjunction with' (in cooperation with), so with is correct. To, for, and by aren't used in this phrase.
words/#90-09/exKo: 우리는 새 예산이 승인될 때까지 채용을 미루기로 했다.
We decided to hold off on hiring until the new budget is approved.
words/#90-09/tip: 'hold off on + 명사' 또는 'hold off + 동명사'로 써서 '(결정·행동을) 잠시 미루다'라는 뜻이며, put off, postpone으로 패러프레이즈된다.
It is used as 'hold off on + noun' or 'hold off + gerund', meaning "to put off (a decision or action) for a while," and is paraphrased as put off or postpone.
words/#90-09/q/k: 동명사 making과 함께 '~하는 것을 미루다'라는 뜻을 이루는 'hold off'의 off가 정답. hold up(지연시키다), hold out(버티다), hold back(억제하다)은 동명사를 바로 취해 '미루다'라는 뜻이 되지 않는다.

Off forms 'hold off' with the gerund making to mean "to delay doing," so it is correct. Hold up (to slow down), hold out (to last; to resist), and hold back (to restrain) don't take a gerund directly to mean "to delay."
words/#90-10/exKo: 그 호텔 식당은 다양한 현지 요리와 세계 요리를 제공한다.
The hotel restaurant serves a variety of local and international dishes.
words/#90-10/tip: 'a variety of + 복수 명사'로 쓰이며 various와 같은 뜻이다. 'a wide variety of'처럼 형용사 wide가 들어간 형태도 빈출이다.
It is used as 'a variety of + plural noun' and means the same as various. The form with the adjective wide, 'a wide variety of', is also common.
words/#90-10/q/k: 관사 a와 형용사 wide 뒤 명사 자리이고 'a wide variety of(매우 다양한)'를 이루므로 variety가 정답. various는 형용사, vary는 동사, variously는 부사다.

The blank is a noun slot after the article a and the adjective wide, forming 'a wide variety of' (a very wide range of), so variety is correct. Various is an adjective, vary is a verb, and variously is an adverb.
words/#90-11/exKo: 많은 직원이 새 주차 정책에 대해 문의했다.
A number of employees have asked about the new parking policy.
words/#90-11/tip: 'a number of + 복수 명사 + 복수 동사(많은 ~)'와 'the number of + 복수 명사 + 단수 동사(~의 수)'를 구분하는 수 일치 문제가 빈출이다.
A common subject-verb agreement question contrasts 'a number of + plural noun + plural verb' (many) with 'the number of + plural noun + singular verb' (the count of).
words/#90-11/q/k: 복수 가산명사 volunteers와 복수 동사 have가 이어지므로 'a large number of'의 number가 정답. amount와 deal은 불가산명사와 쓰고, level은 이 표현을 이루지 않는다.

The plural countable noun volunteers and the plural verb have follow, so number, from 'a large number of', is correct. Amount and deal are used with uncountable nouns, and level doesn't form this phrase.
words/#90-12/exKo: 출장 연회 음식에 관해서는 평이 좋은 지역 업체를 선정했다.
As for the catering, we have chosen a local company with excellent reviews.
words/#90-12/tip: 화제를 바꿔 새로운 대상을 꺼낼 때 문장 맨 앞에 쓰는 전치사구로 regarding, with regard to와 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.
A prepositional phrase used at the start of a sentence to switch to a new topic. It can be swapped with regarding or with regard to.
words/#90-12/q/k: 화제를 전환해 '~에 관해서는'이라는 뜻을 이루는 'As for'의 for가 정답. with, by, of는 as와 결합해 이런 뜻을 만들지 않는다.
For forms 'As for', meaning "regarding" when switching topics, so it is correct. With, by, and of don't combine with as to give this meaning.
words/#90-13/exKo: 그 회사는 이제 계절성 프로젝트에 정규직 대신 계약직 직원을 고용한다.
The firm now hires contract workers, as opposed to full-time staff, for seasonal projects.
words/#90-13/der/0/m: to be against; to object to
words/#90-13/der/1/m: completely different; on the other side
words/#90-13/tip: 'as opposed to'의 to는 전치사라 뒤에 명사나 동명사가 오며, rather than, instead of로 패러프레이즈된다.
The to in 'as opposed to' is a preposition, so a noun or gerund follows. It is paraphrased as rather than or instead of.
words/#90-13/q/k: 'as opposed to(~와는 대조적으로)'라는 고정 표현이므로 과거분사 opposed가 정답. opposite, opposing, opposition은 as ~ to와 결합해 이 표현을 이루지 않는다.
The set phrase is 'as opposed to' (in contrast to), so the past participle opposed is correct. Opposite, opposing, and opposition don't combine with as ~ to to form this phrase.
words/#90-14/m/0: when; no later than the moment that
words/#90-14/exKo: 고객이 도착했을 때는 이미 발표 슬라이드가 인쇄되어 있었다.
By the time the client arrived, the presentation slides had been printed.
words/#90-14/tip: 접속사로 뒤에 절이 오며, 주절에는 과거완료(had p.p.)나 미래완료(will have p.p.)가 자주 함께 쓰인다. 시간 부사절이라 미래의 일도 현재 시제로 쓴다.

It is a conjunction followed by a clause, and the main clause often uses the past perfect (had p.p.) or future perfect (will have p.p.). Because it introduces a time clause, future events are written in the present tense.
words/#90-14/q/k: 절을 이끄는 접속사 'By the time(~할 때쯤에는)'을 이루는 time이 정답. while과 during은 the 뒤에 올 수 없고, period는 by the와 결합해 접속사 역할을 하지 못한다.
Time forms the conjunction 'By the time' (when), which introduces a clause, so it is correct. While and during can't come after the, and period doesn't combine with by the to work as a conjunction.
words/#90-15/exKo: 이사회는 원래 디자인을 거부하고 더 단순하고 저렴한 디자인을 택했다.
The board rejected the original design in favor of a simpler, less expensive one.
words/#90-15/col/2/k: reject A in favor of B
words/#90-15/tip: 'vote in favor of(~에 찬성하다)'가 빈출이며, 'abandon A in favor of B(B를 택하고 A를 버리다)'처럼 선택의 뜻으로도 쓰인다.
The phrase 'vote in favor of' (to vote for) is common, and it is also used to show a choice, as in 'abandon A in favor of B' (to drop A and choose B instead).
words/#90-15/q/k: 'vote in favor of(~에 찬성 투표하다)'를 이루는 명사 favor가 정답. favorable, favorite, favored는 형용사·분사라 in과 of 사이의 명사 자리에 올 수 없다.
The noun favor forms 'vote in favor of' (to vote for), so it is correct. Favorable, favorite, and favored are adjectives or participles and can't fill the noun slot between in and of.
words/#90-16/exKo: 그 회사의 이익은 분석가들의 예상에 부합하게 증가했다.
The company's profits rose in line with analysts' expectations.
words/#90-16/col/2/k: bring A into line with B
words/#90-16/tip: 'in line with expectations/regulations'처럼 기준과의 일치를 나타내며 in accordance with, consistent with로 패러프레이즈된다.
It shows agreement with a standard, as in 'in line with expectations/regulations', and is paraphrased as in accordance with or consistent with.
words/#90-16/q/k: 'in line with(~에 맞춰)'라는 고정 표현이므로 in이 정답. on, at, by는 line with와 결합해 '~에 맞춰'라는 뜻을 만들지 않는다.
The set phrase is 'in line with' (matching), so in is correct. On, at, and by don't combine with line with to mean "matching."
words/#90-17/exKo: 에너지 효율이 높은 창문은 처음에는 더 비싸지만 장기적으로는 돈을 절약해 준다.
Energy-efficient windows cost more at first but save money in the long run.
words/#90-17/tip: '처음에는 ~하지만 장기적으로는'이라는 대비 문맥에 자주 나오며, in the long term, over time으로 패러프레이즈된다.
It often appears in contrasts like "at first ~, but over time," and is paraphrased as in the long term or over time.
words/#90-17/q/k: 'in the long run(장기적으로)'이라는 고정 표현이므로 run이 정답. in the long way, in the long time, in the long walk는 성립하지 않는다.
The set phrase is 'in the long run' (over time), so run is correct. In the long way, in the long time, and in the long walk are not phrases.
words/#90-18/m/0: currently doing; in the middle of
words/#90-18/exKo: We are in the process of updating our customer database.
words/#90-18/tip: 'be in the process of + 동명사'로 진행 중인 일을 나타내며, 전치사 of 뒤에 동사원형이 올 수 없다는 점이 출제된다.
It describes something in progress as 'be in the process of + gerund', and questions test the point that a base verb can't follow the preposition of.
words/#90-18/q/k: 'in the process of -ing(~하는 중인)'라는 고정 표현이므로 process가 정답. progress는 'in progress(진행 중인)'로 쓰고, procedure(절차)와 proceeds(수익금)는 이 표현에 쓰지 않는다.

The set phrase is 'in the process of -ing' (currently doing), so process is correct. Progress is used as 'in progress' (ongoing), and procedure (set of steps) and proceeds (money raised) aren't used in this phrase.
words/#90-19/exKo: 수요 증가를 고려해 공장은 야간 근무조를 추가할 것이다.
In view of the rising demand, the factory will add a night shift.
words/#90-19/col/0/k: in view of the fact that
words/#90-19/tip: in light of, considering과 같은 뜻의 전치사구로 뒤에 명사가 오며, 'in view of the fact that + 절'로도 쓴다. 'with a view to -ing(~할 목적으로)'와 혼동하지 않아야 한다.

A prepositional phrase meaning the same as in light of and considering, followed by a noun. It is also used as 'in view of the fact that + clause'. Don't confuse it with 'with a view to -ing' (in order to).
words/#90-19/q/k: 'In view of(~을 고려하여)'라는 고정 표현이므로 view가 정답. sight, vision, scene은 in ~ of와 결합해 '~을 고려하여'라는 뜻을 만들지 않는다.
The set phrase is 'In view of' (considering), so view is correct. Sight, vision, and scene don't combine with in ~ of to mean "considering."
words/#90-20/exKo: 모든 직원은 이전 경력과 관계없이 동일한 교육을 받는다.
All employees receive the same training, irrespective of their previous experience.
words/#90-20/tip: regardless of와 같은 뜻의 전치사구로 뒤에 명사나 whether절이 온다. regardless와 달리 of 없이 단독 부사로 쓰지 않는다.
A prepositional phrase meaning the same as regardless of, followed by a noun or a whether clause. Unlike regardless, it isn't used alone as an adverb without of.
words/#90-20/q/k: of와 함께 '~와 관계없이'라는 뜻을 이루는 irrespective가 정답. irrelevant는 'irrelevant to(~와 무관한)'로 쓰고, respective(각각의)와 respectively(각각)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.

Irrespective forms "regardless of" with of, so it is correct. Irrelevant is used as 'irrelevant to' (unrelated to), and respective (each one's own) and respectively (in the order given) don't fit the meaning.
words/#90-21/exKo: 대체로 고객들은 새로 디자인된 웹사이트에 만족했다.
On the whole, customers were satisfied with the redesigned website.
words/#90-21/tip: overall, in general과 같은 뜻의 부사구로 문장 앞에 쓰이며, 'as a whole(전체로서)'과 의미·전치사가 다르다.
An adverbial phrase meaning the same as overall and in general, used at the start of a sentence. It differs in meaning and preposition from 'as a whole' (as a complete unit).
words/#90-21/q/k: 'On the whole(대체로)'이라는 고정 표현이므로 whole이 정답. all, total, entire는 on the와 결합해 '대체로'라는 뜻을 만들지 않는다.
The set phrase is 'On the whole' (overall), so whole is correct. All, total, and entire don't combine with on the to mean "overall."
words/#90-22/exKo: 웹사이트의 연락처 목록은 오래되어 수정해야 한다.
The contact list on the website is out of date and needs to be revised.
words/#90-22/tip: 명사 앞에서는 'out-of-date information'처럼 하이픈을 넣고, 반대말 up to date(최신의)와 함께 출제된다.
Before a noun it takes hyphens, as in 'out-of-date information', and it is tested together with its opposite up to date (current).
words/#90-22/q/k: 수치를 업데이트해야 한다고 했으므로 'out of date(오래된)'의 date가 정답. out of time(시간이 없는), out of stock(품절된), out of reach(손이 닿지 않는)는 문맥에 맞지 않는다.
The figures need updating, so date, from 'out of date' (old), is correct. Out of time (with no time left), out of stock (sold out), and out of reach (too far to touch) don't fit the context.
words/#90-23/exKo: 최근 문의와 관련하여, 요청한 상품이 다시 입고되었다.
With respect to your recent inquiry, the item you requested is now back in stock.
words/#90-23/tip: with regard to, regarding과 같은 뜻의 전치사구이며, 형태가 비슷한 respective(각각의), respectively(각각)와 혼동시키는 문제가 나온다.
A prepositional phrase meaning the same as with regard to and regarding. Questions use the look-alikes respective (each one's own) and respectively (in the order given) as traps.
words/#90-23/q/k: 'with respect to(~에 관하여)'를 이루는 명사 respect가 정답. respective와 respectful은 형용사, respectively는 부사라 with와 to 사이에 올 수 없다.
The noun respect forms 'with respect to' (regarding), so it is correct. Respective and respectful are adjectives, and respectively is an adverb, so they can't go between with and to.
words/#90-24/exKo: 구내식당은 쓰레기를 줄이기 위해 더 이상 플라스틱 빨대를 제공하지 않는다.
In an effort to reduce waste, the cafeteria no longer provides plastic straws.
words/#90-24/tip: in order to처럼 목적을 나타내며 뒤에 동사원형이 온다. effort 앞의 관사 an과 전치사 in이 빠지거나 형태가 비슷한 effect로 바꾼 오답이 출제된다.
Like in order to, it shows purpose and is followed by a base verb. Wrong options drop the article an or the preposition in, or swap effort for the look-alike effect.
words/#90-24/q/k: 'In an effort to(~하기 위해)'라는 고정 표현이므로 effort가 정답. effect(효과), affair(일, 사건), efficiency(효율)는 이 표현을 이루지 않는다.
The set phrase is 'In an effort to' (in order to), so effort is correct. Effect (result), affair (matter; event), and efficiency (productivity) don't form this phrase.
words/#90-25/m/0: to take part in; to be part of
words/#90-25/exKo: Gupta 씨는 내년 영업 회의 기획에 참여하고 있다.
Ms. Gupta is involved in planning next year's sales conference.
words/#90-25/tip: 'be involved in + 명사/동명사'의 전치사 in이 출제 포인트이며, actively, directly 같은 부사가 be동사와 involved 사이에 들어간다.
The test point is the preposition in in 'be involved in + noun/gerund', and adverbs like actively and directly go between the be verb and involved.
words/#90-25/q/k: 'be involved in(~에 참여하다)'이므로 in이 정답. at, for, to는 involved와 짝을 이루어 '참여하다'라는 뜻을 만들지 않는다.
The phrase is 'be involved in' (to take part in), so in is correct. At, for, and to don't pair with involved to mean "to take part."
words/#90-26/exKo: 그 도시는 역사적인 건축물과 매년 열리는 재즈 축제로 유명하다.
The town is known for its historic architecture and annual jazz festival.
words/#90-26/tip: 'be known for + 이유(~로 유명하다)', 'be known as + 자격·명칭(~로 알려지다)', 'be known to + 대상(~에게 알려지다)'의 전치사를 구분하는 문제가 빈출이다.
A common question tests the prepositions in 'be known for + reason' (to be famous for), 'be known as + title or role' (to be called), and 'be known to + people' (to be familiar to).
words/#90-26/q/k: 옥상 정원과 전망이 유명한 '이유'이므로 'be known for'의 for가 정답. 'known as'는 명칭·자격, 'known to'는 알고 있는 대상과 쓰며, by는 이 의미로 쓰지 않는다.

The rooftop garden and views are the "reason" the hotel is famous, so for, from 'be known for', is correct. Known as goes with a name or role, known to goes with the people who know it, and by isn't used with this meaning.
words/#90-27/m/0: to be ready or happy to (do)
words/#90-27/exKo: 건물주는 우리가 3년 임대 계약을 맺으면 임대료를 낮춰 줄 의향이 있다.
The landlord is willing to reduce the rent if we sign a three-year lease.
words/#90-27/der/0/m: readiness; being happy to do something
words/#90-27/tip: 'be willing to + 동사원형'으로 쓰이며 명사 willingness('willingness to compromise')도 품사 문제로 나온다. 반대말은 be reluctant to, be unwilling to다.
It is used as 'be willing to + base verb', and the noun willingness ('willingness to compromise') also appears in part-of-speech questions. The opposites are be reluctant to and be unwilling to.
words/#90-27/q/k: be동사 뒤 보어 자리에서 to부정사와 함께 '기꺼이 ~하다'라는 뜻을 이루는 형용사 willing이 정답. willingly는 부사, willingness와 will은 명사다.
In the complement slot after the be verb, the adjective willing forms "to be ready to do" with the to-infinitive, so it is correct. Willingly is an adverb, and willingness and will are nouns.
words/#90-28/exKo: 그 회사의 전기 트럭은 한 번 충전으로 300킬로미터를 주행할 수 있다.
The company's electric trucks are capable of traveling 300 kilometers on a single charge.
words/#90-28/der/1/m: maximum amount something can hold; ability
words/#90-28/tip: 'be capable of + 동명사'로 쓰여 'be able to + 동사원형'과 형태를 혼동시키는 문제가 나온다.
It is used as 'be capable of + gerund', and questions try to confuse it with the form 'be able to + base verb'.
words/#90-28/q/k: 전치사 of와 동명사(handling)를 취해 '~할 수 있다'라는 뜻을 이루는 capable이 정답. able은 'be able to do'로 쓰고, possible과 available은 사람·사물의 능력을 나타내는 of -ing 구조를 취하지 않는다.

Capable takes the preposition of and a gerund (handling) to mean "to be able to," so it is correct. Able is used as 'be able to do', and possible and available don't take the of -ing structure to show ability.
words/#90-29/m/0: to focus on; to notice carefully
words/#90-29/exKo: 기계를 작동하기 전에 안전 수칙에 각별히 주의를 기울이기 바란다.
Please pay close attention to the safety instructions before operating the machine.
words/#90-29/tip: 'pay attention to + 명사/동명사'의 to는 전치사이며, close, special, particular 같은 형용사가 attention 앞에 들어간다.
The to in 'pay attention to + noun/gerund' is a preposition, and adjectives like close, special, and particular go before attention.
words/#90-29/q/k: 형용사 particular의 수식을 받는 명사 자리이고 'pay attention to'를 이루므로 attention이 정답. attentive는 형용사, attend는 동사, attentively는 부사다.
The blank is a noun slot modified by the adjective particular, forming 'pay attention to', so attention is correct. Attentive is an adjective, attend is a verb, and attentively is an adverb.
words/#90-30/m/0: to depend on; to be conditional on
words/#90-30/exKo: 채용 제안은 신원 조회를 무사히 통과하는 것을 조건으로 한다.
The job offer is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check.
words/#90-30/tip: depend on, be subject to와 같은 뜻으로 upon 대신 on도 쓰며, 명사 contingency('contingency plan 비상 계획')도 출제된다.
It means the same as depend on and be subject to, and on can be used instead of upon. The noun contingency ('contingency plan', a backup plan) is also tested.
words/#90-30/q/k: upon과 함께 '~에 달려 있다'라는 뜻을 이루는 contingent가 정답. continuous(계속되는), constant(끊임없는), consistent(일관된)는 upon과 결합해 조건을 나타내지 않는다.
Contingent forms "to depend on" with upon, so it is correct. Continuous (ongoing), constant (unchanging), and consistent (reliable) don't combine with upon to express a condition.
words/#90-31/exKo: 등록한 참가자 중 절반만 오전 세션에 참석했다.
Only half of the registered participants showed up for the morning session.
words/#90-31/tip: arrive, turn up과 같은 뜻의 구동사로 듣기 파트에 자주 나오며 'show up for + 행사' 형태로 쓰인다. Part 7에서 attend, arrive로 패러프레이즈된다.
A phrasal verb meaning the same as arrive and turn up, common in the listening parts and used as 'show up for + event'. In Part 7 it is paraphrased as attend or arrive.
words/#90-31/q/k: 'show up(나타나다)'을 이루는 up이 정답. show off(자랑하다)는 의미가 맞지 않고, show out과 show over는 '도착하다'라는 뜻이 없다.
Up forms 'show up' (to arrive), so it is correct. Show off (to boast) doesn't fit the meaning, and show out and show over don't mean "to arrive."
words/#90-32/exKo: Hall 씨는 관리자가 자리를 비운 동안 추가 업무를 맡기로 했다.
Mr. Hall agreed to take on additional responsibilities while his manager is away.
words/#90-32/tip: 'take on responsibilities/a project'처럼 '맡다'의 뜻으로 assume, undertake로 패러프레이즈되며, '(직원을) 고용하다'의 뜻도 출제된다.
In the sense of "to accept," as in 'take on responsibilities/a project', it is paraphrased as assume or undertake. The meaning "to hire (staff)" is also tested.
words/#90-32/q/k: 새 고객을 '맡다, 받다'라는 뜻의 'take on'이므로 on이 정답. take off(이륙하다, 벗다), take out(꺼내다), take apart(분해하다)는 의미가 맞지 않는다.
The meaning is "to accept" new clients, 'take on', so on is correct. Take off (to leave the ground; to remove), take out (to remove), and take apart (to disassemble) don't fit the meaning.
words/#90-33/m/0: to prove to be; to end up being
words/#90-33/exKo: 새 마케팅 전략은 예상보다 더 효과적인 것으로 드러났다.
The new marketing strategy turned out to be more effective than expected.
words/#90-33/der/0/m: number of people attending or voting
words/#90-33/tip: 'turn out to be + 형용사/명사(~으로 판명되다)'가 빈출이며, 명사 turnout(참석자 수)은 'a large turnout'처럼 Part 7에 나온다.
The pattern 'turn out to be + adjective/noun' (to prove to be) is common, and the noun turnout (number of attendees) appears in Part 7, as in 'a large turnout'.
words/#90-33/q/k: to be와 함께 '~인 것으로 드러나다'라는 뜻을 이루는 'turn out'의 out이 정답. turn up(나타나다), turn into(~으로 변하다), turn over(뒤집다)는 to be와 이런 구조를 이루지 않는다.
Out forms 'turn out' with to be to mean "to prove to be," so it is correct. Turn up (to appear), turn into (to become), and turn over (to flip) don't form this structure with to be.
words/#90-34/exKo: 새 안전 규정은 모든 장비의 정기 점검을 요구한다.
The new safety regulations call for regular inspections of all equipment.
words/#90-34/tip: 사물 주어가 오면 require, necessitate(필요로 하다)의 뜻이고, 사람 주어면 '공개적으로 요구하다'의 뜻이 된다. 'call for proposals(제안서 모집)'도 빈출 표현이다.
With a non-human subject it means require or necessitate (to need), and with a person as subject it means "to demand publicly." The phrase 'call for proposals' (request for proposals) is also common.
words/#90-34/q/k: 조리법이 재료를 '필요로 하다'라는 뜻의 'call for'이므로 for가 정답. call on(방문하다, 요청하다), call up(전화하다), call in(불러들이다)은 의미가 맞지 않는다.
The recipe "needs" ingredients, which is 'call for', so for is correct. Call on (to visit; to ask), call up (to phone), and call in (to bring in) don't fit the meaning.
words/#90-35/exKo: 우리 기술자들이 24시간 이내에 대응할 것이라고 믿어도 좋다.
You can count on our technicians to respond within 24 hours.
words/#90-35/tip: rely on, depend on과 같은 뜻으로 'count on A to do', 'count on A for B' 구조를 취하며, 전치사 on이 빠지거나 바뀐 오답이 출제된다.
It means the same as rely on and depend on, taking the structures 'count on A to do' and 'count on A for B'. Wrong options drop or change the preposition on.
words/#90-35/q/k: 'count on A for B(B를 A에게 의지하다)'이므로 on이 정답. at, in, for는 count 뒤에서 '의지하다'라는 뜻을 만들지 않는다.
The structure is 'count on A for B' (to rely on A for B), so on is correct. At, in, and for don't follow count to mean "to rely on."
words/#90-36/exKo: 그 회사는 경비 절감을 위해 출장을 줄이고 있다.
The company is cutting back on business travel to reduce expenses.
words/#90-36/tip: reduce, curtail과 같은 뜻으로 Part 7에서 패러프레이즈되며, on이 빠지거나 바뀐 오답이 나온다. 명사 cutback(감축)은 주로 복수형으로 쓴다.
It is paraphrased in Part 7 as reduce or curtail, and wrong options drop or change on. The noun cutback (reduction) is mostly used in the plural.
words/#90-36/q/k: 'cut back on(~을 줄이다)'이므로 on이 정답. off, in, at은 cut back과 결합해 '~을 줄이다'라는 뜻을 만들지 않는다.
The phrase is 'cut back on' (to reduce), so on is correct. Off, in, and at don't combine with cut back to mean "to reduce."
words/#90-37/exKo: 많은 출장객이 단거리 항공편 대신 기차를 선택한다.
Many business travelers opt for trains instead of short-haul flights.
words/#90-37/tip: 'opt for + 명사'와 'opt to do' 두 형태로 쓰이고, 'opt out of(~에서 빠지다)'와 전치사를 구분한다. 형용사 optional(선택적인)이 품사 문제로 나온다.
It is used in two forms, 'opt for + noun' and 'opt to do'; tell its preposition apart from 'opt out of' (to choose not to take part). The adjective optional appears in part-of-speech questions.
words/#90-37/q/k: 전치사 for와 함께 '~을 선택하다'라는 뜻을 이루는 자동사 opt가 정답. choose, select, prefer는 목적어를 바로 취하는 타동사라 for와 쓰지 않는다.
The intransitive verb opt forms "to choose" with the preposition for, so it is correct. Choose, select, and prefer are transitive verbs that take a direct object and aren't used with for.
words/#90-38/exKo: 콜센터는 연휴 성수기에 대처하기 위해 직원을 추가로 고용했다.
The call center hired extra staff to cope with the holiday rush.
words/#90-38/tip: 자동사라 전치사 with가 반드시 필요하며, deal with, handle로 패러프레이즈된다.
It is intransitive, so the preposition with is always needed. It is paraphrased as deal with or handle.
words/#90-38/q/k: 전치사 with와 함께 '~에 대처하다'라는 뜻을 이루는 자동사 cope가 정답. handle, treat, address는 목적어를 바로 취하는 타동사라 with와 쓰지 않는다.
The intransitive verb cope forms "to deal with" with the preposition with, so it is correct. Handle, treat, and address are transitive verbs that take a direct object and aren't used with with.
words/#90-39/m/0: (of a plan or deal) to fail to happen; to collapse
words/#90-39/exKo: 두 회사가 가격에 합의하지 못하면서 합병은 무산되었다.
The merger fell through after the two companies failed to agree on a price.
words/#90-39/tip: 계획·거래가 '무산되다'라는 자동사구로 목적어를 취하지 않으며, Part 7에서 did not go through, was canceled로 패러프레이즈된다.
An intransitive phrasal verb meaning a plan or deal "fails to happen," so it takes no object. In Part 7 it is paraphrased as did not go through or was canceled.
words/#90-39/q/k: 구매자가 대출을 받지 못해 매매가 '무산되었다'는 뜻이므로 'fall through'의 through가 정답. fall behind(뒤처지다), fall off(떨어지다, 감소하다), fall down(넘어지다)은 의미가 맞지 않는다.
