The sale "collapsed" because the buyer couldn't get a loan, so through, from 'fall through', is correct. Fall behind (to lag), fall off (to drop; to decline), and fall down (to fall to the ground) don't fit the meaning.
words/#90-40/m/0: to exclude; to eliminate (as a possibility)
words/#90-40/exKo: 당국은 주차 요금 인상 가능성을 배제하지 않았다.
Officials have not ruled out the possibility of raising parking fees.
words/#90-40/tip: 'rule out the possibility of(~의 가능성을 배제하다)'가 빈출이며, exclude, eliminate로 패러프레이즈된다.
The phrase rule out the possibility of (= say something can't happen) is common, and it is often paraphrased as exclude or eliminate.
words/#90-40/q/k: 'rule out(배제하다)'이므로 out이 정답. 기술자들이 시스템 고장의 원인에서 소프트웨어 오류를 배제했다는 뜻이며, off, over, away는 rule과 결합해 '배제하다'라는 뜻을 만들지 않는다.
The phrasal verb rule out means "exclude," so out is correct. The technicians excluded a software error as the cause of the crash; off, over, and away don't combine with rule to mean "exclude."
part1/#p1-1/k: 서류철 몇 개가 책상 위에 쌓여 있다.
Some files are stacked on the desk.
part1/#p1-1/keyKo: piled one on top of another
part1/#p1-1/tip: 사물 상태는 'be + p.p.' 또는 'have been p.p.'로 묘사한다.
The state of objects is described with be + p.p. or have been p.p.
part1/#p1-2/k: 한 여자가 키보드로 타자를 치고 있다.
A woman is typing on a keyboard.
part1/#p1-2/keyKo: to enter text on a computer
part1/#p1-2/tip: 손 동작이 비슷한 'writing', 'using a mouse'와 바꿔 내는 오답에 주의한다.
Watch for wrong options that swap in a similar hand action, such as 'writing' or 'using a mouse'.
part1/#p1-3/k: A man is making a photocopy.
part1/#p1-3/tip: 같은 장면이 'using a copy machine', 'operating a photocopier'로도 나온다.
The same scene can also be described as 'using a copy machine' or 'operating a photocopier'.
part1/#p1-4/k: 한 남자가 선반 위 바인더를 향해 손을 뻗고 있다.
A man is reaching for a binder on the shelf.
part1/#p1-4/keyKo: to stretch out a hand to grab
part1/#p1-4/tip: reach for는 아직 잡지 않은 상태다. 이미 손에 쥐고 있으면 'holding'이 정답이다.
With reach for, the person hasn't grabbed it yet. If it's already in their hand, 'holding' is the answer.
part1/#p1-5/k: 한 여자가 전화 통화를 하고 있다.
A woman is talking on the phone.
part1/#p1-5/tip: 수화기를 귀에 대고 있을 때만 정답이다. 전화기가 책상 위에 놓여 있기만 하면 오답.
It is correct only when the receiver is at the person's ear. If the phone is just sitting on the desk, it's wrong.
part1/#p1-6/k: The man is looking at a monitor.
part1/#p1-6/tip: 시선이 어디를 향하는지 확인하자. looking at, staring at, gazing at 모두 '보다'.
Check where the person's eyes are directed. Looking at, staring at, and gazing at all mean "to look."
part1/#p1-7/k: 서류 몇 장이 책상 여기저기에 흩어져 있다.
Some papers are scattered across the desk.
part1/#p1-7/tip: scattered는 정돈되지 않은 상태, stacked·piled는 쌓여 있는 상태로 구분한다.
Tell them apart: scattered means messy and spread out, while stacked and piled mean placed in a pile.
part1/#p1-8/k: 서류 캐비닛 서랍이 열린 채로 있다.
A file cabinet drawer has been left open.
part1/#p1-8/tip: 'be left + 형용사/p.p.'는 사물 상태를 묘사하는 단골 표현이다.
The pattern be left + adjective/p.p. is a regular way to describe the state of an object.
part1/#p1-9/k: The woman is filing some documents.
part1/#p1-9/keyKo: to put papers away in order
part1/#p1-9/tip: 명사 file(서류철)뿐 아니라 동사 file(철하다, 정리해 넣다)도 함께 기억하자.
Remember the verb file (to put papers away in order) as well as the noun file (a folder of papers).
part1/#p1-10/k: 한 여자가 메모장에 무언가를 적고 있다.
A woman is writing on a notepad.
part1/#p1-10/keyKo: to jot something down on a pad
part1/#p1-10/tip: writing과 reading처럼 손과 시선의 동작을 비교해 고르게 하는 문제가 많다.
Many questions make you compare hand and eye actions, such as writing vs. reading.
part1/#p1-11/k: Some of the chairs are unoccupied.
part1/#p1-11/tip: occupied(사용 중인) ↔ unoccupied·empty·vacant(비어 있는). 사람이 없는 사진의 정답으로 자주 나온다.
Occupied (in use) ↔ unoccupied, empty, vacant (not in use). This is a common correct answer for photos with no people.
part1/#p1-12/k: 한 남자가 전선을 콘센트에 꽂고 있다.
A man is plugging a cord into an outlet.
part1/#p1-12/keyKo: to connect A to B (by inserting the end)
part1/#p1-12/tip: An outlet is a wall socket for electricity, and it often appears in Part 1.
part1/#p1-13/keyKo: to be getting fixed right now
part1/#p1-13/tip: 'is being p.p.'(진행 수동태)는 지금 누군가 그 동작을 하고 있다는 뜻이다. 수리하는 사람이 사진에 있어야 정답이고, 사람 없이 복사기만 있으면 오답이다.
The present progressive passive is being p.p. means someone is doing the action right now. It is correct only if someone is fixing it in the photo; a copier on its own makes it wrong.
part1/#p1-14/k: 한 남자가 의자에 등을 기대고 있다.
A man is leaning back in his chair.
part1/#p1-14/keyKo: to sit back against a chair
part1/#p1-14/tip: lean back(뒤로 기대다)과 lean forward(앞으로 숙이다)의 방향을 구분해 듣자.
Listen for the direction: lean back (tilt backward) vs. lean forward (bend toward the front).
part1/#p1-15/k: The woman is wearing a headset.
part1/#p1-15/tip: wearing은 착용한 상태, putting on은 착용하는 동작이다. 사진에서는 대부분 wearing이 정답이다.
Wearing is the state of having something on; putting on is the action of dressing. In photos, wearing is usually the answer.
part1/#p1-16/k: 상품 몇 개가 가게 진열창에 진열되어 있다.
Some merchandise is displayed in a store window.
part1/#p1-16/keyKo: to be set out for people to see
part1/#p1-16/tip: 'on display'도 같은 뜻이다. 예외적으로 'is being displayed'는 사람이 없어도 정답이 될 수 있다.
The phrase 'on display' means the same. As an exception, 'is being displayed' can be correct even with no people in the photo.
part1/#p1-17/k: 한 손님이 옷걸이에 걸린 옷들을 둘러보고 있다.
A customer is browsing through a rack of clothing.
part1/#p1-17/tip: browse는 '이것저것 구경하다'라는 뜻으로 매장 사진의 단골 동사다.
Browse means to look casually at various items, and it is a regular verb in store photos.
part1/#p1-18/k: 한 남자가 재킷을 입어 보고 있다.
A man is trying on a jacket.
part1/#p1-18/keyKo: to put on (clothes) to check the fit
part1/#p1-18/tip: try on은 입어 보는 동작이다. 거울 앞에서 옷을 걸쳐 보는 장면에 주로 나온다.
Try on is the action of testing clothes. It usually appears in scenes of someone holding clothes up in front of a mirror.
part1/#p1-19/tip: 'is being p.p.'(진행 수동태)는 지금 누군가 그 동작을 하고 있다는 뜻이다. 직원이 물건을 채우는 모습이 보여야 정답이다. 이미 다 채워진 선반이면 'The shelves are stocked.'

The present progressive passive is being p.p. means someone is doing the action right now. A worker filling the shelves must be visible. If the shelves are already full, it's 'The shelves are stocked.'
part1/#p1-20/k: The shelves are stocked with canned goods.
part1/#p1-20/keyKo: to be filled with; to hold a supply of
part1/#p1-20/tip: 사람이 없는 진열대 사진이라면 being이 없는 상태 수동태가 정답이다.
In a photo of shelves with no people, the stative passive without being is the answer.
part1/#p1-21/k: 한 쇼핑객이 통로를 따라 카트를 밀고 있다.
A shopper is pushing a cart down an aisle.
part1/#p1-21/tip: In aisle (a walkway between shelves), the s is silent: /aɪl/, the same sound as I'll.
part1/#p1-22/k: 한 손님이 계산대에서 물건값을 계산하고 있다.
A customer is paying for some items at the counter.
part1/#p1-22/keyKo: to give money for; to buy
part1/#p1-22/tip: 계산대 장면에서는 cashier(계산원), register(금전 등록기)도 함께 나온다.
Checkout scenes also feature cashier (person who takes payment) and register (cash machine).
part1/#p1-23/k: A server is pouring water into a glass.
part1/#p1-23/tip: pour[포어]의 발음을 익혀 두자. pouring과 drinking을 바꿔 내는 오답에 주의한다.
Learn how to say pour: /pɔːr/, like "poor" or "pore." Watch for wrong options that swap pouring with drinking.
part1/#p1-24/k: A customer is reading a menu.
part1/#p1-24/keyKo: to look over the list of dishes
part1/#p1-24/tip: 같은 장면이 'looking at a menu', 'studying a menu'로도 나온다.
The same scene can also be described as 'looking at a menu' or 'studying a menu'.
part1/#p1-25/k: A server is taking an order.
part1/#p1-25/keyKo: to write down what a customer wants
part1/#p1-25/tip: 메모지를 든 종업원이 손님 옆에 서 있는 장면이 전형적이다.
The typical scene is a server holding a notepad and standing next to a customer.
part1/#p1-26/k: 한 여자가 과일 하나를 살펴보고 있다.
A woman is examining a piece of fruit.
part1/#p1-26/keyKo: to look at closely; to inspect
part1/#p1-26/tip: examine, inspect, look over, check 모두 '살펴보다'로 묶어 외우자.
Learn examine, inspect, look over, and check together as words for "look at closely."
part1/#p1-27/k: 식사를 위해 테이블 몇 개가 차려져 있다.
Some tables have been set for a meal.
part1/#p1-27/keyKo: (of a table) ready with plates, cutlery, etc.
part1/#p1-27/tip: set the table(상을 차리다)의 수동형이다. 사람이 상을 차리는 중이라면 'is being set'.
This is the passive of set the table (to put out plates and cutlery). If someone is still doing it, use 'is being set'.
part1/#p1-28/k: Price tags have been attached to the items.
part1/#p1-28/keyKo: to be fixed onto; to be stuck to
part1/#p1-28/tip: attach(붙이다) ↔ remove(떼다). 사물 상태는 완료 수동태로 자주 묘사된다.
Attach (fix onto) ↔ remove (take off). The state of objects is often described with the perfect passive.
part1/#p1-29/k: A worker is wiping off a counter.
part1/#p1-29/keyKo: to clean (a surface) with a cloth
part1/#p1-29/tip: 청소 동사를 구분하자. wipe(천으로 닦다), mop(대걸레질하다), sweep(빗자루로 쓸다).
Know your cleaning verbs: wipe (clean with a cloth), mop (clean a floor with a wet mop), sweep (clean with a broom).
part1/#p1-30/k: 손님 몇 명이 줄을 서서 기다리고 있다.
Some customers are waiting in line.
part1/#p1-30/keyKo: to queue; to stand in a row waiting
part1/#p1-30/tip: 'standing in line', 'forming a line'도 같은 장면에 쓰인다.
The phrases 'standing in line' and 'forming a line' are also used for the same scene.
part1/#p1-31/k: 차 몇 대가 길을 따라 주차되어 있다.
Some cars are parked along the street.
part1/#p1-31/tip: 사람이 없는 사진에서 'is being parked'가 들리면 오답이다.
In a photo with no people, 'is being parked' is wrong.
part1/#p1-32/keyKo: to stand in a row along the road
part1/#p1-32/tip: 동사 line(줄지어 서 있다)은 능동형으로 상태를 묘사한다. 'The street is lined with trees.'도 같은 뜻이다.
The verb line (to stand in a row along) describes a state in the active voice. The sentence 'The street is lined with trees.' means the same.
part1/#p1-33/k: 차량 몇 대가 신호등 앞에 줄지어 서 있다.
Some vehicles are lined up at a traffic light.
part1/#p1-33/tip: 사람에게도 사물에게도 쓴다. 'in a row(한 줄로)'와 함께 자주 나온다.
It is used for both people and things, and it often appears with 'in a row' (in a single line).
part1/#p1-34/tip: board ↔ get off·step off(내리다). 사람이 타는 방향인지 내리는 방향인지 확인하자.
Board ↔ get off, step off (leave a vehicle). Check whether people are getting on or getting off.
part1/#p1-35/k: A woman is stepping off a train.
part1/#p1-35/tip: get off, exit도 같은 의미로 쓰인다.
Get off and exit are used with the same meaning.
part1/#p1-36/k: 사람 몇 명이 길을 건너고 있다.
Some people are crossing the street.
part1/#p1-36/keyKo: to go to the other side of the road
part1/#p1-36/tip: It often appears with 'at a crosswalk' (at a pedestrian crossing).
part1/#p1-37/k: 자전거 한 대가 기둥에 기대어 세워져 있다.
A bicycle is leaning against a pole.
part1/#p1-37/tip: 사람뿐 아니라 자전거·사다리 같은 사물 주어에도 lean against를 쓴다.
Lean against is used not only for people but also for things like bicycles and ladders.
part1/#p1-38/k: 사람 몇 명이 승강장에서 기다리고 있다.
Some people are waiting on a platform.
part1/#p1-38/keyKo: to wait where passengers get on trains
part1/#p1-38/tip: 기차역 사진의 핵심 어휘: platform(승강장), track(선로), railing(난간).
Key words for train station photos: platform (where you board), track (rails), railing (handrail or barrier).
part1/#p1-39/k: Traffic is moving in both directions.
part1/#p1-39/tip: in both directions(양방향)와 in the same direction(같은 방향)을 구분해 듣자.
Listen carefully to tell in both directions (two ways) from in the same direction (one way).
part1/#p1-40/k: 한 남자가 트렁크에 짐을 싣고 있다.
A man is loading luggage into a trunk.
part1/#p1-40/keyKo: to put A into B (to carry)
part1/#p1-40/tip: load(싣다) ↔ unload(내리다). 짐이 들어가는 방향인지 나오는 방향인지 확인하자.
Load (put in) ↔ unload (take out). Check whether the bags are going in or coming out.
part1/#p1-41/k: 보행자 몇 명이 인도를 따라 걷고 있다.
Some pedestrians are walking along a sidewalk.
part1/#p1-41/keyKo: to go on foot beside or down (a path)
part1/#p1-41/tip: sidewalk(인도), pedestrian(보행자)은 거리 사진의 필수 어휘다.
Sidewalk (path for walkers) and pedestrian (person on foot) are must-know words for street photos.
part1/#p1-42/k: 차 한 대가 교차로에 멈춰 서 있다.
A car is stopped at an intersection.
part1/#p1-42/keyKo: to have come to a halt at
part1/#p1-42/tip: Also remember intersection (where roads cross) and traffic light.
part1/#p1-43/keyKo: to be getting cleaned right now
part1/#p1-43/tip: 'is being p.p.'(진행 수동태)는 지금 누군가 그 동작을 하고 있다는 뜻이다. 세차하는 사람이 보여야 정답이다. 'A man is washing a car.'와 같은 의미다.
The present progressive passive is being p.p. means someone is doing the action right now. Someone washing the car must be visible. It means the same as 'A man is washing a car.'
part1/#p1-44/k: A man is riding a bicycle.
part1/#p1-44/tip: 타고 가는 riding과 끌고 가는 pushing·walking a bicycle을 구분하자.
Tell riding (sitting on and moving) apart from pushing or walking a bicycle (moving it by hand).
part1/#p1-45/k: A traffic sign is posted at the corner.
part1/#p1-45/keyKo: put up for people to see
part1/#p1-45/tip: The verb post (to put up) goes well with sign and notice.
part1/#p1-46/tip: under renovation(보수 중), under repair(수리 중)도 함께 기억하자.
Also remember under renovation (being updated) and under repair (being fixed).
part1/#p1-47/keyKo: to surface (a road) with asphalt, etc.
part1/#p1-47/tip: paved road(포장도로), pavement(포장 도로, 보도)도 함께 나온다.
You'll also see paved road (road with a hard surface) and pavement (road surface; sidewalk).
part1/#p1-48/k: 사다리 하나가 벽에 기대어 세워져 있다.
A ladder is propped against a wall.
part1/#p1-48/tip: 'is leaning against'와 같은 뜻으로, 사다리 사진의 단골 정답이다.
It means the same as 'is leaning against', and it is a regular correct answer in ladder photos.
part1/#p1-49/k: Some bricks are piled on the ground.
part1/#p1-49/tip: The phrases 'in a pile' and 'stacked' are also used for the same scene.
part1/#p1-50/k: A man is operating heavy machinery.
part1/#p1-50/tip: machinery는 불가산명사다. operate, run, use 모두 정답 표현으로 나올 수 있다.
Machinery is uncountable. Operate, run, and use can all appear in correct answers.
part1/#p1-51/k: A worker is climbing a ladder.
part1/#p1-51/tip: 사다리가 세워져 있기만 하고 아무도 오르지 않으면 climbing은 오답이다.
If a ladder is just standing there and no one is on it, climbing is wrong.
part1/#p1-52/k: Workers are unloading materials from a truck.
part1/#p1-52/tip: load와 unload를 바꿔 치는 오답에 주의한다.
Watch for wrong options that swap load and unload.
part1/#p1-53/keyKo: to be getting a coat of paint right now
part1/#p1-53/tip: 'is being p.p.'(진행 수동태)는 지금 누군가 그 동작을 하고 있다는 뜻이다. 붓이나 롤러로 칠하는 사람이 있어야 정답이다. 칠이 끝난 벽은 'has been painted'.

The present progressive passive is being p.p. means someone is doing the action right now. Someone painting with a brush or roller must be visible. A wall that is already finished is 'has been painted'.
part1/#p1-54/k: 한 인부가 벽에 구멍을 뚫고 있다.
A worker is drilling a hole in the wall.
part1/#p1-54/keyKo: to make a hole (with a power tool)
part1/#p1-54/tip: 공구 이름도 익혀 두자: drill(드릴), hammer(망치), saw(톱).
Learn tool names too: drill, hammer, saw.
part1/#p1-55/k: 한 남자가 나무판의 치수를 재고 있다.
A man is measuring a piece of wood.
part1/#p1-55/keyKo: to find the size or length of
part1/#p1-55/tip: 줄자(tape measure)를 들고 있는 장면이 전형적이다.
The typical scene shows someone holding a tape measure.
part1/#p1-56/k: 한 남자가 널빤지를 어깨에 메고 나르고 있다.
A man is carrying a plank on his shoulder.
part1/#p1-56/tip: on his shoulder(어깨에), in his arms(품에), under his arm(옆구리에) 등 위치 표현을 끝까지 듣자.
Listen all the way to the location phrase: on his shoulder, in his arms (held against his chest), under his arm (at his side).
part1/#p1-57/k: Scaffolding has been put up beside a building.
part1/#p1-57/tip: scaffolding(공사장 비계)은 공사 사진의 핵심 명사다.
Scaffolding (a temporary frame for building work) is a key noun in construction photos.
part1/#p1-58/k: 한 인부가 잔해를 쓸어 담고 있다.
A worker is sweeping up debris.
part1/#p1-58/keyKo: to clean up with a broom
part1/#p1-58/tip: In debris (broken pieces, waste), the s is silent: /dəˈbriː/.
part1/#p1-59/k: 한 남자가 작업대 위로 몸을 숙이고 있다.
A man is bending over a workbench.
part1/#p1-59/tip: It is used for the same scene as 'leaning over'.
part1/#p1-60/k: 도로 위에 원뿔형 표지 몇 개가 놓여 있다.
Some traffic cones have been placed on the road.
part1/#p1-60/tip: 공사장 사진에서는 cone(원뿔형 표지), barrier(차단벽)가 자주 나온다.
Construction photos often show cone (cone-shaped road marker) and barrier (something that blocks the way).
part1/#p1-61/k: 벽에 그림 한 점이 걸려 있다.
A picture is hanging on the wall.
part1/#p1-61/keyKo: to be fixed to a wall, etc. from above
part1/#p1-61/tip: hang은 능동 진행형(is hanging)으로도 상태를 나타낸다. 'has been hung'과 같은 뜻이다.
Hang can describe a state in the active progressive (is hanging). It means the same as 'has been hung'.
part1/#p1-62/k: A television is mounted on the wall.
part1/#p1-62/keyKo: to be fixed to; to be installed on
part1/#p1-62/tip: 벽걸이 TV, 선반, 시계처럼 고정된 사물에 쓴다.
It is used for things fixed in place, such as wall TVs, shelves, and clocks.
part1/#p1-63/k: 쿠션 몇 개가 소파 위에 가지런히 놓여 있다.
Some cushions are arranged on a sofa.
part1/#p1-63/tip: 'in a row(한 줄로)', 'in a circle(원형으로)' 같은 배열 표현과 함께 나온다.
It appears with layout phrases such as 'in a row' (in a line) and 'in a circle' (in a ring).
part1/#p1-64/k: A lamp is positioned next to a bed.
part1/#p1-64/tip: next to, beside, between 등 위치 전치사까지 사진과 맞는지 확인하자.
Check that location prepositions like next to, beside, and between also match the photo.
part1/#p1-65/k: A rug covers most of the floor.
part1/#p1-65/tip: 사물 주어 + 능동 동사(cover, line, overlook)로 상태를 묘사하는 문장도 자주 나온다.
Sentences that describe a state with a thing as the subject + an active verb (cover, line, overlook) are also common.
part1/#p1-66/k: 꽃병 하나가 창턱 위에 놓여 있다.
A vase is resting on a windowsill.
part1/#p1-66/tip: rest on은 '쉬다'가 아니라 '~ 위에 놓여 있다'는 뜻이다. windowsill(창턱)도 기억하자.
Rest on here doesn't mean "relax"; it means "be placed on top of." Also remember windowsill (the ledge at the bottom of a window).
part1/#p1-67/k: A light fixture is suspended from the ceiling.
part1/#p1-67/tip: 'is hanging from the ceiling'과 같은 뜻이다.
It means the same as 'is hanging from the ceiling'.
part1/#p1-68/k: 선반 몇 개가 책으로 가득 차 있다.
Some shelves are filled with books.
part1/#p1-68/tip: 'be full of'와 같은 뜻이다. empty(비어 있는)와 대비되어 출제된다.
It means the same as 'be full of', and it is often contrasted with empty.
part1/#p1-69/k: 한 여자가 식물에 물을 주고 있다.
A woman is watering some plants.
part1/#p1-69/keyKo: to wet plants (with a can or hose)
part1/#p1-69/tip: 명사 water가 동사로 쓰였다. watering can(물뿌리개)도 함께 나온다.
The noun water is used here as a verb. You'll also see watering can.
part1/#p1-70/k: 한 남자가 대걸레로 바닥을 닦고 있다.
A man is mopping the floor.
part1/#p1-70/keyKo: to clean (a floor) with a wet cleaning tool
part1/#p1-70/tip: Don't confuse mop (clean with a wet mop) with sweep (clean with a broom).
part1/#p1-71/k: A woman is folding some laundry.
part1/#p1-71/keyKo: to make washed clothes into neat piles
part1/#p1-71/tip: fold는 옷·수건·종이를 접거나 갤 때 쓴다.
Fold is used for clothes, towels, and paper.
part1/#p1-72/tip: lower(내리다) ↔ raise(올리다). 블라인드·커튼의 상태를 사진에서 확인하자.
Lower (pull down) ↔ raise (pull up). Check the position of blinds and curtains in the photo.
part1/#p1-73/keyKo: (of a bed) being tidied with sheets
part1/#p1-73/tip: 'is being p.p.'(진행 수동태)는 지금 누군가 그 동작을 하고 있다는 뜻이다. make the bed(침대를 정돈하다)하는 사람이 보여야 정답이다. 정돈이 끝났다면 'The bed has been made.'

The present progressive passive is being p.p. means someone is doing the action right now. The photo must show someone as they make the bed (tidy the sheets). If it's already done, it's 'The bed has been made.'
part1/#p1-74/k: 접시 몇 개가 건조대에서 마르고 있다.
Some dishes are drying on a rack.
part1/#p1-74/keyKo: to be left on a stand until dry
part1/#p1-74/tip: rack은 '선반, 걸이'로 dish rack, coat rack, bike rack 등으로 쓰인다.
A rack is a stand or frame for holding things: dish rack, coat rack, bike rack.
part1/#p1-75/k: 코트 한 벌이 의자에 걸쳐져 있다.
A coat has been draped over a chair.
part1/#p1-75/tip: 옷이나 천이 늘어지게 걸쳐진 상태를 묘사한다.
It describes clothes or cloth hanging loosely over something.
part1/#p1-76/k: 배 몇 척이 항구에 정박해 있다.
Some boats are docked in a harbor.
part1/#p1-76/keyKo: tied up at a pier; anchored
part1/#p1-76/tip: docked, moored, tied up 모두 '정박해 있다'. pier, dock, harbor도 함께 외우자.
Docked, moored, and tied up all mean "parked at the shore." Learn pier, dock, and harbor together.
part1/#p1-77/k: 범선 한 척이 해안 근처에 정박해 있다.
A sailboat is moored near the shore.
part1/#p1-77/keyKo: tied up with ropes (at the shore)
part1/#p1-77/tip: moor는 배를 밧줄로 매어 두는 것이다. 'is tied to a dock'도 같은 장면에 쓴다.
Moor means to tie a boat in place with ropes. The phrase 'is tied to a dock' is also used for the same scene.
part1/#p1-78/k: 두 사람이 노를 저어 배를 몰고 있다.
Two people are rowing a boat.
part1/#p1-78/keyKo: to move a boat with oars
part1/#p1-78/tip: 동사 row(노를 젓다)와 명사 row(줄, 열)는 철자가 같다. 문맥으로 구분하자.
The verb row (to use oars) and the noun row (a line) are spelled the same, so use context to tell them apart.
part1/#p1-79/k: 집 몇 채가 물가를 내려다보고 있다.
part1/#p1-79/keyKo: to have a view of (from above)
part1/#p1-79/tip: 사물 주어 + overlook은 '~이 내려다보이는 곳에 있다'는 뜻이다. '간과하다'의 뜻과 구별하자.
A thing as subject + overlook means "to be located with a view down over." Don't mix it up with the meaning "to fail to notice."
part1/#p1-80/k: 나무 한 그루가 잔디 위에 그림자를 드리우고 있다.
A tree is casting a shadow on the grass.
part1/#p1-80/tip: 예외적으로 'Shadows are being cast ~'는 사람이 없어도 정답이 될 수 있다.
As an exception, 'Shadows are being cast ~' can be correct even with no people in the photo.
part1/#p1-81/k: 한 커플이 산책로를 따라 거닐고 있다.
A couple is strolling along a path.
part1/#p1-81/keyKo: to walk slowly; to take a walk
part1/#p1-81/tip: stroll, take a walk, walk along 모두 걷는 장면에 쓴다.
Stroll, take a walk, and walk along are all used in walking scenes.
part1/#p1-82/k: 한 남자가 난간 너머로 몸을 숙이고 있다.
A man is leaning over a railing.
part1/#p1-82/keyKo: to bend forward over a handrail
part1/#p1-82/tip: lean against(~에 기대다)와 lean over(~ 위로 몸을 숙이다)를 구분하자.
Tell lean against (rest on for support) apart from lean over (bend forward above).
part1/#p1-83/k: Water is flowing from a fountain.
part1/#p1-83/tip: fountain(분수), spray(뿜다)도 공원 사진에서 자주 나온다.
Fountain and spray (to shoot out water) also often appear in park photos.
part1/#p1-84/k: 사람 몇 명이 공원에서 소풍을 즐기고 있다.
Some people are having a picnic in a park.
part1/#p1-84/tip: 잔디에 앉아 음식을 먹는 장면이면 'sitting on the grass'도 정답이 될 수 있다.
If people are sitting on the grass eating, 'sitting on the grass' can also be correct.
part1/#p1-85/k: 오솔길 하나가 공원 사이로 구불구불 나 있다.
A path winds through the park.
part1/#p1-85/keyKo: to follow a curving route through
part1/#p1-85/tip: 동사 wind는 [와인드]로 발음한다. 명사 wind(바람, [윈드])와 구분하자.
The verb wind rhymes with "find" (/waɪnd/). Don't confuse it with the noun wind (moving air), which sounds like "pinned."
part1/#p1-86/k: 한 남자가 부두에서 낚시를 하고 있다.
A man is fishing off a pier.
part1/#p1-86/tip: Remember pier (walkway over water), dock (place where boats tie up), and shore (land along the water) together.
part1/#p1-87/k: 나무 몇 그루가 물에 비치고 있다.
Some trees are reflected in the water.
part1/#p1-87/tip: You'll also see reflection (the image on the water).
part1/#p1-88/k: 한 남자가 갈퀴로 낙엽을 긁어모으고 있다.
part1/#p1-88/keyKo: to gather fallen leaves (with a garden tool)
part1/#p1-88/tip: Rake is used both as a noun (a garden tool) and as a verb (to gather with that tool).
part1/#p1-89/k: A woman is mowing the lawn.
part1/#p1-89/tip: mow[모우]의 발음을 익혀 두자. lawn mower(잔디 깎는 기계)도 함께 나온다.
Learn how to say mow: it rhymes with "go." You'll also see lawn mower (grass-cutting machine).
part1/#p1-90/k: 다리 하나가 강을 가로질러 놓여 있다.
part1/#p1-90/tip: 'A bridge crosses a river.', 'extends across a river'도 같은 뜻이다.
The sentences 'A bridge crosses a river.' and 'extends across a river' mean the same.
part1/#p1-91/k: 한 여자가 서류를 나눠 주고 있다.
A woman is handing out some papers.
part1/#p1-91/tip: hand out, distribute, pass out 모두 '배포하다'.
Hand out, distribute, and pass out all mean "to give to each person."
part1/#p1-92/k: A man is pointing at a chart.
part1/#p1-92/tip: 'point to'도 같은 뜻이다. 화면이나 차트 앞의 발표 장면에 단골로 나온다.
The phrase 'point to' means the same. It is a regular in presentation scenes in front of a screen or chart.
part1/#p1-93/k: A man is giving a presentation.
part1/#p1-93/keyKo: to deliver a talk; to present
part1/#p1-93/tip: The phrase 'making a presentation' means the same.
part1/#p1-94/k: 기술자들이 무대 위에 장비를 설치하고 있다.
Technicians are setting up equipment on a stage.
part1/#p1-94/tip: set up은 설치하는 동작이다. 이미 설치가 끝난 상태면 'has been set up'.
Set up is the action of installing. If it's already installed, it's 'has been set up'.
part1/#p1-95/k: 사람 몇 명이 테이블에 둘러앉아 있다.
Some people are seated around a table.
part1/#p1-95/tip: be seated는 sitting과 같은 상태 표현이다. around a table, in a row 같은 위치 표현까지 끝까지 듣자.
Be seated is a state expression meaning the same as sitting. Listen all the way to location phrases like around a table or in a row.
part1/#p1-96/k: An audience is gathered in an auditorium.
part1/#p1-96/tip: Remember auditorium (large hall), audience (listeners), and crowd (large group of people) together.
part1/#p1-97/k: A speaker is addressing an audience.
part1/#p1-97/tip: Besides "place where someone lives," address also appears in Part 1 as a verb meaning "to give a speech to."
part1/#p1-98/k: 사람 몇 명이 악수를 하고 있다.
part1/#p1-98/tip: Hands is always plural in this phrase.
part1/#p1-99/tip: The phrase 'writing something down' is also used for the same scene.
part1/#p1-100/k: Some refreshments have been laid out on a table.
part1/#p1-100/tip: refreshments(다과)는 행사 사진의 단골 명사다. lay out(펼쳐 놓다)의 수동형.
Refreshments (light snacks and drinks) is a regular noun in event photos. It is the passive of lay out (to spread out).
part1/#p1-101/tip: 'is being p.p.'(진행 수동태)는 지금 누군가 그 동작을 하고 있다는 뜻이다. 나눠 주는 사람이 사진에 있어야 정답이다. 서류가 탁자 위에 놓여 있기만 하면 오답.
The present progressive passive is being p.p. means someone is doing the action right now. Someone handing them out must be in the photo. If the documents are just lying on the table, it's wrong.
part1/#p1-102/k: 한 여자가 마이크에 대고 말하고 있다.
A woman is speaking into a microphone.
part1/#p1-102/keyKo: to talk with one's mouth near a mic
part1/#p1-103/k: 사람 몇 명이 연설자에게 박수를 치고 있다.
Some people are applauding a speaker.
part1/#p1-103/tip: Applaud and clap mean the same.
part1/#p1-104/k: A man is adjusting a microphone.
part1/#p1-104/tip: adjust는 높이나 위치를 맞추는 동작이다. 의자·화면·장비 등에도 쓴다.
Adjust means to set the height or position. It is also used for chairs, screens, equipment, and so on.
part1/#p1-105/k: 사람 몇 명이 사진 촬영을 위해 포즈를 취하고 있다.
Some people are posing for a photograph.
part1/#p1-105/keyKo: to stand still for a picture
part1/#p1-105/tip: 'having their picture taken'도 같은 장면에 쓴다.
The phrase 'having their picture taken' is also used for the same scene.
part1/#p1-106/k: 한 남자가 커피 한 잔을 들고 있다.
A man is holding a cup of coffee.
part1/#p1-106/tip: holding은 들고 있는 상태, picking up은 집어 드는 동작이다.
Holding is the state of having it in hand; picking up is the action of lifting it.
part1/#p1-107/k: 한 여자가 코트를 입고 있다(입는 중이다).
A woman is putting on a coat.
part1/#p1-107/tip: putting on은 입는 '동작'이다. 이미 입고 있는 상태라면 'wearing'이 정답이다.
Putting on is the action of dressing. If the person already has it on, 'wearing' is the answer.
part1/#p1-108/k: 한 남자가 바닥에 무릎을 꿇고 있다.
A man is kneeling on the floor.
part1/#p1-108/tip: The k in kneel is silent, so it sounds like "neel" (/niːl/).
part1/#p1-109/k: 두 사람이 서로 마주 보고 있다.
Two people are facing each other.
part1/#p1-109/tip: 'facing the same direction(같은 방향을 보고 있다)'과 구분하자.
Don't confuse it with 'facing the same direction' (looking the same way).
part1/#p1-110/k: 한 여자가 머그잔에 든 음료를 홀짝이고 있다.
A woman is sipping from a mug.
part1/#p1-110/keyKo: to drink in small amounts from
part1/#p1-110/tip: sip(조금씩 마시다)과 drink(마시다)는 같은 장면에 쓰인다.
Sip (drink a little at a time) and drink are used for the same scene.
part1/#p1-111/k: 한 남자가 신발 끈을 묶고 있다.
A man is tying his shoe.
part1/#p1-111/tip: 허리를 숙이거나 무릎을 꿇은 자세의 사진에 자주 나온다.
It often appears in photos of someone bending down or kneeling.
part1/#p1-112/k: A woman is walking up the stairs.
part1/#p1-112/tip: up(올라가다)과 down(내려가다)의 방향을 확인하자. 'climbing the stairs'도 같은 뜻.
Check the direction: up vs. down. The phrase 'climbing the stairs' means the same.
part1/#p1-113/k: 사람 몇 명이 서로 담소를 나누고 있다.
Some people are chatting with each other.
part1/#p1-113/tip: talking, conversing, having a conversation 모두 같은 장면에 쓴다.
Talking, conversing, and having a conversation are all used for the same scene.
part1/#p1-114/k: 한 여자가 소포를 집어 들고 있다.
A woman is picking up a package.
part1/#p1-114/tip: pick up은 집어 드는 동작, holding은 들고 있는 상태다.
Pick up is the action of lifting; holding is the state of having it in hand.
part1/#p1-115/k: 한 남자가 공구를 제자리에 정리하고 있다.
A man is putting away some tools.
part1/#p1-115/keyKo: to store; to return to its place
part1/#p1-115/tip: put away(치우다)와 take out(꺼내다)을 바꿔 치는 오답에 주의한다.
Watch for wrong options that swap put away (store) and take out (remove from storage).
part1/#p1-116/k: A man is taking off his glasses.
part1/#p1-116/tip: take off(벗는 동작) ↔ put on(입는 동작) ↔ wear(착용 상태).
Take off (removing) ↔ put on (dressing) ↔ wear (having on).
part1/#p1-117/k: A woman is staring out a window.
part1/#p1-117/keyKo: to look fixedly through a window
part1/#p1-117/tip: 'looking out a window', 'gazing out a window'도 같은 뜻이다.
The phrases 'looking out a window' and 'gazing out a window' mean the same.
part1/#p1-118/k: Two men are walking side by side.
part1/#p1-118/keyKo: to go along next to each other
part1/#p1-118/tip: side by side(나란히)와 one behind the other(앞뒤로)를 구분하자.
Tell side by side (next to each other) apart from one behind the other (in single file).
part1/#p1-119/k: 상자 하나가 선반 위로 들어 올려지고 있다.
A box is being lifted onto a shelf.
part1/#p1-119/tip: 'is being p.p.'(진행 수동태)는 지금 누군가 그 동작을 하고 있다는 뜻이다. 누군가 상자를 드는 모습이 보여야 정답이다. 'Someone is lifting a box.'와 같은 의미.
The present progressive passive is being p.p. means someone is doing the action right now. Someone lifting the box must be visible. It means the same as 'Someone is lifting a box.'
part1/#p1-120/k: 한 남자가 소매를 걷어 올리고 있다.
A man is rolling up his sleeves.
part1/#p1-120/keyKo: to fold up the ends of one's sleeves
part1/#p1-120/tip: roll up(걷어 올리다) ↔ roll down(내리다). 걷어 올리는 동작은 'is rolling up', 이미 걷어 올린 상태는 'His sleeves are rolled up.'으로 묘사한다.
Roll up ↔ roll down. The action is 'is rolling up', and the finished state is described as 'His sleeves are rolled up.'
lc/#lc-1/k: Q: 보고서 마감이 언제예요? / A: 김 씨가 아직 검토하고 있어요.
Q: When is the report due? / A: Ms. Kim is still reviewing it.
lc/#lc-1/keyKo: 아직 검토 중인 (→ 아직 정해지지 않았다)
not done checking it (→ no date set yet)
lc/#lc-1/tip: When 질문에 시점 대신 '아직 검토 중'이라고 돌려 답하는 전형적인 정답 유형이다.
This is a typical correct answer: instead of giving a time to a When question, the speaker indirectly says it is still being checked.
lc/#lc-2/k: Q: 교육은 누가 진행하나요? / A: 아직 안 정해졌어요.
Q: Who's going to lead the training session? / A: It hasn't been decided yet.
lc/#lc-2/keyKo: no decision has been made (so far)
lc/#lc-2/tip: Who·When·Where 등 거의 모든 의문사 질문에 정답이 되는 '미정' 응답이다.
This "not decided" response can be correct for almost any wh-question, such as Who, When, or Where.
lc/#lc-3/k: Q: 이 상자들 어디에 둘까요? / A: 사무장님께 여쭤볼게요.
Q: Where should I put these boxes? / A: Let me ask the office manager.
lc/#lc-3/keyKo: I'll check with ~ (→ I'm not sure either)
lc/#lc-3/tip: 장소를 직접 말하지 않아도 '확인해 보겠다'는 응답이 정답이 될 수 있다.
A response saying "I'll find out" can be correct even if it doesn't name a place.
lc/#lc-4/k: Q: 고객한테 청구서 보냈어요? / A: 당신이 보낸 줄 알았는데요.
Q: Did you send the invoice to the client? / A: I thought you did.
lc/#lc-4/keyKo: 당신이 한 줄 알았다 (→ 나는 안 했다)
I assumed it was you (→ I didn't do it)
lc/#lc-4/tip: Yes/No 없이 상대에게 되묻듯 답하는 응답. 대동사 did가 send를 대신한다.
This answers without yes or no, turning the question back on the other person. The pro-verb did stands in for send.
lc/#lc-4/xk/0: The client is based in Seattle.
lc/#lc-5/k: Q: 지붕 수리비가 얼마나 들까요? / A: 아직 견적을 기다리고 있어요.
Q: How much will the roof repairs cost? / A: We're still waiting for an estimate.
lc/#lc-5/keyKo: we haven't received ~ yet (→ we don't know yet)
lc/#lc-5/tip: How much 질문에 금액 대신 estimate(견적)나 quote를 언급하는 응답이 자주 정답이다.
For How much questions, a response mentioning an estimate (expected cost) or a quote instead of an amount is often correct.
lc/#lc-6/k: Q: 프린터가 왜 안 되죠? / A: 점검 관련 이메일 못 받으셨어요?
Q: Why isn't the printer working? / A: Didn't you get the email about the maintenance?
lc/#lc-6/keyKo: 이메일 못 받았어요? (→ 이미 공지된 내용이다)
Didn't you see the message? (→ it was already announced)
lc/#lc-6/tip: 질문에 질문으로 답하는 유형. 이유를 직접 말하지 않고 정보 출처를 알려 준다.
This type answers a question with a question. Instead of giving the reason directly, it points to where the information is.
lc/#lc-7/k: Q: 직원을 더 뽑을까요, 아니면 초과 근무 수당을 줄까요? / A: 그건 예산에 달렸죠.
Q: Should we hire more staff or pay overtime? / A: That depends on the budget.
lc/#lc-7/keyKo: 그건 ~에 달려 있다 (→ 지금은 정할 수 없다)
it's decided by ~ (→ can't choose right now)
lc/#lc-7/tip: 선택 의문문에서 둘 중 하나를 고르지 않는 응답도 정답이 된다.
In choice questions (A or B), a response that picks neither option can also be correct.
lc/#lc-7/xk/1: I paid with a credit card.
lc/#lc-8/k: Q: 시카고에서 어느 호텔에 묵어요? / A: 제가 보낸 일정표를 확인해 보세요.
Q: Which hotel are we staying at in Chicago? / A: Check the itinerary I sent you.
lc/#lc-8/keyKo: to look at the travel schedule (→ the answer is there)
lc/#lc-8/tip: 답 대신 '자료를 보라'고 안내하는 응답. schedule, handout, website도 같은 패턴이다.
Instead of answering, this response tells you to look at a document. Schedule, handout, and website follow the same pattern.
lc/#lc-8/xk/1: 네, 시카고에 가 본 적 있어요.
lc/#lc-9/k: Q: 새 일정 관리 소프트웨어 쓰기 쉬워요? / A: 아직 써 볼 기회가 없었어요.
Q: Is the new scheduling software easy to use? / A: I haven't had a chance to try it yet.
lc/#lc-9/keyKo: I haven't been able to ~ yet
lc/#lc-9/tip: Yes/No 의문문에 '아직 안 해 봐서 모른다'고 답하는 전형적인 정답이다.
This is a typical correct answer to a yes/no question: "I haven't tried it yet, so I don't know."
lc/#lc-10/k: Q: 제품 출시 행사는 언제예요? / A: 무기한 연기됐어요.
Q: When does the product launch take place? / A: It's been postponed indefinitely.
lc/#lc-10/keyKo: it was delayed (→ there's no set date)
lc/#lc-10/tip: When 질문에 '연기·취소'로 답하는 응답은 시점이 없어도 정답이다.
For a When question, a response about a delay or cancellation is correct even without a time.
lc/#lc-11/k: Q: 지금 앤더슨 거래처는 누가 맡고 있어요? / A: 제이슨이 알 거예요.
Q: Who's handling the Anderson account now? / A: Jason would know.
lc/#lc-11/tip: 제3자를 알려 주는 응답. 질문의 단어를 그대로 반복하는 보기보다 이런 응답이 정답인 경우가 많다.
This response names a third person who knows. Such responses are often correct, rather than options that repeat words from the question.
lc/#lc-12/k: Q: 내일 공항까지 태워 줄 수 있어요? / A: 제 차가 정비소에 있어요.
Q: Can you give me a ride to the airport tomorrow? / A: My car is in the shop.
lc/#lc-12/keyKo: (차가) 수리 중인 (→ 태워 줄 수 없다)
(of a car) being repaired (→ can't drive you)
lc/#lc-12/tip: No 없이 사정을 설명해 거절하는 유형. shop을 '가게'로만 들으면 놓친다.
This type declines by explaining the situation without saying no. If you only hear shop as "store," you'll miss it.
lc/#lc-12/xk/1: I gave it to her yesterday.
lc/#lc-13/k: Q: 새 안내 책자 도착했어요? / A: 안내 데스크에 확인해 볼게요.
Q: Have the new brochures arrived? / A: I'll check with the front desk.
lc/#lc-13/tip: 'I'll find out.', 'Let me look into it.'으로도 나온다.
It also appears as 'I'll find out.' or 'Let me look into it.'
lc/#lc-14/k: Q: 안건 자료 복사해 둘까요? / A: 못 들었어요? 회의 취소됐어요.
Q: Should I make copies of the agenda? / A: Haven't you heard? The meeting was called off.
lc/#lc-14/keyKo: 못 들었어요? (→ 상황이 바뀌어 할 필요가 없다)
Didn't anyone tell you? (→ plans changed, no need)
lc/#lc-14/tip: 제안 질문에 '상황이 바뀌었다'는 정보로 답하는 우회 응답이다.
This indirect response answers an offer with news that the situation has changed.
lc/#lc-15/k: Q: 토요일 회사 야유회 가세요? / A: 다른 일정이 있어요.
Q: Are you going to the company picnic on Saturday? / A: I have other plans.
lc/#lc-15/keyKo: I'm busy then (→ I can't go)
lc/#lc-15/tip: No를 말하지 않는 불참 응답. 'I'll be out of town.'도 같은 의미로 자주 나온다.
This declines without saying no. The line 'I'll be out of town.' often appears with the same meaning.
lc/#lc-15/xk/0: The picture is on the wall.
lc/#lc-16/k: Q: 실례지만 제일 가까운 우체국이 어디예요? / A: 죄송해요, 저도 여기 처음이에요.
Q: Excuse me, where's the nearest post office? / A: Sorry, I'm new here myself.
lc/#lc-16/keyKo: I don't know this area either (→ I don't know)
lc/#lc-16/tip: 길·위치를 묻는 Where 질문에 대한 대표적인 '모른다' 응답이다.
This is the standard "I don't know" response to a Where question about directions or locations.
lc/#lc-17/k: Q: 창가 자리로 드릴까요, 통로 자리로 드릴까요? / A: 아무 데나 괜찮아요.
Q: Would you like a window seat or an aisle seat? / A: Either is fine.
lc/#lc-17/tip: 선택 의문문의 단골 정답. 'Whichever is cheaper.', 'I don't have a preference.'도 같은 유형이다.
This is a regular correct answer to choice questions. Lines like 'Whichever is cheaper.' and 'I don't have a preference.' are the same type.
lc/#lc-18/k: Q: 기술자가 지금쯤 와 있어야 하지 않나요? / A: 방금 차가 막힌다고 전화 왔어요.
Q: Shouldn't the technician be here by now? / A: He just called to say he's stuck in traffic.
lc/#lc-18/keyKo: ~ phoned a moment ago and said
lc/#lc-18/tip: 부정 의문문도 일반 의문문처럼 내용만 판단한다. 늦는 이유를 알려 주면 정답이다.
Judge a negative question by its content, just like a regular question. A response giving the reason for the delay is correct.
lc/#lc-19/k: Q: 고객이 우리 제안서를 어떻게 생각했대요? / A: 아직 답을 못 받았어요.
Q: How did the client like our proposal? / A: We haven't heard back from them yet.
lc/#lc-19/tip: 결과·반응을 묻는 질문에 '아직 연락이 없다'고 답하는 유형이다.
This type answers a question about results or reactions with "they haven't replied yet."
lc/#lc-19/xk/1: Yes, I like it a lot.
lc/#lc-20/k: Q: 여분 열쇠가 어디 있는지 아세요? / A: 맨 위 서랍을 찾아보세요.
Q: Do you know where the spare keys are? / A: Try the top drawer.
lc/#lc-20/tip: Do you know ~? 간접 의문문은 Yes/No보다 뒤의 의문사(where)에 맞는 답을 고른다.
For an indirect question like Do you know ~?, choose the answer that fits the wh-word after it (where), not yes or no.
lc/#lc-20/xk/1: The key is to work fast.
lc/#lc-21/k: 창문 좀 닫아 주시겠어요? 여기 좀 춥네요.
Would you mind closing the window? It's a little cold in here.
lc/#lc-21/tip: mind는 '꺼리다'라서 수락할 때 'Not at all.', 'Of course not.'처럼 부정으로 답한다.
Mind means "object to," so to agree you answer with a negative such as 'Not at all.' or 'Of course not.'
lc/#lc-22/k: Q: 스테이플러 좀 빌려도 될까요? / A: 그럼요. 제 책상 위에 있어요.
Q: Would you mind if I borrowed your stapler? / A: Not at all. It's on my desk.
lc/#lc-22/tip: Would you mind 질문에 'Yes, I would.'라고 하면 '싫다'는 거절이 된다.
If you answer a Would you mind question with 'Yes, I would.', it means "No, I don't want you to."
lc/#lc-22/xk/1: It staples up to fifty pages.
lc/#lc-23/k: 다음 세션 전에 잠깐 쉬는 게 어때요?
Why don't we take a short break before the next session?
lc/#lc-23/tip: Why로 시작하지만 이유를 묻는 게 아니다. Because로 시작하는 보기는 오답이다.
It starts with Why, but it isn't asking for a reason. Options starting with Because are wrong.
lc/#lc-24/k: Q: 팀 전체 점심을 주문하는 게 어때요? / A: 좋아요.
Q: Why don't we order lunch for the whole team? / A: Sounds good to me.
lc/#lc-24/tip: 제안 수락 표현. 'Good idea.', 'Let's do that.'도 같은 기능이다.
This accepts a suggestion. Lines like 'Good idea.' and 'Let's do that.' do the same job.
lc/#lc-25/k: Could you send me the updated figures by noon?
lc/#lc-25/tip: 요청에는 'Sure.', 'No problem.' 같은 수락이나 이유를 댄 거절이 정답이 된다.
For requests, the answer is an acceptance like 'Sure.' or 'No problem.', or a refusal with a reason.
lc/#lc-26/k: Q: 누가 출장 요리 업체에 전화해서 주문 확인 좀 해 줄래요? / A: 네, 제가 처리할게요.
Q: Could someone call the caterer to confirm the order? / A: Sure, I'll take care of it.
lc/#lc-26/tip: 'I'll handle it.', 'Leave it to me.'로 바뀌어 나온다.
It can be swapped for 'I'll handle it.' or 'Leave it to me.'
lc/#lc-27/k: Q: 금요일에 제 근무 좀 대신해 줄 수 있어요? / A: 미안하지만 안 되겠어요. 그날 멀리 가 있거든요.
Q: Can you cover my shift on Friday? / A: I'm afraid I can't. I'll be out of town.
lc/#lc-27/keyKo: sorry, but I'm unable to (polite refusal)
lc/#lc-27/tip: I'm afraid는 '두렵다'가 아니라 유감을 나타내는 완곡 표현이다.
Here I'm afraid doesn't mean "scared"; it is a soft way to express regret.
lc/#lc-28/k: 길 건너 카페에서 만나는 게 어때요?
How about meeting at the café across the street?
lc/#lc-28/tip: How로 시작해도 방법을 묻는 게 아니다. 뒤에 명사나 동명사가 오면 제안이다.
It starts with How, but it isn't asking about a method. A noun or gerund after it signals a suggestion.
lc/#lc-29/k: Q: 컨벤션 센터까지 택시 탈까요? / A: 저는 걷는 게 좋겠어요. 멀지 않거든요.
Q: Should we take a taxi to the convention center? / A: I'd rather walk; it's not far.
lc/#lc-29/tip: 제안을 받아들이지 않고 대안을 내는 응답. 'I'd prefer to ~'로도 나온다.
This response doesn't accept the suggestion and offers an alternative. It also appears as 'I'd prefer to ~'.
lc/#lc-30/k: Would you like me to make copies of the agenda?
lc/#lc-30/tip: Would you like to ~?(~하실래요?)와 달리 me가 들어가면 화자가 해 주겠다는 제안이다.
Unlike Would you like to ~? (Do you want to ~?), adding me makes it an offer by the speaker to do something.
lc/#lc-31/k: Q: 역으로 데리러 갈까요? / A: 그래 주면 정말 좋죠, 고마워요.
Q: Do you want me to pick you up at the station? / A: That would be great, thanks.
lc/#lc-32/k: Q: 그 상자들 옮기는 거 도와드릴까요? / A: 고맙지만 혼자 할 수 있어요.
Q: Would you like some help with those boxes? / A: Thanks, but I can manage.
lc/#lc-32/keyKo: I can do it alone (turning down help)
lc/#lc-32/tip: manage를 '관리하다'로만 알면 놓친다. 여기서는 '그럭저럭 해내다'라는 뜻이다.
If you only know manage as "run a business," you'll miss it. Here it means "cope; get it done."
lc/#lc-33/k: 발표 준비에 필요한 게 더 있으면 알려 주세요.
Let me know if you need anything else for the presentation.
lc/#lc-33/tip: 대화·담화 마무리에 자주 나오며, 추가 요청이 있으면 연락하라는 뜻이다.
It often comes at the end of a conversation or talk and means "contact me if you need anything more."
lc/#lc-34/k: Q: 오늘 조금 일찍 퇴근해도 될까요? / A: 그러세요.
Q: Is it all right if I leave a little early today? / A: Go ahead.
lc/#lc-34/tip: 허락 요청에는 'Sure.', 'Of course.'가 정답이다. 'I left early.'처럼 시제를 바꾼 보기는 함정이다.
For a request for permission, 'Sure.' or 'Of course.' is correct. An option with a changed tense, like 'I left early.', is a trap.
lc/#lc-35/k: Q: 새 인턴한테 사무실 좀 구경시켜 줄래요? / A: 기꺼이요.
Q: Could you show the new intern around the office? / A: I'd be happy to.
lc/#lc-35/tip: happy를 듣고 기분을 묻는 질문으로 착각하지 말 것. 요청을 수락하는 표현이다.
Don't mistake happy for a question about feelings. It is a way to accept a request.
lc/#lc-35/xk/1: He's happy with his new office.
lc/#lc-36/k: 기다리시는 동안 마실 것 좀 갖다 드릴까요?
Can I get you something to drink while you wait?
lc/#lc-36/tip: get이 '가져다주다'의 뜻이다. 응답은 'Just some water, please.'처럼 짧게 나온다.
Here get means "bring." The reply is short, like 'Just some water, please.'
lc/#lc-37/k: Q: 고객이 계약서를 3시까지 수정해 달래요. / A: 바로 할게요.
Q: The client wants the contract revised by three o'clock. / A: I'm on it.
lc/#lc-37/tip: Part 2 평서문 문제에서도 숨은 요청을 파악해 수락 응답을 고른다.
Even for Part 2 statements, spot the hidden request and choose the accepting response.
lc/#lc-38/k: Q: 오늘 저녁 저희랑 같이 식사하실래요? / A: 그러고 싶은데, 이 보고서를 끝내야 해요.
Q: Would you like to join us for dinner tonight? / A: I'd love to, but I have to finish this report.
lc/#lc-38/tip: love만 듣고 수락으로 판단하면 안 된다. but 뒤가 핵심이다.
Don't decide it's a yes just from love. The key part comes after but.
lc/#lc-38/xk/0: I joined the gym last month.
lc/#lc-39/k: Q: 수리 기사를 부를까요? / A: 그럴 필요는 없을 것 같아요.
Q: Should I call a repair technician? / A: I don't think that's necessary.
lc/#lc-39/keyKo: 그럴 필요 없을 것 같다 (완곡한 거절)
we probably don't need to (soft refusal)
lc/#lc-40/k: Do you need a hand setting up the projector?
lc/#lc-40/tip: give/lend a hand도 '돕다'라는 뜻이다. hand를 손 동작으로 해석한 보기는 오답이다.
Give a hand and lend a hand also mean "help." Options that treat hand as a body part or hand movement are wrong.
lc/#lc-41/k: 회의를 목요일 오후로 다시 잡을 수 있을까요?
Could we reschedule our meeting for Thursday afternoon?
lc/#lc-41/keyKo: to change the time or date of
lc/#lc-41/tip: Part 3 전화 목적 문제에서 'To change an appointment'로 패러프레이즈된다.
In Part 3 questions about why someone is calling, it is paraphrased as 'To change an appointment'.
lc/#lc-42/k: The deadline has been pushed back to next Friday.
lc/#lc-42/keyKo: to delay; to move to a later date
lc/#lc-42/tip: push back = postpone = delay. 반대 의미인 move up과 바꿔 내는 함정에 주의한다.
Push back = postpone = delay. Watch for traps that swap in the opposite, move up.
lc/#lc-43/k: We need to move up the product launch by a week.
lc/#lc-43/keyKo: to bring forward; to make earlier
lc/#lc-43/tip: move up = bring forward. move만 듣고 장소 이동으로 착각하기 쉽다.
Move up = bring forward. If you only hear move, it's easy to think it means changing location.
lc/#lc-44/k: 죄송해요, 좀 늦을 것 같아요. 고속도로가 너무 막혀요.
Sorry, I'm running late. The traffic on the highway is terrible.
lc/#lc-44/tip: 늦는 이유(교통, 이전 회의)가 바로 뒤에 나오므로 이유를 묻는 문제의 단서가 된다.
The reason for being late (traffic, an earlier meeting) comes right after it, so it's the clue for questions about the reason.
lc/#lc-45/k: 죄송하지만 토요일 밤은 예약이 다 찼습니다.
I'm sorry, but we're fully booked on Saturday night.
lc/#lc-45/tip: It appears as 'no rooms available' or 'no openings'.
lc/#lc-46/k: The outdoor concert was called off because of the storm.
lc/#lc-46/tip: call off = cancel. call을 듣고 전화 관련 보기를 고르면 오답이다.
Call off = cancel. Choosing a phone-related option because you heard call is wrong.
lc/#lc-47/k: 워크숍은 추후 공지가 있을 때까지 연기되었습니다.
The workshop has been postponed until further notice.
lc/#lc-47/keyKo: until a new announcement is made
lc/#lc-47/tip: 새 일정이 아직 없다는 뜻. 'A new date has not been set.'이 정답 보기로 나온다.
It means there is no new date yet. The line 'A new date has not been set.' appears as the correct option.
lc/#lc-48/k: 화요일 오전에 잠깐 통화할 시간 되세요?
Are you available on Tuesday morning for a quick call?
lc/#lc-48/keyKo: (of a person) free; able to meet
lc/#lc-48/tip: 사람에게는 '시간이 되는', 사물에는 '이용 가능한'. free, open으로 바꿔 나온다.
For people it means "free (to meet)"; for things it means "can be used or obtained." It is paraphrased as free or open.
lc/#lc-49/k: Does three o'clock work for you?
lc/#lc-49/tip: work를 '일하다'로만 알면 놓친다. suit, be convenient for와 같은 뜻이다.
If you only know work as "do a job," you'll miss it. It means the same as suit and be convenient for.
lc/#lc-50/k: 파텔 선생님이 오늘 바쁘시지만 4시에 진료를 잡아 드릴 수 있어요.
Dr. Patel is busy today, but she can fit you in at four.
lc/#lc-50/keyKo: to make time for ~ (in a busy schedule)
lc/#lc-50/tip: squeeze ~ in도 같은 뜻으로 자주 쓰인다.
Squeeze ~ in is also often used with the same meaning.
lc/#lc-51/k: 그날 일정이 겹쳐서 세미나에 참석할 수 없어요.
I have a scheduling conflict that day, so I can't attend the seminar.
lc/#lc-51/keyKo: two events at the same time; a clash
lc/#lc-51/tip: 불참 이유 문제의 정답이 'She has another commitment.'로 패러프레이즈된다.
In questions about why someone can't attend, the answer is paraphrased as 'She has another commitment.'
lc/#lc-52/k: 오전 내내 회의 때문에 꼼짝 못 하지만 점심 이후엔 시간이 돼요.
I'm tied up in meetings all morning, but I'm free after lunch.
lc/#lc-52/tip: busy의 패러프레이즈. '묶여 있다'는 물리적 의미로 만든 보기에 주의한다.
It is a paraphrase of busy. Watch for options based on the physical sense of "tied with rope."
lc/#lc-53/k: The renovation project is already two weeks behind schedule.
lc/#lc-53/tip: 반대는 ahead of schedule, 예정대로는 on schedule. 세 가지를 구분하는 문제가 나온다.
The opposite is ahead of schedule, and "as planned" is on schedule. Questions test telling the three apart.
lc/#lc-54/k: 갑작스러운 연락에도 이렇게 와 주셔서 감사합니다.
Thank you for coming in on such short notice.
lc/#lc-54/keyKo: with little warning; at the last minute
lc/#lc-55/k: 내일 10시 이 선생님 진료 예약을 확인하려고 전화드렸습니다.
I'm calling to confirm your appointment with Dr. Lee tomorrow at ten.
lc/#lc-55/keyKo: to check that a booking is still on
lc/#lc-55/tip: 병원·치과 음성 메시지에서 전화 목적 문제의 정답으로 자주 나온다.
In voicemails from clinics or dentists, it is often the answer to questions about why the speaker is calling.
lc/#lc-56/k: 공항에 발이 묶여서 회의에 못 갈 것 같아요.
I'm stuck at the airport, so I won't be able to make it to the meeting.
lc/#lc-56/keyKo: to get to (in time); to attend
lc/#lc-56/tip: can't make it은 불참을 뜻한다. make를 '만들다'로 해석한 보기는 오답이다.
Can't make it means "can't attend." Options that read make as "create" are wrong.
lc/#lc-57/k: 일이 좀 생겨서 오늘 점심 약속을 취소해야겠어요.
Something came up, so I have to cancel our lunch today.
lc/#lc-57/tip: 구체적인 사정을 밝히지 않고 약속을 취소·변경할 때 쓰는 말이다.
People say this to cancel or change plans without giving details.
lc/#lc-58/k: Sorry I'm late. I got held up at the bank.
lc/#lc-58/tip: hold up을 '들어 올리다'로 해석하지 말 것. 늦은 이유를 나타낸다.
Don't read hold up as "lift up." It gives the reason someone is late.
lc/#lc-59/k: There's been a last-minute change to the conference schedule.
lc/#lc-59/keyKo: a sudden change just before an event
lc/#lc-59/tip: 담화 초반에 나오면 무엇이 바뀌었는지가 문제로 이어진다.
If it comes early in a talk, a question about what changed usually follows.
lc/#lc-60/k: 일단 월요일로 잡아 둘게요. 금요일까지 확정해 주세요.
I'll pencil you in for Monday, and you can confirm by Friday.
lc/#lc-60/keyKo: to put ~ on the schedule for now (not final)
lc/#lc-60/tip: 연필로 적어 두듯 '아직 확정 전'이라는 뉘앙스가 핵심이다.
The key nuance is "not confirmed yet," as if written in pencil.
lc/#lc-61/k: 잠시만 기다리시면 청구 부서로 연결해 드리겠습니다.
Please hold, and I'll put you through to the billing department.
lc/#lc-61/tip: It is paraphrased as 'transfer your call' or 'connect you'.
lc/#lc-62/k: 잠시 끊지 말고 기다려 주시겠어요? 그분 일정을 확인해 볼게요.
Could you hold the line for a moment? I'll check his schedule.
lc/#lc-62/keyKo: to wait (on the phone) without hanging up
lc/#lc-62/tip: It is also said briefly, as in 'Hold on.' or 'Please hold.'
lc/#lc-63/k: 지금 자리에 안 계신데, 메시지 남기시겠어요?
He's not at his desk right now. Would you like to leave a message?
lc/#lc-63/keyKo: to record a note for someone
lc/#lc-63/tip: leave는 전화 건 사람이 남기는 것, take는 받는 사람이 받아 적는 것이다.
You leave a message when you're the caller; you take a message when you answer and write it down.
lc/#lc-64/k: She's in a meeting. Can I take a message?
lc/#lc-64/keyKo: to write down a caller's message
lc/#lc-64/tip: Part 3에서 화자가 해 주겠다는 일로 'Write down a message'가 정답이 된다.
In Part 3, when asked what the speaker offers to do, 'Write down a message' is the answer.
lc/#lc-65/k: I'll get back to you as soon as I have the numbers.
lc/#lc-65/tip: It appears as 'contact you later' or 'respond'.
lc/#lc-66/k: You can reach me directly at extension 4127.
lc/#lc-66/tip: '연장'이라는 뜻도 있지만 전화 맥락에서는 내선 번호다.
It can also mean "making longer," but in a phone context it means an internal line number.
lc/#lc-67/k: 안녕하세요, 그랜트 씨. 오늘 아침에 주신 전화에 회신드립니다.
Hi, Ms. Grant. I'm returning your call from this morning.
lc/#lc-67/tip: 전화 목적 문제에서 'To respond to a message'로 패러프레이즈된다.
In questions about why someone is calling, it is paraphrased as 'To respond to a message'.
lc/#lc-68/k: What's the best number to reach you at?
lc/#lc-68/tip: '도착하다', '손을 뻗다' 외에 '연락이 닿다'의 뜻으로 자주 쓰인다.
Besides "arrive at" and "stretch out a hand," it is often used to mean "get in touch with."
lc/#lc-69/k: 박 씨는 점심 식사하러 나가셨어요. 한 시간 뒤에 다시 전화해 주시겠어요?
Mr. Park is out to lunch. Could you call back in an hour?
lc/#lc-69/tip: 부재 이유(out to lunch)와 다시 걸 시간(in an hour)이 함께 문제로 나온다.
Both the reason the person is away (out to lunch) and when to call again (in an hour) can be asked about.
lc/#lc-70/k: 리베라 씨는 지금 자리에 안 계십니다.
Ms. Rivera is away from her desk at the moment.
lc/#lc-70/keyKo: not at one's workstation right now
lc/#lc-70/tip: not available, out of the office와 함께 부재를 나타낸다.
Along with not available and out of the office, it shows someone is away.
lc/#lc-71/k: He's on another line. Would you like to hold?
lc/#lc-72/k: 죄송해요, 전화가 끊겼네요. 엘리베이터에서 신호가 안 잡혔나 봐요.
Sorry, we got cut off. I think I lost the signal in the elevator.
lc/#lc-72/tip: cut을 듣고 자르는 동작이나 예산 삭감 보기를 고르면 오답이다.
Choosing an option about cutting something or budget cuts because you heard cut is wrong.
lc/#lc-73/k: 죄송하지만 전화 잘못 거신 것 같아요.
I'm sorry, but I think you have the wrong number.
lc/#lc-74/k: Q: 여보세요, 로라 김 씨와 통화할 수 있을까요? / A: 전데요. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
Q: Hello, may I speak with Laura Kim? / A: Speaking. How can I help you?
lc/#lc-74/keyKo: (on the phone) this is me; I'm that person
lc/#lc-74/tip: 'This is she.', 'This is he.'도 같은 뜻이다.
The lines 'This is she.' and 'This is he.' mean the same.
lc/#lc-75/k: Hi, this is Mark Evans calling from Brightline Office Supplies.
lc/#lc-75/tip: 음성 메시지 첫 문장. 화자의 소속·업종을 묻는 문제의 정답 근거다.
This is the first line of a voicemail, and it is the evidence for questions about the speaker's company or field.
lc/#lc-76/k: 웹사이트에 올라온 채용 공고 건으로 전화드렸습니다.
I'm calling about the job opening posted on your website.
lc/#lc-76/keyKo: the reason for my call is ~
lc/#lc-76/tip: 전화 목적 문제의 핵심 단서. 'I'm calling to ~', regarding도 같은 신호다.
It is the key clue for questions about the purpose of a call. The phrases 'I'm calling to ~' and regarding are the same kind of signal.
lc/#lc-77/k: 그 사람한테 전화해 봤는데 바로 음성 사서함으로 넘어갔어요.
I tried calling him, but it went straight to voicemail.
lc/#lc-77/keyKo: to go to the answering service
lc/#lc-78/k: Give me a call when you get a chance.
lc/#lc-78/tip: 음성 메시지 끝의 요청 사항 문제에서 'Return a call'이 정답으로 나온다.
In questions about what the speaker asks for at the end of a voicemail, 'Return a call' is the answer.
lc/#lc-79/k: 조금만 크게 말씀해 주시겠어요? 잘 안 들려서요.
Could you speak up a little? I can barely hear you.
lc/#lc-79/tip: '의견을 말하다'라는 뜻도 있지만 전화에서는 목소리를 키워 달라는 뜻이다.
It can also mean "give your opinion," but on the phone it is a request to raise your voice.
lc/#lc-80/k: 그분이 돌아오시는 대로 메시지 전해 드릴게요.
I'll pass along your message as soon as he gets back.
lc/#lc-80/tip: pass on, let him know로 바뀌어 나온다.
It appears as pass on or let him know.
lc/#lc-81/k: 고객이 오기 전에 매출 수치를 검토해 봅시다.
Let's go over the sales figures before the client arrives.
lc/#lc-81/tip: It is paraphrased as review or look over.
lc/#lc-82/k: We need to wrap up the meeting by four.
lc/#lc-82/keyKo: to finish; to bring to an end
lc/#lc-82/tip: wrap을 '포장하다'로 해석한 보기는 오답. finish, conclude와 같은 뜻이다.
Options that read wrap as "put paper around" are wrong. It means the same as finish and conclude.
lc/#lc-83/keyKo: on the list of topics (for a meeting)
lc/#lc-83/tip: In Part 3, it is the clue for questions about what is being discussed.
lc/#lc-84/k: 제가 휴가 가 있는 동안 오티즈 씨가 프로젝트를 맡을 거예요.
Ms. Ortiz will take over the project while I'm on leave.
lc/#lc-84/tip: 'assume responsibility for', 'be in charge of'로 바뀌어 나온다.
It appears as 'assume responsibility for' or 'be in charge of'.
lc/#lc-85/k: 내일 직원회의에 저 대신 들어가 줄 수 있어요?
Can you fill in for me at the staff meeting tomorrow?
lc/#lc-85/tip: fill in(서류를 작성하다)과 구분한다. for가 붙으면 '대신하다'다.
Tell it apart from fill in (complete a form). With for, it means "do someone's job for them."
lc/#lc-86/k: 지난주에 보낸 이메일 건으로 확인차 연락드렸어요.
I'm just following up on the email I sent last week.
lc/#lc-86/keyKo: to check back on; to take further action on
lc/#lc-86/tip: 전화·이메일 목적 문제에서 '이전 연락에 대한 후속'이라는 정답의 근거다.
In questions about the purpose of a call or email, it is the evidence for "following up on an earlier contact."
lc/#lc-87/k: 다음 주에 다시 연락해서 프로젝트 진행 상황을 확인해요.
Let's touch base next week to see how the project is going.
lc/#lc-87/keyKo: to contact briefly to share updates
lc/#lc-87/tip: 야구에서 온 말이지만 업무 맥락에서는 '연락하다'. check in과 비슷하다.
It comes from baseball, but at work it means "get in contact." It is similar to check in.
lc/#lc-88/k: 끝내기 전에 한 가지 문제를 더 말씀드리고 싶습니다.
I'd like to bring up one more issue before we finish.
lc/#lc-88/tip: It is paraphrased as raise or mention.
lc/#lc-89/k: 금요일까지 새 마케팅 전략을 생각해 내야 해요.
We need to come up with a new marketing strategy by Friday.
lc/#lc-89/keyKo: to think of (an idea or plan)
lc/#lc-89/tip: It appears as develop or think of.
lc/#lc-90/k: Who's in charge of the annual conference this year?
lc/#lc-90/tip: Who 질문에 이름 대신 부서명이나 직책으로 답해도 정답이다.
For a Who question, answering with a department or job title instead of a name is also correct.
lc/#lc-91/k: Please hand in your expense reports by Friday.
lc/#lc-91/keyKo: to submit; to give (to a person in charge)
lc/#lc-91/tip: submit, turn in과 같은 뜻. hand out(나눠 주다)과 혼동하지 말 것.
It means the same as submit and turn in. Don't confuse it with hand out (give to each person).
lc/#lc-92/k: 이달 말까지 끝내는 일정대로 잘 진행되고 있나요?
Are we still on track to finish by the end of the month?
lc/#lc-92/keyKo: going as planned; making good progress
lc/#lc-92/tip: on schedule과 같은 뜻. track을 선로·트랙으로 해석한 보기는 오답이다.
It means the same as on schedule. Options that read track as railway tracks or a running track are wrong.
lc/#lc-93/k: 마감을 맞추려면 초과 근무를 해야 할 거예요.
We'll have to work overtime to meet the deadline.
lc/#lc-93/keyKo: to finish by the due date
lc/#lc-93/tip: meet을 '만나다'로 해석하면 안 된다. meet a goal, meet demand도 '충족하다'라는 뜻이다.
Don't read meet as "see someone." In meet a goal and meet demand, it also means "satisfy."
lc/#lc-94/k: 예산에 변동이 생기면 계속 알려 주세요.
Keep me posted on any changes to the budget.
lc/#lc-94/tip: keep me updated, let me know와 같은 뜻이다.
It means the same as keep me updated and let me know.
lc/#lc-95/k: The board has decided to go ahead with the merger.
lc/#lc-95/keyKo: to proceed with; to carry out
lc/#lc-95/tip: 단독으로 쓰는 'Go ahead.'(그러세요)와 달리 with가 붙으면 계획을 실행한다는 뜻이다.
Unlike 'Go ahead.' on its own (Sure, you may), adding with means carrying out a plan.
lc/#lc-96/k: The director still needs to sign off on the budget.
lc/#lc-96/tip: approve의 패러프레이즈. sign off를 '방송을 마치다'로만 알면 놓친다.
It is a paraphrase of approve. If you only know sign off as "end a broadcast," you'll miss it.
lc/#lc-97/k: 월요일까지 짧은 발표 자료를 준비해 줄 수 있어요?
Could you put together a short presentation for Monday?
lc/#lc-97/tip: It appears as prepare or create.
lc/#lc-98/k: I'll look into the billing error and let you know.
lc/#lc-98/keyKo: to investigate; to find out about
lc/#lc-98/tip: investigate, check로 패러프레이즈된다. look at(보다)과 혼동하지 말 것.
It is paraphrased as investigate or check. Don't confuse it with look at (to view).
lc/#lc-99/k: All right, everyone, let's get down to business.
lc/#lc-99/keyKo: to start on the main topic; to start working
lc/#lc-100/k: 이번 주는 일손이 부족해서 모두 힘을 보태야 해요.
We're short-staffed this week, so everyone needs to pitch in.
lc/#lc-100/tip: Part 3 문제점 문제에서 'not enough employees'로 패러프레이즈된다.
In Part 3 questions about a problem, it is paraphrased as 'not enough employees'.
lc/#lc-101/k: 죄송하지만 그 모델은 지금 재고가 없습니다.
I'm sorry, that model is out of stock at the moment.
lc/#lc-101/keyKo: sold out; not available right now
lc/#lc-101/tip: sold out, unavailable, not in stock으로 바뀌어 나온다.
It appears as sold out, unavailable, or not in stock.
lc/#lc-102/k: 이 재킷 M 사이즈 재고 있어요?
Do you have this jacket in stock in a medium?
lc/#lc-102/tip: stock은 동사로 '(물건을) 채우다'. Part 1의 be stocked with와 함께 기억한다.
As a verb, stock means "fill (with goods)." Remember it together with be stocked with from Part 1.
lc/#lc-103/k: I'd like to place an order for twenty boxes of printer paper.
lc/#lc-103/keyKo: to request goods from a supplier; to buy
lc/#lc-103/tip: place를 '두다'로 해석하면 안 된다. order는 '주문'과 '순서' 둘 다 된다.
Don't read place as "put." Order can mean both "a request to buy" and "sequence."
lc/#lc-104/k: 전자 제품 반품 규정이 어떻게 되나요?
What's your return policy on electronics?
lc/#lc-104/keyKo: the store's rules for taking back items
lc/#lc-104/tip: Return can mean both "bring back an item" and "come back," so use context to tell them apart.
lc/#lc-105/k: You'll need your receipt to return this item.
lc/#lc-105/tip: p가 묵음이라 [리씨트]로 들린다. 'proof of purchase'로 패러프레이즈된다.
The p is silent: /rɪˈsiːt/. It is paraphrased as 'proof of purchase'.
lc/#lc-106/k: 현금 환불은 안 되지만 매장 적립금으로 드릴 수 있어요.
We can't give you cash back, but we can offer you store credit.
lc/#lc-106/keyKo: 매장 적립금 (그 매장에서만 쓸 수 있는 금액)
money you can spend only at that store
lc/#lc-106/tip: 환불 대신 제시하는 해결책을 묻는 문제에서 자주 정답이 된다.
It is often the answer to questions about the solution offered instead of a refund.
lc/#lc-107/k: 완전히 만족하지 않으시면 전액 환불해 드립니다.
If you're not completely satisfied, you'll receive a full refund.
lc/#lc-107/tip: It is paraphrased as 'get your money back'.
lc/#lc-108/k: 이 셔츠를 더 큰 사이즈로 교환할 수 있을까요?
Can I exchange this shirt for a larger size?
lc/#lc-108/tip: 교환(exchange)과 환불(refund)을 구분하는 문제가 자주 나온다.
Questions often test the difference between an exchange (swap for another item) and a refund (money back).
lc/#lc-109/k: 원하시는 프린터는 입고 대기 중인데, 2주 안에 들어올 거예요.
The printer you want is on back order, but it should arrive in two weeks.
lc/#lc-109/keyKo: ordered but waiting for new stock
lc/#lc-109/tip: 주문은 받지만 지금은 재고가 없다는 뜻. out of stock과 함께 나온다.
It means the store takes your order but has none right now. It appears together with out of stock.
lc/#lc-110/k: Orders over fifty dollars qualify for free shipping.
lc/#lc-110/tip: 광고 담화에서 혜택을 묻는 문제의 정답. 조건(금액·기간)까지 들어야 한다.
It is the answer to questions about the benefit in an ad. Listen for the conditions too (amount, time period).
lc/#lc-111/k: 이 운동화는 이번 주에 할인 중이에요. 30퍼센트 할인이에요.
These running shoes are on sale this week. They're thirty percent off.
lc/#lc-111/tip: on sale은 '할인 중', for sale은 '판매 중'. 둘을 구분하는 함정이 있다.
On sale means "discounted," and for sale means "available to buy." A trap tests the difference.
lc/#lc-112/k: 이 청소기는 2년 품질 보증이 포함되어 있습니다.
This vacuum cleaner comes with a two-year warranty.
lc/#lc-112/tip: warranty는 guarantee로 패러프레이즈된다. under warranty는 '보증 기간 내'다.
Warranty is paraphrased as guarantee. Under warranty means "still covered by the guarantee."
lc/#lc-113/k: 이 주문 확인 번호로 온라인에서 배송 조회를 하실 수 있어요.
You can track your order online with this confirmation number.
lc/#lc-113/keyKo: to check where a delivery is
lc/#lc-114/k: 도움 받고 계신가요, 고객님? 새로 나온 모델을 보여 드릴게요.
Are you being helped, sir? I'd be glad to show you our new models.
lc/#lc-114/keyKo: 다른 직원이 응대하고 있나요? (점원의 응대 인사)
Is someone already assisting you? (a clerk's greeting)
lc/#lc-114/tip: Part 3 첫 대사에서 장소(매장)와 화자 관계(점원과 고객)를 알려 준다.
As the first line in Part 3, it tells you the place (a store) and the speakers' relationship (clerk and customer).
lc/#lc-115/k: Q: 찾으시는 거 있으세요? / A: 아뇨, 괜찮아요. 그냥 둘러보는 중이에요.
Q: Can I help you find something? / A: No, thanks. I'm just looking.
lc/#lc-115/tip: The line 'I'm just browsing.' means the same.
lc/#lc-115/xk/0: I found my keys on the bus.
lc/#lc-116/k: Breakfast is complimentary for all hotel guests.
lc/#lc-116/tip: free of charge, at no cost로 패러프레이즈된다. complementary(보완적인)와 철자가 다르다.
It is paraphrased as free of charge or at no cost. Don't confuse its spelling with complementary (completing something else).
lc/#lc-117/k: Will you be paying by credit card or in cash?
lc/#lc-117/keyKo: to use a card to settle the bill
lc/#lc-117/tip: by card, in cash처럼 전치사가 다르다. 선택 의문문은 둘 중 하나나 제3의 답이 정답이다.
The prepositions differ: by card, in cash. For choice questions, the answer is one of the two or a third option.
lc/#lc-118/k: 결제할 때 프로모션 코드를 입력하시면 10퍼센트 할인됩니다.
Enter the promo code at checkout to get ten percent off.
lc/#lc-118/tip: discount code, coupon code와 같은 말이다.
It is the same as discount code or coupon code.
lc/#lc-119/k: 지난주에 산 믹서기가 알고 보니 불량이었어요.
The blender I bought last week turned out to be defective.
lc/#lc-119/tip: Part 3 문제점 문제에서 'not working properly', faulty로 바뀌어 나온다.
In Part 3 questions about a problem, it appears as 'not working properly' or faulty.
lc/#lc-120/k: 오늘 저녁 7시에 네 명 예약하고 싶습니다.
I'd like to make a reservation for four at seven tonight.
lc/#lc-120/tip: book a table로도 쓴다. 인원·시간 숫자가 문제로 나온다.
Book a table is also used. The numbers (people, time) are often asked about.
lc/#lc-121/k: Q: 새 노트북 주문하기 전에 예산을 확인해야 하지 않을까요? / A: 좋은 지적이에요.
Q: Shouldn't we check the budget before ordering new laptops? / A: That's a good point.
lc/#lc-121/keyKo: 좋은 지적이다 → 상대 의견을 인정하고 받아들인다
you're right → accepts the other person's view
lc/#lc-121/tip: 의도 파악 문제의 정답은 'To agree with a suggestion' 유형이다.
For a speaker's intent question, the answer is like 'To agree with a suggestion'.
lc/#lc-121/xk/0: 노트북 가방은 제 책상 위에 있어요.
The laptop case is on my desk.
lc/#lc-122/k: Q: 금요일까지 보고서를 끝낼 방법이 없을까요? / A: 어떻게든 해 볼게요.
Q: Is there any way you could finish the report by Friday? / A: I'll see what I can do.
lc/#lc-122/keyKo: 할 수 있는 데까지 해 보겠다 → 확답은 못 하지만 요청을 들어주려 노력하겠다
I'll try my best → no promise, but I'll try to help
lc/#lc-122/tip: 수락도 거절도 아닌 '노력하겠다'는 의도. promise처럼 확정하는 보기는 오답이다.
The intent is neither yes nor no, but "I'll try." Options that make a firm promise are wrong.
lc/#lc-122/xk/1: It's on the way to the station.
lc/#lc-123/k: Q: 이번 주 정말 길었네요. / A: 누가 아니래요.
Q: This has been a really long week. / A: You can say that again.
lc/#lc-123/tip: '다시 말해 달라'는 요청이 아니다. repeat이 들어간 보기는 함정이다.
It isn't a request to repeat something. Options containing repeat are a trap.
lc/#lc-123/xk/1: Next week is fine with me.
lc/#lc-124/k: 휴가를 드리고 싶지만 제가 결정할 일이 아니에요. 첸 씨께 여쭤보셔야 해요.
I'd love to give you the day off, but it's not my call. You'll need to ask Mr. Chen.
lc/#lc-124/keyKo: 내가 결정할 일이 아니다 → 결정권이 다른 사람에게 있다
I'm not the one who decides → someone else has the power
lc/#lc-124/tip: call을 '전화'로 들으면 함정에 빠진다. 여기서 call은 '결정'이다.
If you hear call as "phone call," you'll fall into the trap. Here call means "decision."
lc/#lc-125/k: Q: 우리 웹사이트 정말 업데이트해야 해요. / A: 전적으로 동의해요.
Q: We should really update our website. / A: I couldn't agree more.
lc/#lc-125/keyKo: 더할 나위 없이 동의한다 → 강한 동의
I fully share your view → strong agreement
lc/#lc-125/tip: couldn't라는 부정형 때문에 반대 의견으로 오해하기 쉽다.
Because of the negative couldn't, it's easy to mistake it for disagreement.
lc/#lc-125/xk/0: The construction site is on Elm Street.
lc/#lc-125/xk/1: Yes, I really liked the movie.
lc/#lc-126/k: Cutting costs by thirty percent? That's easier said than done.
lc/#lc-126/keyKo: 말은 쉽지만 실행은 어렵다 → 제안의 실현 가능성을 의심한다
it sounds easy but is hard to do → doubts the plan will work
lc/#lc-126/tip: 의도 파악 문제의 정답은 'To express doubt', 'To point out a difficulty' 유형이다.
For a speaker's intent question, the answer is like 'To express doubt' or 'To point out a difficulty'.
lc/#lc-127/k: 오해하지 마세요, 디자인은 마음에 들어요. 비용이 좀 걱정될 뿐이에요.
Don't get me wrong, I like the design. I'm just worried about the cost.
lc/#lc-127/keyKo: 오해하지 마라 → 우려나 비판을 말하기 전에 완곡하게 덧붙인다
please don't misunderstand → softens a concern or criticism that follows
lc/#lc-127/tip: 이 표현 뒤 but이나 just 다음에 나오는 말이 화자의 진짜 의견이다.
After this phrase, what comes after but or just is the speaker's real opinion.
lc/#lc-128/k: 새 공급업체가 더 싸니까 한번 써 볼 만해요.
The new supplier is cheaper, so it's worth a try.
lc/#lc-128/keyKo: 시도해 볼 만하다 → 제안을 받아들이거나 권한다
it could be good to give it a go → accepts or recommends a suggestion
lc/#lc-129/k: 좋은 생각이긴 한데 이번 분기는 예산이 빠듯해요.
That sounds great, but we're on a tight budget this quarter.
lc/#lc-129/keyKo: 예산이 빠듯한 → 비용이 드는 제안은 어렵다 (완곡한 거절)
short of money → can't do anything costly (soft refusal)
lc/#lc-129/tip: 제안을 거절하는 이유로 자주 나오며 'can't afford it'으로 패러프레이즈된다.
It often appears as the reason for turning down a suggestion and is paraphrased as 'can't afford it'.
lc/#lc-130/k: Q: 다음 달에 사무실 이전하는 거 알았어요? / A: 정말요? 처음 듣는 얘기예요.
Q: Did you know the office is moving next month? / A: Really? That's news to me.
lc/#lc-130/keyKo: I hadn't heard that → I didn't know; I'm surprised
lc/#lc-130/tip: news를 듣고 신문·뉴스 관련 보기를 고르면 오답이다.
Choosing an option about newspapers or the news because you heard news is wrong.
lc/#lc-130/xk/0: Next month is fine with me.
lc/#lc-131/k: Q: 화물이 월요일까지 도착할까요? / A: 기대하지 않는 게 좋을 거예요.
Q: Do you think the shipment will arrive by Monday? / A: I wouldn't count on it.
lc/#lc-131/keyKo: don't expect it → it probably won't happen
lc/#lc-131/tip: count를 '세다'로 해석한 숫자 관련 보기는 함정이다.
Options with numbers that read count as "add up" are a trap.
lc/#lc-132/k: Q: 시내 교통이 날마다 심해지네요. / A: 그러게 말이에요. 여기 오는 데 한 시간 걸렸어요.
Q: The traffic downtown is getting worse every day. / A: Tell me about it. It took me an hour to get here.
lc/#lc-132/keyKo: 그러게 말이다 → 공감·동의 (설명해 달라는 뜻이 아니다)
I know exactly what you mean → sympathy, agreement (not a request to explain)
lc/#lc-132/tip: 글자 그대로 '말해 달라'는 요청으로 해석하면 오답이다.
Reading it literally as a request to be told something is wrong.
lc/#lc-132/xk/0: The downtown branch opened last year.
lc/#lc-133/k: Q: 유연 근무제를 도입하는 거 어떻게 생각해요? / A: 대찬성이에요.
Q: What do you think about offering flexible hours? / A: I'm all for it.
lc/#lc-133/tip: It is paraphrased as 'support the idea'.
lc/#lc-134/k: 도와드리고 싶지만 이제 제 손을 떠났어요. 최종 결정은 법무팀이 해요.
I'd like to help, but it's out of my hands now. Legal has the final say.
lc/#lc-134/keyKo: 내 손을 떠났다 → 내가 더는 어떻게 할 수 없다
I no longer control it → there's nothing more I can do
lc/#lc-134/tip: 'It's not my call.'처럼 권한이 없음을 나타낸다.
Like 'It's not my call.', it shows the speaker doesn't have the authority.
lc/#lc-135/k: Q: 엘런 웨이드라는 고객 기억나세요? / A: 음, 이름은 들어 본 것 같아요.
Q: Do you remember a client named Ellen Wade? / A: Hmm, the name rings a bell.
lc/#lc-135/keyKo: 들어 본 것 같다 → 어렴풋이 기억난다
to sound familiar → I vaguely remember
lc/#lc-135/tip: bell을 듣고 초인종·종소리 보기를 고르면 함정에 걸린다.
Choosing an option about a doorbell or bells ringing because you heard bell is a trap.
lc/#lc-135/xk/0: Please remember to lock the door.
lc/#lc-136/k: Q: 학회 끝나고 갈 식당을 예약할까요? / A: 상황 봐서 정하죠.
Q: Should we book a restaurant for after the conference? / A: Let's play it by ear.
lc/#lc-136/keyKo: 상황을 봐 가며 정하다 → 지금 확정하지 않겠다
to decide as things happen → not deciding now
lc/#lc-136/xk/0: I read that book last year.
lc/#lc-136/xk/1: The conference room is on the left.
lc/#lc-137/k: It's a generous offer, but let me sleep on it.
lc/#lc-137/keyKo: 하룻밤 생각해 보겠다 → 지금 바로 결정하지 않겠다
I'll think about it overnight → I won't decide right now
lc/#lc-137/tip: 결정을 미루는 의도. sleep을 듣고 피곤함·수면 관련 보기를 고르면 오답이다.
The intent is to put off a decision. Choosing an option about being tired or sleeping because you heard sleep is wrong.
lc/#lc-138/k: Q: 고객 발표를 인턴들한테 맡기죠. / A: 음, 그게 좋은 생각인지 모르겠네요.
Q: Let's ask the interns to handle the client presentation. / A: Hmm, I'm not sure that's a good idea.
lc/#lc-138/keyKo: I have doubts about this → soft disagreement
lc/#lc-138/tip: 직접 No라고 하지 않는 반대 표현. 의도 파악 문제의 정답은 'To express disagreement'다.
It disagrees without saying no directly. For a speaker's intent question, the answer is 'To express disagreement'.
lc/#lc-139/k: Q: 점심에 새로 생긴 태국 음식점 가 볼래요? / A: 좋죠.
Q: Do you want to try the new Thai place for lunch? / A: Why not?
lc/#lc-139/keyKo: 안 될 거 없지 → 흔쾌히 수락
sure, let's do it → happy agreement
lc/#lc-139/tip: Why로 시작하지만 이유를 묻는 게 아니라 동의하는 표현이다.
It starts with Why, but it isn't asking for a reason; it shows agreement.
lc/#lc-139/xk/0: I tried on a jacket yesterday.
lc/#lc-140/k: Q: 몇 명이서 금요일에 무역 박람회에 가요. / A: 저도 갈게요.
Q: A few of us are going to the trade show on Friday. / A: Count me in.
lc/#lc-140/tip: The opposite, 'Count me out.', means you won't take part.
lc/#lc-140/xk/0: 작년에 제 헌 차를 보상 판매했어요.
I traded in my old car last year.
lc/#lc-141/k: 승객 여러분께 알려 드립니다. 덴버행 207편은 14번 게이트에서 출발하게 되었습니다.
Attention, passengers: Flight 207 to Denver will now depart from Gate 14.
lc/#lc-141/tip: 첫마디에서 장소(공항·역)와 청자를 묻는 문제의 정답이 나온다.
The opening words give the answer to questions about the place (airport, station) and the listeners.
lc/#lc-142/k: 선로 보수 작업으로 8시 15분 열차가 지연되고 있습니다. 불편을 드려 죄송합니다.
The 8:15 train has been delayed due to track maintenance. We apologize for the inconvenience.
lc/#lc-142/tip: 사과 문구 바로 앞에 나오는 지연·변경 사유가 문제로 나온다.
The reason for the delay or change, which comes right before the apology, is often asked about.
lc/#lc-143/k: 곧 탑승을 시작하오니 탑승권을 준비해 주십시오.
We'll begin boarding shortly, so please have your boarding pass ready.
lc/#lc-143/keyKo: to have your flight ticket in hand
lc/#lc-143/tip: 청자 요청 사항 문제에서 'Prepare a document'로 패러프레이즈된다.
In questions about what listeners are asked to do, it is paraphrased as 'Prepare a document'.
lc/#lc-144/k: 광고 후 바로 날씨 예보가 이어집니다. 채널 고정해 주세요.
Stay tuned for the weather report right after the break.
lc/#lc-144/keyKo: keep listening; don't change the station
lc/#lc-144/tip: 라디오 방송 끝부분에 나오며 '다음에 무엇을 듣게 되는가' 문제의 단서다.
It comes near the end of a radio broadcast, and it is the clue for questions about what listeners will hear next.
lc/#lc-145/k: 이번 토요일 단 하루, 개업 기념 세일을 놓치지 마세요!
Don't miss our grand opening sale, this Saturday only!
lc/#lc-145/tip: 광고 담화의 신호. 뒤따르는 기간·할인율 숫자에 집중한다.
It signals an ad. Focus on the numbers that follow, such as dates and discount rates.
lc/#lc-146/k: 페어뷰 치과입니다. 지금은 진료 시간이 아닙니다.
You've reached Fairview Dental Clinic. Our office is currently closed.
lc/#lc-146/tip: 녹음 메시지 첫 문장. 업종·장소를 묻는 문제의 정답 근거다.
It is the first line of a recorded message, and it is the evidence for questions about the type of business or place.
lc/#lc-147/k: Our regular business hours are Monday through Friday, nine to five.
lc/#lc-147/tip: office hours, opening hours와 같은 말. 주말·공휴일 변동이 문제로 나온다.
It is the same as office hours or opening hours. Changes on weekends or holidays are often asked about.
lc/#lc-148/k: For questions about your bill, please press two.
lc/#lc-148/tip: 번호별 안내가 이어지므로 문제에 나온 용건에 해당하는 번호를 골라 듣는다.
The menu lists a number for each service, so listen for the number that matches the need in the question.
lc/#lc-149/keyKo: glad to have you on this flight; (to a new hire) glad you've joined us
lc/#lc-149/tip: 신입 사원 환영 인사로도 쓰여 '새 직원 소개' 담화의 단서가 된다.
It is also used to welcome a new employee, so it is a clue for talks introducing a new staff member.
lc/#lc-150/k: 안전벨트 표시등이 꺼질 때까지 자리에 앉아 계십시오.
Please remain seated until the seatbelt sign has been turned off.
lc/#lc-151/k: 델몬트 인더스트리 전 직원을 대표해 와 주셔서 감사드립니다.
On behalf of everyone at Delmont Industries, thank you for coming.
lc/#lc-151/tip: 화자의 소속을 묻는 문제의 단서가 된다.
It is the clue for questions about which organization the speaker belongs to.
lc/#lc-152/k: 기조연설자 아니타 샤 박사님을 함께 환영해 주십시오.
Please join me in welcoming our keynote speaker, Dr. Anita Shah.
lc/#lc-152/keyKo: let's all give a warm welcome to ~
lc/#lc-152/tip: 인물 소개 담화의 신호. 뒤에 나오는 경력·업적이 문제로 나온다.
It signals a talk introducing someone. The person's career and achievements that follow are often asked about.
lc/#lc-153/k: 사진은 자유롭게 찍으셔도 되지만 작품은 만지지 마십시오.
Feel free to take photos, but please don't touch the artwork.
lc/#lc-153/tip: 투어 안내에서 허용 사항과 금지 사항을 구분하는 문제가 나온다.
In tour talks, questions test what is allowed and what isn't.
lc/#lc-154/k: 나가시는 길에 기념품 가게에 꼭 들러 보세요.
Be sure to stop by the gift shop on your way out.
lc/#lc-154/tip: 청자에게 권하는 일(요청 사항) 문제의 정답 근거다.
It is the evidence for questions about what listeners are advised to do.
lc/#lc-155/k: 비상시에는 엘리베이터가 아닌 계단을 이용해 주십시오.
In the event of an emergency, please use the stairs, not the elevators.
lc/#lc-156/k: 현재 통화량이 많습니다. 끊지 말고 기다려 주십시오.
We're currently experiencing a high volume of calls. Please stay on the line.
lc/#lc-156/keyKo: to have many calls coming in
lc/#lc-156/tip: 대기 안내 녹음. 이어지는 대안(웹사이트 이용, 회신 요청)을 묻는 문제가 나온다.
This is a hold message. Questions often ask about the alternatives that follow (using the website, requesting a callback).
lc/#lc-157/k: 문제를 해결하는 동안 기다려 주셔서 감사합니다.
Thank you for your patience while we resolve the issue.
lc/#lc-157/tip: 지연 상황을 암시하므로 문제점을 묻는 문제와 함께 출제된다.
It hints at a delay, so it often appears with questions about a problem.
lc/#lc-158/k: 이것으로 공장 견학을 마치겠습니다. 즐거우셨기를 바랍니다.
This concludes our tour of the factory. I hope you enjoyed it.
lc/#lc-158/tip: 담화 끝부분의 신호. 이후 일정을 묻는 문제가 이어진다.
It signals the end of a talk, and a question about what happens next usually follows.
lc/#lc-159/k: 12번 출구 근처에서 난 사고로 9번 고속도로가 정체되고 있습니다.
Traffic is backed up on Highway 9 due to an accident near Exit 12.
lc/#lc-159/tip: It is paraphrased as heavy traffic, congestion, or delays.
lc/#lc-160/k: Admission is free for children under twelve.
lc/#lc-160/keyKo: you can get in at no cost
lc/#lc-160/tip: admission은 '입장(료)'. no charge, free of charge로 패러프레이즈된다.
Admission means "entry (fee)." It is paraphrased as no charge or free of charge.
lc/#lc-161/k: Q: 오카포 씨가 은퇴하면 누가 그 자리를 맡을까요? / A: 저도 모르기는 마찬가지예요.
Q: Who's going to replace Mr. Okafor after he retires? / A: Your guess is as good as mine.
lc/#lc-161/keyKo: 당신 추측이나 내 추측이나 같다 (→ 나도 모른다)
I know as little as you do (→ I don't know)
lc/#lc-161/tip: '모른다'를 돌려 말하는 관용 표현. guess만 듣고 추측한 내용이 나올 거라 기대하면 안 된다.
This idiom is an indirect way to say "I don't know." Hearing guess doesn't mean an actual guess will follow.
lc/#lc-162/k: Q: 새 지점이 올해 수익을 낼까요? / A: 아직 판단하기엔 일러요.
Q: Will the new branch be profitable this year? / A: It's too early to tell.
lc/#lc-162/keyKo: we can't know yet (→ not sure yet)
lc/#lc-162/tip: Yes/No 의문문에 Yes/No 없이 '아직 알 수 없다'고 답하는 정답 유형이다.
This is a correct-answer type that replies to a yes/no question without yes or no, saying "we can't know yet."
lc/#lc-162/xk/1: Yes, it was a profitable trip.
lc/#lc-163/k: Q: 이번 주 직원 회의는 어디서 열려요? / A: 게시판에 공지돼 있을 거예요.
Q: Where's the staff meeting being held this week? / A: It should be posted on the bulletin board.
lc/#lc-163/keyKo: to be shown on ~ (→ check there)
lc/#lc-163/tip: 장소를 직접 말하지 않고 정보가 있는 곳(bulletin board, intranet)을 알려 주는 응답이다.
This response doesn't name the place directly but tells you where to find the information (bulletin board, intranet).
lc/#lc-163/xk/1: Yes, I held it for you.
lc/#lc-164/k: Q: 이 구매 주문서는 누가 승인했어요? / A: 회계팀 사람한테 물어보셔야 할 거예요.
Q: Who approved this purchase order? / A: You'd have to ask someone in Accounting.
lc/#lc-164/keyKo: you should check with ~ (→ I don't know)
lc/#lc-164/tip: 제3자에게 물어보라는 응답. 사람 이름 대신 부서(Accounting)가 나와도 정답이다.
This response tells you to ask a third person. It is correct even if it names a department (Accounting) instead of a person.
lc/#lc-164/xk/0: By the end of the week.
lc/#lc-165/k: Q: 작년 연회 때 어느 출장 요리 업체를 썼죠? / A: 저는 작년에 여기 없었어요.
Q: Which caterer did we use for last year's banquet? / A: I wasn't here last year.
lc/#lc-165/keyKo: I didn't work here then (→ I don't know)
lc/#lc-165/tip: 과거 일을 묻는 질문에 '그때 없었다'며 모른다고 답하는 유형이다.
This type answers a question about the past with "I wasn't here then," meaning "I don't know."
lc/#lc-165/xk/1: Yes, it was a great banquet.
lc/#lc-166/k: Q: 이사회 회의에 쓸 매출 수치 준비됐어요? / A: 분기 수치 말씀이세요?
Q: Are the sales figures ready for the board meeting? / A: Do you mean the quarterly ones?
lc/#lc-166/keyKo: Are you talking about ~? (→ checking by asking back)
lc/#lc-166/tip: 질문에 질문으로 되묻는 응답도 정답이 된다. 무엇을 가리키는지 확인하는 패턴이다.
Answering a question with a question can also be correct. This pattern checks what the speaker is referring to.
lc/#lc-167/k: Q: 엘리베이터는 언제 고쳐지나요? / A: 저도 그걸 알아보는 중이에요.
Q: When will the elevator be fixed? / A: That's what I'm trying to find out.
lc/#lc-167/keyKo: 그걸 지금 알아보는 중이다 (→ 아직 모른다)
I'm checking on that now (→ I don't know yet)
lc/#lc-167/tip: When 질문에 시점 없이 '알아보는 중'이라고 답해도 정답이다.
For a When question, answering "I'm finding out" without a time is also correct.
lc/#lc-168/k: Q: 프리미엄 요금제로 업그레이드할까요? / A: 그건 이사님이 정하실 일이에요.
Q: Should we upgrade to the premium plan? / A: It's up to the director.
lc/#lc-168/keyKo: ~에게 달려 있다 (→ 내가 정할 일이 아니다)
lc/#lc-168/tip: 결정권자를 알려 주는 응답. up을 위쪽(층)으로 오해한 보기는 함정이다.
This response names who makes the decision. Options that read up as "upstairs" are a trap.
lc/#lc-169/k: Q: 오늘 오후에 회의실 쓰세요? / A: 왜요, 필요하세요?
Q: Are you using the conference room this afternoon? / A: Why, do you need it?
lc/#lc-169/keyKo: Why? Do you want ~? (→ asking back to check the intent)
lc/#lc-169/tip: 여기서 Why는 이유를 묻는 의문사가 아니라 '왜요?' 하고 되묻는 말이다.
Here Why isn't asking for a reason; it is a "Why do you ask?" reply.
lc/#lc-170/k: Q: 사무실 이전 계획은 어떻게 돼요? / A: 경영진이 아직 세부 사항을 정하고 있어요.
Q: What's the plan for the office relocation? / A: Management is still working out the details.
lc/#lc-170/keyKo: 세부 사항을 정하다 (→ 아직 확정되지 않았다)
to settle the specifics (→ not final yet)
lc/#lc-170/tip: 계획을 묻는 질문에 '아직 정하는 중'이라고 답하는 미정 응답이다.
This "not decided yet" response answers a question about plans with "still deciding."
lc/#lc-171/k: Q: 발표 때 노트북 좀 빌려도 될까요? / A: 5시까지만 돌려주시면요.
Q: Can I borrow your laptop for the presentation? / A: As long as you return it by five.
lc/#lc-171/keyKo: only if ~; on condition that ~ (conditional yes)
lc/#lc-171/tip: 조건을 붙여 허락하는 응답. as long as를 '~하는 동안'으로만 알면 놓친다.
This response gives permission with a condition. If you only know as long as as "while," you'll miss it.
lc/#lc-171/xk/1: It's a long way to the station.
lc/#lc-172/k: Q: 퇴근하고 커피 한잔하실래요? / A: 다음에 해요.
Q: Would you like to grab a coffee after work? / A: Maybe some other time.
lc/#lc-172/tip: No 없이 다음으로 미루는 정중한 거절. 'Can I take a rain check?'도 같은 뜻이다.
This polite refusal puts it off without saying no. The line 'Can I take a rain check?' means the same.
lc/#lc-172/xk/0: She works at a cafe downtown.
lc/#lc-173/k: Q: 공항까지 차로 데려다 드릴까요? / A: 말씀은 고맙지만 이미 셔틀을 예약했어요.
Q: Would you like me to drive you to the airport? / A: Thanks for the offer, but I've already booked a shuttle.
lc/#lc-173/keyKo: that's kind of you, but ~ (polite refusal)
lc/#lc-173/tip: 도움 제안을 거절할 때 쓰는 표현. Thanks만 듣고 수락으로 판단하지 말 것.
It is used to turn down an offer of help. Don't decide it's a yes just from Thanks.
lc/#lc-173/xk/1: 그는 지난주에 차를 몰고 거기 갔어요.
lc/#lc-174/k: Q: 자기소개서 교정 봐 드릴까요? / A: 그래 주시면 감사하죠.
Q: Do you want me to proofread your cover letter? / A: I'd appreciate it.
lc/#lc-174/tip: 도움 제안을 받아들이는 정중한 표현. appreciate(감사하다)를 꼭 기억한다.
This is a polite way to accept an offer of help. Make sure you remember appreciate (to be thankful for).
lc/#lc-175/k: Q: 이 청구서들 좀 검토해 주실래요? / A: 점심 먹고 나서 해도 될까요?
